# Field

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/field

> A label, a hint and an error around one control, with the ids and aria attributes wired for you.

`Field` puts a label above a control, a hint under it and an error when there is one, and connects them. The control gets its `id`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid` and `aria-required` from the field, merged with any it already has, so a screen reader hears the error the moment it appears.

Field:

```tsx
<Field label="Email" hint="We only use it to send receipts." required>
    <Input id="email" placeholder="you@example.com" />
</Field>

<Field label="Workspace" error={errors.workspace} hint="Lowercase letters and dashes.">
    <Input id="workspace" />
</Field>
```

## What it wires

- The label's `htmlFor` points at the control's `id`. The control keeps its own `id`; a control without one gets a generated id.
- `aria-describedby` lists the control's own description first, then the error, then the hint.
- While `error` is set the control is `aria-invalid`. `Input` (with any `type`, `"password"` included), `Textarea` and the fields built on them, such as `Select` and `NumberInput`, also draw their error styling, with no separate `error` prop.
- `required` adds `aria-required` and an asterisk after the label. The asterisk is hidden from screen readers so it is not read out twice.

The hint stays visible while the error shows, so the instruction is still there when the user goes back to fix the value.

## Field or Input alone

`Input` and `Textarea` work on their own: a floating `label` inside the box, and `description` and `errorMessage` under it at the same 16px inset as the text. That suits a single field, like a search box or a settings row.

In a form, wrap each control in a `Field`. The label sits above the box, the hint and error start under the label, and every control in the form, `Select` or a custom picker included, looks the same. `FormErrorSummary` links to the ids a `Field` wires.

Inside a `Field`, give the label, hint and error to the `Field` and leave the control's own `label`, `description` and `errorMessage` unset. Set both and you get two labels, and messages at two different insets; in development the control warns in the console.

```tsx
// One label, messages under it
<Field label="Email" hint="We never share it" error={errors.email}>
  <Input id="email" />
</Field>
```

## Any control

Native elements and third-party controls get the same props. For a control that needs them somewhere other than its root, pass a function: it receives the props to spread.

```tsx
<Field label="Plan" error={errors.plan}>
  {(control) => <MyPlanPicker inputProps={control} />}
</Field>
```

A custom control can also read the field from context with `useField()`, which returns the `id`, `invalid`, `required` and `describedBy` of the enclosing field, or `null` outside one.

## In a Form

A `Field` takes `span` like any other field, and lays out in a `Form` grid. With `density="stacked"` the controls still fuse; the labels and messages sit outside the group's border.

Form:

```tsx
<Form columns={2}>
    <Field label="First name"><Input id="first" /></Field>
    <Field label="Last name"><Input id="last" /></Field>
    <Field label="Bio" hint="Shown on your profile." span={2}>
        <Textarea id="bio" lines={3} />
    </Field>
</Form>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Visible label above the control, linked to it with htmlFor. |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the control, read out as part of its description. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  | The error message. While it is set the control is marked invalid. |
| `required` | `boolean` | `false` | Adds aria-required and an asterisk after the label. |
| `controlId` | `string` |  | The control's id. Defaults to the control's own id, then to a generated one. |
| `span` | `number` |  | Columns to occupy inside a Form grid. |
| `children (required)` | `ReactNode \| ((control: FieldControlProps) => ReactNode)` |  | One control element, or a function that receives the control's props. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `...HTMLAttributes` |  |  | Also takes these props |

---

# Fieldset

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/fieldset

> A titled section of a form: a real fieldset with a legend, laying its fields out like a Form.

`Fieldset` groups related fields under a name. It renders a real `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`, so a screen reader announces the section on entering it, and `disabled` turns off every native control inside at once. The fields are laid out by a `Form` grid, so a section takes the same `density`, `columns` and `span`.

Fieldset:

```tsx
<Fieldset legend="Billing address" description="Where we send invoices." density="stacked" columns={2}>
    <Input id="street" placeholder="Street" span={2} />
    <Input id="city" placeholder="City" />
    <Input id="zip" placeholder="Postal code" />
</Fieldset>
```

## Sections in a form

Put several sections in one `Form`. Each one fuses its own group of corners, and takes the form's `size` unless it sets its own.

```tsx
<Form as="form" density="spacious" onSubmit={save}>
  <Fieldset legend="Account" density="stacked">
    <Input id="email" placeholder="Email" />
    <Input id="password" placeholder="Password" type="password" />
  </Fieldset>
  <Fieldset legend="Profile" columns={{ xs: 1, m: 2 }}>
    <Field label="First name"><Input id="first" /></Field>
    <Field label="Last name"><Input id="last" /></Field>
  </Fieldset>
  <SubmitButton>Save</SubmitButton>
</Form>
```

## Disabled

`disabled` disables every native control in the section, the way a disabled `<fieldset>` always has. Use it for a section that does not apply yet, such as a shipping address while "same as billing" is checked.

Disabled:

```tsx
<Fieldset legend="Shipping address" description="Same as billing." disabled>
    <Input id="ship-street" placeholder="Street" />
</Fieldset>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `legend` | `ReactNode` |  | The section's name, rendered as its legend. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | A line under the legend, read out as the section's description. |
| `span` | `number` |  | Columns to occupy inside an outer Form grid. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `-` | Disable every native control in the section. |
| `name` | `string` | `-` | The fieldset's name, for form.elements. |
| `density` | `"stacked" \| "tight" \| "spacious"` | `"tight"` | Gap and grouping for the section's fields, as on Form. |
| `columns` | `FormColumns` | `1` | Grid columns, as on Form. |
| `size` | `TShirtSizes` | `-` | Size for every field in the section. Defaults to the outer form's. |

---

# Form

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/form

> Form lays fields out in a grid and carries their spacing density and grouping as one decision.

The `Form` component lays a set of fields out and decides how they read together. `density` carries the gap and the grouping as one choice, because they are one choice: `"stacked"` fuses the fields into a single control, while `"tight"` and `"spacious"` leave each one its own.

Form:

```tsx
<Form density="stacked">
    <Input id="email" placeholder="Email" />
    <Input id="password" placeholder="Password" type="password" />
    <Input id="workspace" placeholder="Workspace" />
</Form>
```

## Why not assign corners by hand

A stacked group is often built by passing `corners="top"`, `"none"` and `"bottom"` down a list. That is positional bookkeeping, and it breaks the moment the list changes: hide the third of four fields behind a condition and the group ends on a square edge, because the field that was told it was in the middle is now last.

`Form` works the other way round. It looks at which children actually rendered, works out where each one lands in the grid, and rounds only the corners that end up on the outside of the group. Nothing has to be told its position.

## Density

`"stacked"` collapses the gap to nothing and pulls adjacent borders onto a single shared hairline. `"tight"` and `"spacious"` are ordinary gaps, and every field keeps its own border and radius.

Density:

```tsx
<Form density="tight">...</Form>
<Form density="spacious">...</Form>
```

## Columns and spans

`columns` lays the fields out in a grid. A field can take more than one column with `span`, which `Form` reads off the child and strips before it reaches the DOM.

Columns:

```tsx
<Form density="stacked" columns={2}>
    <Input id="first" placeholder="First name" />
    <Input id="last" placeholder="Last name" />
    <Input id="email" placeholder="Email" span={2} />
    <Textarea id="note" placeholder="Note" span={2} />
</Form>
```

A last row that does not fill is handled too. Three fields in two columns make an L, and the second field keeps its bottom-right corner because that corner is on the outside of the group — even though it is not the last child.

## Responsive columns

`columns` also takes a per-breakpoint map. The column count changes with the viewport, and so does which field sits in a corner — so `Form` works the placement out for every breakpoint and lets CSS pick. Nothing is measured and nothing re-renders on resize.

Responsive:

```tsx
<Form density="stacked" columns={{ xs: 1, m: 2 }}>
    <Input id="first" placeholder="First name" />
    <Input id="last" placeholder="Last name" />
    <Input id="email" placeholder="Email" span={2} />
</Form>
```

## Size

`size` sets the size of every field in the group. A field that sets its own `size` keeps it. It travels by context rather than being cloned onto the children, so a child that is not a field picks up nothing.

Size:

```tsx
<Form density="stacked" size="s">
    <Input id="email" placeholder="Email" />
    <Input id="workspace" placeholder="Workspace" />
</Form>
```

## Toolbar size

`size="xxs"` makes every field 32px, the height of a `size="s"` Button, and rounds a stacked group at `radius-m` to match. Labels show as placeholders at this size.

Toolbar size:

```tsx
<Form density="stacked" size="xxs">
    <Input id="email" label="Email" />
    <Input id="workspace" label="Workspace" />
</Form>
```

## Focus

In a stacked group the fields overlap by a pixel, so a focused field has to paint above its neighbours — all four of them in two dimensions. `Form` lifts the focused cell for you. Turn the ring itself on with `focusRing` on the fields, which is worth doing for a form a keyboard user has to get through.

## What fuses, and what does not

`Form` rounds the corners of children that mark their own bordered box as a fusable surface. `Input`, `Textarea` and the fields built on them do. Anything else is laid out in the grid and spaced normally, but keeps its own corners — so a `Button` or a block of text can sit in a form without being absorbed into the group.

## Submitting

Pass `as="form"` to render a real `<form>` and take `onSubmit`. Return a promise from `onSubmit` and the form is pending until it settles: it is marked `aria-busy`, a [SubmitButton](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/submitButton) inside it shows a spinner, and a second submit is ignored. For a submit that does not run through `onSubmit`, pass `pending`.

```tsx
<Form
  as="form"
  density="stacked"
  onSubmit={async (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    await save(new FormData(event.currentTarget));
  }}
>
  <Input id="email" placeholder="Email" />
  <SubmitButton>Save</SubmitButton>
</Form>
```

## Building blocks

`Form` lays fields out. The pieces around them are separate components that work inside it:

- [Field](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/field) puts a label, hint and error around any control and wires its ids and aria attributes.
- [Fieldset](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/fieldset) names a section of the form and lays out its own group of fields.
- [SubmitButton](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/submitButton) follows the form's pending state.
- [FormErrorSummary](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/formErrorSummary) lists every error after a failed submit and links to each field.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `density` | `"stacked" \| "tight" \| "spacious"` | `tight` | Gap and grouping as one decision. "stacked" fuses the fields into a single control; "tight" and "spacious" leave each its own border and radius. |
| `columns` | `FormColumns` |  | Grid columns — a number, or a per-breakpoint map like { xs: 1, m: 2 }. |
| `size` | `FieldSize` |  | Size for every field in the group. A field that sets its own size keeps it. |
| `as` | `"div" \| "form"` | `div` | Render a real <form> rather than a <div>. |
| `onSubmit` | `(event: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => unknown` |  | Submit handler. Only attached when as is "form". Return a promise and the form is pending until it settles. |
| `pending` | `boolean` |  | Mark the form as submitting from outside. Wins over the state onSubmit tracks. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  | The fields. Conditional children that render nothing are ignored, and the corners follow. |
| `...HTMLAttributes` |  |  | Also takes these props |

---

# FormErrorSummary

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/formErrorSummary

> Every error in a form in one alert after a failed submit, each one linking to its field.

`FormErrorSummary` lists a form's errors at the top after a failed submit. Each entry links to its field, and activating it moves focus into the control. When the summary appears, or its errors change, it takes focus itself, so a keyboard or screen reader user is brought to it rather than left on the submit button wondering why nothing happened. With no errors it renders nothing, so it can stay in the form.

FormErrorSummary:

```tsx
<Form as="form" onSubmit={submit}>
    <FormErrorSummary errors={errors} />
    <Field label="Email" error={errors.email}>
        <Input id="email" />
    </Field>
    <Field label="Plan" error={errors.plan}>
        <Input id="plan" />
    </Field>
    <SubmitButton>Continue</SubmitButton>
</Form>
```

## Errors

`errors` takes either a map from control id to message, which is the shape most validation libraries return, or a list of `{ id, message }`. Empty messages are skipped. An entry without an `id`, such as a server error that belongs to no field, is listed as plain text.

```tsx
<FormErrorSummary errors={[{ message: "The server could not be reached. Try again." }]} />
```

The ids are the controls' ids, the same ones a `Field` uses, so the link lands on the right element.

## Focus

`autoFocus` is on by default. Turn it off when the summary is on screen from the first render, like the preview above, because taking focus on page load moves a screen reader away from the top of the page.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `errors (required)` | `FormErrorItem[] \| Record<string, ReactNode>` |  | A map from control id to message, or a list of { id, message }. |
| `title` | `string` |  | Heading above the list. Defaults to "Check the highlighted fields". |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Move focus to the summary when it appears or its errors change. |
| `span` | `number` |  | Columns to occupy inside a Form grid. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

---

# Input

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/input

> Input provides a flexible text entry field with support for labels, validation, and custom styling.

The `Input` component provides a text entry field with floating labels, validation support, and customizable styling. Use it for collecting user input in forms.

Input:

```tsx
<Input
    id="input-1"
    label="Email"
    prefix={
      <Icon marginLeft="4" onBackground="neutral-weak" name="email" size="xs" />
    }
/>
```

## Error

The Input component supports error state and message separately. Access them with the `error` and `errorMessage` props.

Error:

```tsx
<Input
    id="input-1"
    label="Email"
    error
    errorMessage={
      <Row vertical="center" gap="8">
        <Icon name="danger" size="xs" />
        Please enter a valid email address
      </Row>
    }
/>
```

## Validation

The Input component supports custom validation through the `validate` prop. This prop accepts a function that receives the input value and returns either an error message or null. The validation is happens automatically on value change with an automatic debounce of 1 second.

Validation:

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("");

const validateEmail = (email: any) => {
    if (!email) return null;
    
    const emailRegex = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;
    if (!emailRegex.test(email)) {
      return "Please enter a valid email address";
    }
    
    return null;
};

<Input
    id="input-1"
    value={value}
    onChange={(e) => setValue(e.target.value)}
    validate={validateEmail}
    placeholder="Email"
/>
```

## Prefix & Suffix

Add icons or other elements before or after the input text.

Prefix & Suffix:

```tsx
const [searchValue, setSearchValue] = useState<string>("");

const handleChange = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    setSearchValue(e.target.value);
};

const handleClear = () => {
    setSearchValue("");
};

<Input
    id="input-1"
    label="Search"
    value={searchValue}
    onChange={handleChange}
    prefix={<Icon name="search" size="xs" />}
    suffix={
      searchValue.length > 0 ? (
        <IconButton 
          variant="ghost" 
          icon="close" 
          size="s" 
          onClick={handleClear}
          aria-label="Clear search"
        />
      ) : null
    }
/>
```

## Password

With `type="password"`, Input adds a button in the suffix that switches the field between masked and visible, so a password can be checked without being retyped (2.x's `PasswordInput`). The button is named "Show password" or "Hide password" as it toggles, and a `suffix` of your own sits before it. Pass `reveal={false}` for a plain masked field.

Password:

```tsx
const [password, setPassword] = useState<string>("");

<Input
    id="password"
    label="Password"
    type="password"
    value={password}
    onChange={(e) => setPassword(e.target.value)}
/>
```

## Placeholder

Use the `placeholder` prop to use placeholder instead of label. The placeholder disappears when the input has value.

Placeholder:

```tsx
<Input
    id="input-1"
    placeholder="Name"
/>
```

## Description

Use the `description` prop to add a description below the input.

Description:

```tsx
<Input
    id="input-1"
    label="Email"
    description="Provide your email address in the format name@domain.com"
/>
```

## Character count

Display a character counter with color-coded feedback based on remaining characters. The counter changes color when approaching the limit.

Character count:

```tsx
const [bio, setBio] = useState<string>("");

const handleChange = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    setBio(e.target.value);
};

<Input
    id="bio-input"
    placeholder="Bio"
    value={bio}
    onChange={handleChange}
    maxLength={100}
    characterCount
/>
```

## Size

The Input component supports six sizes, from `xxs` (32px) through `xs` (40px), `s` (48px), `m` (56px, the default) and `l` (64px) to `xl` (72px).

Sizes:

```tsx
<Input id="size-xxs" label="Extra Extra Small" size="xxs" />
<Input id="size-xs" label="Extra Small" size="xs" />
<Input id="size-s" label="Small" size="s" />
<Input id="size-m" label="Medium" size="m" />
<Input id="size-l" label="Large" size="l" />
<Input id="size-xl" label="Extra Large" size="xl" />
```

Toolbar:

```tsx
const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
const [status, setStatus] = useState("all");

<Row fillWidth gap="8" vertical="center" s={{ direction: "column" }}>
    <Input
        id="toolbar-search"
        size="xxs"
        label="Search orders"
        value={query}
        onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}
        prefix={<Icon name="search" size="xs" onBackground="neutral-weak" />}
    />
    <Select
        id="toolbar-status"
        size="xxs"
        label="Status"
        value={status}
        onValueChange={(next) => setStatus(next as string)}
        options={[
            { label: "All statuses", value: "all" },
            { label: "Paid", value: "paid" },
            { label: "Pending", value: "pending" },
            { label: "Refunded", value: "refunded" },
        ]}
    />
    <Button size="s" variant="secondary" prefixIcon="download">
        Export
    </Button>
</Row>
```

## On touch devices

iOS Safari zooms the page when a focused control computes below 16px, and it
does not reliably zoom back out — the page is left scrolled somewhere else.
Once UI's mobile base is 15px, which put three of the five sizes under that
threshold, `size="m"` among them.

On touch pointers only, the value is therefore clamped:

| | clamp |
| --- | --- |
| font-size | `max(token, 16px)` |
| line-height | `max(token, 1.3 × font-size)` |
| min-height (`xs`, `s`) | `40px` and `48px` |

`xxs` has no height floor: it is small on purpose, and a floor would make it
the same field as `xs` on a phone. Its 16px value and 20.8px line still fit
its 22px box.

Line-height is clamped alongside the font because `xs` and `s` resolve
`--line-height-body-s` to 16.88px on mobile — 16px glyphs would otherwise sit
in a line box barely taller than themselves.

Nothing changes on a mouse pointer, and `l` and `xl` are untouched either way:
they already cleared 16px. The visible consequence is that `xs`, `s` and `m`
render the same text size on a phone and differ by height alone, which is how
iOS treats its own text fields.

The floating label and the value are positioned from where their ink falls —
cap height, baseline and descender — so the pair stays optically centred at
whatever size and height the clamps produce.

## Variants

The Input component supports two variants: `default` and `ghost`.

Variants:

```tsx
<Input id="variant-default" label="Default" variant="default" />
<Input id="variant-ghost" label="Ghost" variant="ghost" />
```

Loading:

```tsx
<Input
  id="username"
  label="Username"
  loading
  placeholder="Checking availability..."
/>
```

## Focus ring

Fields draw no focus ring by default — the quiet, borderless look modern native
inputs have settled on. Set `focusRing` to outline the field on focus, using the
same ring `Card` and `SmartLink` use, so a keyboard user can see where they are.
Worth turning on for any form someone has to tab through.

Note it shows on a mouse click too: `:focus-visible` always matches a field that
takes keyboard input, however that field was focused.

Focus ring:

```tsx
<Input id="email" label="Email" focusRing />
```

## Built on Input

Three components build on `Input`. They keep everything on this page and add one
thing each, so they live on pages of their own:

- [NumberInput](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/numberInput) — steppers, `min`/`max`/`step`, and a numeric `onValueChange`
- [OTPInput](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/otpInput) — one box per digit, with paste and an `onComplete`
- [TagInput](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/tagInput) — an array of removable tags instead of a string

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id (required)` | `string` |  | Ties the label to the field. Required, and must be unique on the page. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Floats above the value once the field is focused or filled. At size xxs it shows as the placeholder instead, and stays the accessible name. |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Shown while the field is empty. Not a substitute for a label. |
| `size` | `FieldSize` |  | Field height and type scale: xxs 32px, xs 40px, s 48px, m 56px (default), l 64px, xl 72px. xxs matches a size="s" Button, for toolbars. |
| `error` | `boolean` | `false` | Put the field in its error state. |
| `errorMessage` | `ReactNode` |  | Message shown under the field when error is set. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the field, for the rule the label cannot carry. |
| `corners` | `"none" \| "top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "top-left" \| "top-right" \| "bottom-right" \| "bottom-left"` |  | Round only some corners — for stacking fields into one block by hand. Inside a [Form](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/form) with density="stacked" this is worked out for you. |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` |  | Rendered before the value: an icon, a currency symbol, a select. |
| `suffix` | `ReactNode` |  | Rendered after the value: a unit, a clear button, a Kbd hint. |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "ghost"` | `default` | "ghost" drops the border and background, for a field inside a surface that already has them. |
| `focusRing` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `characterCount` | `boolean` |  | Show how much has been typed, against maxLength. |
| `cursor` | `undefined \| "interactive"` |  | Set "interactive" for a read-only field that opens something on click. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the field's text after every change, after the native onChange. Controlled only when value is set. |
| `validate` | `(value: ReactNode) => ReactNode \| null` |  | Run on a debounce, controlled or not; return a message to show, or null to clear. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a spinner in the suffix while something resolves. |
| `reveal` | `boolean` | `true` | With type="password", show the button that unmasks the value. Default true. |
| `span` | `number` |  | How many columns to occupy inside a [Form](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/form) grid. Ignored outside one. |
| `fillWidth` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `...InputHTMLAttributes` |  |  | Also takes these props |
| `className` | `string` | `-` |  |
| `style` | `CSSProperties` | `-` |  |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# InteractiveDetails

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/interactiveDetails

> Internal since 3.0: the label block of Checkbox, RadioButton and Switch.

`InteractiveDetails` is internal in Once UI 3.0. It is the label and description block `Checkbox`, `RadioButton` and `Switch` draw, and it is no longer exported from `@once-ui-system/core`.

Pass `label` and `description` to the control instead:

Checkbox:

```tsx
<Checkbox label="Email updates" description="One message a month, no more." />
```

See [Migrating from 2.x](https://github.com/once-ui-system/core/blob/main/MIGRATING.md) for the full list of exports that became internal.

# NumberInput

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/numberInput

> A numeric field with increment and decrement controls, bounded by min, max and step.

`NumberInput` is [Input](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/input) for numbers. It adds stepper
controls and clamps what can be typed, so the value reaching `onValueChange` is
already a number within range — no parsing, no `NaN`.

NumberInput:

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<number>(0);

const handleChange = (newValue: number) => {
    setValue(newValue);
};

<NumberInput
    id="quantity"
    label="Quantity"
    value={value}
    onValueChange={handleChange}
    min={0}
    max={100}
    step={1}
/>
```

## Following the value

The field follows its `value` prop after mount, so a number changed somewhere
else (an undo, a reset, a drag on a timeline) shows up in it. There is no need
to remount it with a `key`. It does not rewrite what the user is typing: a
partial entry such as `-` or `1.` stays as typed until it reads as a number.

## Toolbar size

`size="xxs"` draws a 32px field, the height of a `size="s"` Button. Two steppers stacked in it would get 15px each, so at this size they sit side by side, down then up.

Toolbar size:

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<number>(0);

<NumberInput
    id="quantity"
    label="Quantity"
    size="xxs"
    value={value}
    onValueChange={setValue}
    min={0}
    max={100}
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` |  | The current number, controlled. Leave it out and the field keeps its own. |
| `defaultValue` | `number` |  | The starting number when `value` is left out. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: number) => void` |  | Receives the number itself. Was onChange in 2.x. |
| `min` | `number` |  | Lower bound. The decrement control stops here. |
| `max` | `number` |  | Upper bound. The increment control stops here. |
| `step` | `number` | `1` | How much each press moves the value. |
| `padStart` | `number` |  | Pad to this many digits with leading zeros — 7 shown as 007. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler` | `-` | The native change event of the input, as on Input, so a form library's register() works. |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

Everything on [Input](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/input) — `label`, `description`, `error`,
`size`, `prefix`, `suffix` — works here too.

---

# OTPInput

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/otpInput

> One field per digit for verification codes, with paste, keyboard navigation and a completion callback.

`OTPInput` collects a one-time code as separate boxes rather than one field. It
moves focus as digits are typed, accepts a pasted code into all boxes at once,
and calls `onComplete` the moment the last one is filled.

Unlike the other inputs here it does not extend [Input](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/input) —
it is a group of fields, not one, so it has its own small surface.

OTPInput:

```tsx
const { addToast } = useToast();

const handleComplete = (code: string) => {
    addToast({ tone: "success", message: "Submitted " + code });
};

<OTPInput
    id="verification-code"
    length={6}
    onComplete={handleComplete}
    autoFocus
/>
```

## Screen readers and autofill

The boxes are one group, named "One-time code", and each box says which digit it is ("OTP digit 2 of 6"). The first box asks the browser for a code from a text message (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`), and a whole code arriving at once, by autofill or paste, fills every box. With `error`, every box is invalid and described by `errorMessage`. Name the group with `aria-label`, or translate both names with `labels`.

Translated:

```tsx
<OTPInput
    length={6}
    labels={{
      group: "Code de vérification",
      digit: (n, of) => `Chiffre ${n} sur ${of}`,
    }}
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `length` | `number` | `4` | How many digits, and so how many boxes. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The code typed so far, controlled. Leave it out and the boxes keep their own. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The starting code when `value` is left out. |
| `onValueChange` | `(code: string) => void` |  | Called with the code after every digit typed or erased. |
| `onComplete` | `(code: string) => void` |  | Called with the full code once the last box is filled. |
| `error` | `boolean` | `false` | Put the group in its error state. |
| `errorMessage` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Message shown under the boxes when error is set. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Block input across every box. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `false` | Focus the first box on mount. Leave it off if the code is not the first thing on the page. |
| `labels` | `OTPInputLabels` |  | The group's and the boxes' accessible names, to translate them. |
| `className` | `string` | `-` | Applied to the root, as are the other div props. They used to land on every box. |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# PasswordInput

`PasswordInput` folded into [`Input`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/input#password) in 3.0: use `<Input type="password">`, which keeps the show/hide toggle. The 3.0 codemod rewrites it (see the migration guide, "Components that merged").

# RadioButton

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/radioButton

> RadioButton provides a selectable control for mutually exclusive options with customizable labels and styling.

The `RadioButton` component provides a selectable control for mutually exclusive options in a group. Its `label` and `description` are drawn the same way as on `Checkbox` and `Switch`.

RadioButton:

```tsx
<RadioButton
    name="subscription"
    value="monthly"
    label="Monthly subscription"
    description="Billed monthly at $9.99"
    onCheckedChange={() => console.log('Selected monthly')}
/>
```

## State

Use the `checked` prop to control the radio button state externally.

State:

```tsx
const [selectedPlan, setSelectedPlan] = useState<string>("monthly");

const handleToggle = (value: string) => {
    setSelectedPlan(value);
};

<Column gap="16">
    <RadioButton
      name="subscription"
      value="monthly"
      label="Monthly subscription"
      description="Billed monthly at $9.99"
      checked={selectedPlan === "monthly"}
      onCheckedChange={() => handleToggle("monthly")}
    />
    <RadioButton
      name="subscription"
      value="annual"
      label="Annual subscription"
      description="Billed annually at $99.99"
      checked={selectedPlan === "annual"}
      onCheckedChange={() => handleToggle("annual")}
    />
    <RadioButton
      name="subscription"
      value="lifetime"
      label="Lifetime access"
      description="One-time payment of $299.99"
      checked={selectedPlan === "lifetime"}
      onCheckedChange={() => handleToggle("lifetime")}
    />
</Column>
```

## Disabled

Disable the radio button to prevent user interaction.

Disabled:

```tsx
<RadioButton
    label="Disabled radio button"
    disabled
/>
```

## Hover

Disable the hover pulse animation by setting `hoverable` to `false`.

Hover:

```tsx
<RadioButton
    label="No hover effect"
    hoverable={false}
/>
```

## Validation and size

`error` marks the RadioButton invalid (a danger border and `aria-invalid`);
`errorMessage` shows under it, linked with `aria-describedby`, and marks it
invalid too. `size` (`s`, `m`, `l`) scales the control and its text; left out,
it takes the enclosing `Form`'s `size`, as `Input` does.

Validation:

```tsx
<RadioButton
    label="Annual"
    value="annual"
    size="l"
    errorMessage="Pick a billing period"
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `TShirtSizes` |  | s, m or l. Left out, the enclosing Form's size, else m. |
| `error` | `boolean` |  | Mark it invalid: a danger border and aria-invalid. |
| `errorMessage` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown under it, linked with aria-describedby; marks it invalid too. |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `description` | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| `iconButtonProps` | `IconButtonProps` |  |  |
| `auto` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `checked` | `boolean` |  | Whether this one is chosen, controlled. Leave it out and the radio keeps its own state. |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | The starting state when `checked` is left out. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Group name. Radios sharing one are mutually exclusive. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Form field value. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Block interaction. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new state when it is picked: true when it becomes the chosen one. |
| `hoverable` | `boolean` | `true` | Highlight the row on hover. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `iconButtonProps` | `IconButtonProps` | `-` | Props forwarded to the icon button beside the label. |
| `...InputHTMLAttributes` |  |  | Also takes these props |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler` | `-` | The native change event of the hidden input, with the rest of the input attributes (name, required, onBlur), so a form library's register() works. |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# RadioGroup

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/radioGroup

> One choice from a set of radio buttons, as a single labelled form field with the keyboard behaviour screen readers expect.

`RadioGroup` turns a set of [`RadioButton`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/radioButton)s into one
field: a `radiogroup` named by its `label`, one value, one `name` for the form, and
one stop in the page's Tab order. Describe the choices with `options`.

RadioGroup:

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Plan"
  description="You can change your plan at any time."
  defaultValue="annual"
  options={[
    { value: "monthly", label: "Monthly", description: "Billed every month at $9" },
    { value: "annual", label: "Annual", description: "Billed once a year at $90" },
    { value: "lifetime", label: "Lifetime", description: "One payment of $249" },
  ]}
/>
```

Without `value` or `defaultValue`, nothing is selected until someone picks an option.
Without a visible `label`, name the group with `aria-label`.

## Controlled

Pass `value` and `onValueChange` when something else owns the choice. `onValueChange` gets the
new option's `value`, and is not called for the option already selected.

Controlled:

```tsx
const [plan, setPlan] = useState("annual");

<RadioGroup label="Plan" name="plan" options={plans} value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan} />
```

## Horizontal

`orientation="horizontal"` lays the radios out in a row that wraps. The arrow keys
work the same way in both orientations.

Horizontal:

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Size"
  orientation="horizontal"
  defaultValue="m"
  options={[
    { value: "s", label: "Small" },
    { value: "m", label: "Medium" },
    { value: "l", label: "Large" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Disabled

`disabled` on an option keeps it visible and skips it with the arrow keys. `disabled`
on the group disables every radio, and a disabled group submits nothing.

Disabled:

```tsx
<RadioGroup
  label="Region"
  defaultValue="eu"
  options={[
    { value: "eu", label: "Europe" },
    { value: "us", label: "United States" },
    { value: "ap", label: "Asia Pacific", description: "Coming soon", disabled: true },
  ]}
/>
```

## Custom layout

For a layout `options` cannot describe, such as radio cards in a grid, put
`RadioButton`s with a `value` anywhere inside the group. The group owns their
checked state, `name`, `disabled` and focus, and a RadioButton's own `onCheckedChange`
still runs when it is picked. `options`, when given too, render first.

Custom layout:

```tsx
<RadioGroup label="Instance" defaultValue="m">
  <Grid columns="3" gap="12" s={{ columns: "1" }}>
    <Column border radius="l" padding="16">
      <RadioButton value="s" label="Small" description="1 vCPU, 2 GB" />
    </Column>
    <Column border radius="l" padding="16">
      <RadioButton value="m" label="Medium" description="2 vCPU, 4 GB" />
    </Column>
    <Column border radius="l" padding="16">
      <RadioButton value="l" label="Large" description="4 vCPU, 8 GB" />
    </Column>
  </Grid>
</RadioGroup>
```

## Forms

Give the group a `name` and a form submits the selected `value` under it, as a set
of native radios would. Nothing is submitted while no option is selected.

## Keyboard

Only the selected radio is in the page's Tab order, or the first enabled radio
while none is selected, so Tab moves past the whole group in one step.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Down / Right | Focus and select the next radio, wrapping at the end. Right and Left swap in a right-to-left layout. |
| Up / Left | Focus and select the previous radio, wrapping at the start. |
| Space | Select the focused radio. |

Selection follows focus, as it does for native radios: a radio group is one choice,
and moving through it is how you make it.

## Validation and size

`error` marks the RadioGroup invalid (a danger border and `aria-invalid`);
`errorMessage` shows under it, linked with `aria-describedby`, and marks it
invalid too. `size` (`s`, `m`, `l`) scales the control and its text; left out,
it takes the enclosing `Form`'s `size`, as `Input` does.

Validation:

```tsx
<Form size="s">
    <RadioGroup
        label="Plan"
        errorMessage="Choose a plan"
        options={plans}
    />
</Form>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `TShirtSizes` |  | s, m or l. Left out, the enclosing Form's size, else m. |
| `error` | `boolean` |  | Mark it invalid: a danger border and aria-invalid. |
| `errorMessage` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown under it, linked with aria-describedby; marks it invalid too. |
| `options` | `RadioGroupOption[]` |  | One RadioButton per option, in order. |
| `value` | `string` |  | The selected option's value, when the host owns the state. Pair with onValueChange. |
| `defaultValue` | `string` |  | The option selected first when the group keeps its own state. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the newly selected value. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Submitted with the selected value inside a form. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | Visible label that names the group. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Helper text under the label, read out as the group's description. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable every radio in the group. |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `vertical` | Stack the radios, or lay them out in a row that wraps. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | RadioButtons with a value, in any layout. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

### RadioGroupOption

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | `-` | What value and onValueChange carry, and what a form submits. |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` | `-` | The radio's label. |
| `description` | `React.ReactNode` | `-` | Helper text under the label. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `-` | Visible, not selectable, skipped by the arrow keys. |
| `iconButtonProps` | `IconButtonProps` | `-` | A help button beside the label, as on RadioButton. |

# Select

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/select

> Select provides a dropdown menu for choosing from a list of options with optional search functionality.

The `Select` component offers a dropdown menu for selecting from a list of options. It's built on top of the `Dropdown` and `Input` components, providing a consistent user experience with other form controls. It draws a chevron that turns up while the list is open; a `suffix` you pass takes its place.

## When to use Select

Use `Select` for a form value: a field with a label that sits in a form or a settings row and is submitted, such as a timezone, a country or a member's role.

For a sort, filter, view or action picker on a toolbar or page header, use a secondary `Button` with `suffixIcon="chevronDown"` as the trigger of a `Dropdown` of `Option`s, and let the button's label name the current choice ("Sort: Newest"). It reads as a control, not as a field. A toolbar filter over a long list that people search is the exception: use the [toolbar size](#toolbar-size) below. Two to four choices that should stay visible fit a `SegmentedControl`.

Select:

```tsx
const [selectedCountry, setSelectedCountry] = useState("");

<Select
    id="basic-select"
    label="Choose a country"
    value={selectedCountry}
    options={[
      { label: "United States", value: "us" },
      { label: "Canada", value: "ca" },
      { label: "United Kingdom", value: "uk" },
      { label: "Australia", value: "au" }
    ]}
    onValueChange={country => setSelectedCountry(country as string)}
/>
```

## Searchable

Enable search functionality to filter options in large lists.

Searchable:

```tsx
const [selectedCountry, setSelectedCountry] = useState("");

<Select
    id="searchable-select"
    label="Choose a country"
    value={selectedCountry}
    searchable
    options={[
      { label: "United States", value: "us" },
      { label: "Canada", value: "ca" },
      { label: "United Kingdom", value: "uk" },
      { label: "Australia", value: "au" },
      { label: "Germany", value: "de" },
      { label: "France", value: "fr" },
      { label: "Japan", value: "jp" },
      { label: "Brazil", value: "br" }
    ]}
    onValueChange={country => setSelectedCountry(country as string)}
/>
```

## Empty state

Customize the message shown when no options match the search query.

Empty State:

```tsx
const [selectedCountry, setSelectedCountry] = useState("");

<Select
    id="empty-state-select"
    label="Choose a country"
    value={selectedCountry}
    searchable
    emptyState={
      <Text onBackground="neutral-weak">
        No matching countries found
      </Text>
    }
    options={[
      { label: "United States", value: "us" },
      { label: "Canada", value: "ca" },
      { label: "United Kingdom", value: "uk" },
      { label: "Australia", value: "au" }
    ]}
    onValueChange={country => setSelectedCountry(country as string)}
/>
```

## Multiple selection

Set `multiple` to allow selecting more than one option. `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange` take arrays when multiple mode is enabled.

Multiple selection:

```tsx
const [tags, setTags] = useState<string[]>([]);

<Select
  id="tags-select"
  label="Tags"
  multiple
  value={tags}
  options={[
    { label: "Design", value: "design" },
    { label: "Engineering", value: "engineering" },
    { label: "Product", value: "product" },
  ]}
  onValueChange={(value) => setTags(value as string[])}
/>
```

## Aligned

`alignSelected` opens the list with the selected option sitting on the field, and the others above and below it in their own order, as macOS draws a pop-up button. With nothing picked, the first option sits there. A long list shows a few rows on each side and scrolls the rest. It suits short, settings-style choices. Near the top or bottom of the screen, and on a searchable or multiple Select, it opens as a dropdown instead.

Aligned:

```tsx
const [density, setDensity] = useState("comfortable");

<Select
    id="aligned-select"
    label="Density"
    alignSelected
    value={density}
    options={[
      { label: "Compact", value: "compact" },
      { label: "Cozy", value: "cozy" },
      { label: "Comfortable", value: "comfortable" },
      { label: "Spacious", value: "spacious" },
      { label: "Roomy", value: "roomy" }
    ]}
    onValueChange={(next) => setDensity(next as string)}
/>
```

## Toolbar size

`size="xxs"` draws a 32px field, the height of a `size="s"` Button, for a filter in a toolbar. The label shows as the placeholder, and a searchable Select opens an `xxs` search field to match. Every other size keeps the `s` search field it had.

Toolbar size:

```tsx
const [status, setStatus] = useState("");

<Select
    id="xxs-select"
    size="xxs"
    label="Status"
    searchable
    value={status}
    options={[
      { label: "Paid", value: "paid" },
      { label: "Pending", value: "pending" },
      { label: "Refunded", value: "refunded" }
    ]}
    onValueChange={(next) => setStatus(next as string)}
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options (required)` | `SelectOptionType[]` |  | The choices, as value and label pairs. |
| `value` | `string \| string[]` |  | The selection, controlled. An array when multiple is set. Leave it out and the Select keeps its own. |
| `defaultValue` | `string \| string[]` |  | The starting selection when `value` is left out. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string \| string[]) => void` |  | Called with the new selection (the whole array when multiple is set). Was onSelect in 2.x. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Whether the list is open, controlled. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the list starts open, when `open` is left out. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with every open and close. |
| `emptyState` | `ReactNode` | `No results` | Shown when a search matches nothing. |
| `placement` | `Placement` |  | Which side the list opens on. |
| `alignSelected` | `boolean` | `false` | Open the list with the selected option sitting on the field, the others above and below it. |
| `searchable` | `boolean` | `false` | Add a filter field above the options. |
| `multiple` | `boolean` | `false` | Allow more than one choice. |
| `labels` | `SelectLabels` |  | The search field's name and its clear button's, { search, clear }, for a translated interface. Omitted fields stay English. |
| `fillWidth` | `boolean` | `true` | Match the parent's width. |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |  |
| `minHeight` | `SpacingToken` |  |  |
| `minWidth` | `SpacingToken` |  |  |
| `maxWidth` | `SpacingToken` |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

### SelectOptionType

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `value` | `string` |  |  |
| `onClick` | `(value: string) => void` |  |  |

# SubmitButton

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/submitButton

> A Button that shows a spinner and ignores repeat presses while its form submits.

`SubmitButton` is a `Button` with `type="submit"` that follows its form. When a `Form`'s `onSubmit` returns a promise, the form is pending until it settles: the button shows a spinner, can swap its label for `pendingLabel`, and ignores further presses, so a double click sends one request. The form is marked `aria-busy` meanwhile.

SubmitButton:

```tsx
<Form
    as="form"
    onSubmit={async (event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        await save(new FormData(event.currentTarget));
    }}
>
    <Input id="name" placeholder="Name" />
    <SubmitButton pendingLabel="Saving…">Save</SubmitButton>
</Form>
```

## Pending from outside

When the submit does not run through `onSubmit`, such as a server action or a mutation hook, pass `pending` to the `Form`, or to the button itself.

```tsx
const { mutate, isPending } = useSaveProfile();

<Form as="form" pending={isPending} onSubmit={(event) => { event.preventDefault(); mutate(); }}>
  <SubmitButton>Save</SubmitButton>
</Form>
```

`useFormPending()` returns the same state for anything else in the form that should react to it.

## Why aria-disabled

While pending the button is `aria-disabled`, not `disabled`. A natively disabled button drops focus to the page the moment it is pressed with the keyboard, and the user loses their place in the form. This one keeps focus and refuses the second press. Enter in a text field is refused the same way.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pendingLabel` | `ReactNode` |  | Label while the form is submitting. Defaults to the usual label. |
| `pending` | `boolean` |  | Force the pending look, for a submit the form does not track. |
| `...ButtonProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

---

# Switch

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/switch

> Switch provides a toggle control for binary states with a sliding animation and optional loading state.

The `Switch` component provides a toggle control for binary states, featuring a sliding animation when toggled. It's commonly used for enabling or disabling features and settings.

Switch:

```tsx
<Switch
    label="Enable notifications"
    description="Receive updates about new features and improvements"
    checked={isChecked}
    onCheckedChange={() => setIsChecked(!isChecked)}
/>
```

## State

Control the switch state with the `checked` prop. `onCheckedChange` receives the state the switch moves to, so the setter can be passed straight in.

State:

```tsx
const [isChecked, setIsChecked] = useState(false);

<Switch
    label={isChecked ? "Feature is now enabled" : "Feature is currently disabled"}
    checked={isChecked}
    onCheckedChange={setIsChecked}
/>
```

## Uncontrolled

Leave out `checked` and the switch keeps its own state, starting from `defaultChecked`. `onCheckedChange` still reports every change, and with a `name` the switch submits its value with a form.

Uncontrolled:

```tsx
<Switch
    label="Email notifications"
    name="notifications"
    value="on"
    defaultChecked
/>
```

## Loading

Show a loading spinner while an action is being processed.

Loading:

```tsx
const [isChecked, setIsChecked] = useState(false);
const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);

const handleToggle = () => {
    setIsLoading(true);
    
    // Simulate API call with timeout
    setTimeout(() => {
      setIsChecked(!isChecked);
      setIsLoading(false);
    }, 1000);
};

<Switch
    label="Processing"
    checked={isChecked}
    loading={isLoading}
    onCheckedChange={handleToggle}
/>
```

## Disabled

Disable the switch to prevent user interaction.

Disabled:

```tsx
<Switch
    label="Disabled switch"
    disabled
    checked={isChecked}
    onCheckedChange={() => setIsChecked(!isChecked)}
/>
```

## Reversed

Place the switch on the right side of the label.

Reversed:

```tsx
const [isChecked, setIsChecked] = useState(false);

<Switch
    label="Align switch to the right"
    description="This places the switch after the label text"
    reverse
    checked={isChecked}
    onCheckedChange={() => setIsChecked(!isChecked)}
/>
```

## Validation and size

`error` marks the Switch invalid (a danger border and `aria-invalid`);
`errorMessage` shows under it, linked with `aria-describedby`, and marks it
invalid too. `size` (`s`, `m`, `l`) scales the control and its text; left out,
it takes the enclosing `Form`'s `size`, as `Input` does.

Validation:

```tsx
<Switch
    label="Two-factor authentication"
    error
    errorMessage="Required for admins"
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `TShirtSizes` |  | s, m or l. Left out, the enclosing Form's size, else m. |
| `error` | `boolean` |  | Mark it invalid: a danger border and aria-invalid. |
| `errorMessage` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown under it, linked with aria-describedby; marks it invalid too. |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `description` | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| `iconButtonProps` | `IconButtonProps` |  |  |
| `auto` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `checked` | `boolean` |  | Whether it is on, controlled. Leave it out and the switch keeps its own state. |
| `defaultChecked` | `boolean` | `false` | The starting state when `checked` is left out. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Show a spinner in the track while something resolves. |
| `name` | `string` |  | Form field name. |
| `value` | `string` |  | Form field value. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Block interaction. |
| `reverse` | `boolean` | `false` | Put the label before the switch instead of after it. |
| `onCheckedChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the new state when it is flipped, by pointer or keyboard: true when it turns on. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `iconButtonProps` | `IconButtonProps` | `-` | Props forwarded to the icon button beside the label. |
| `...InputHTMLAttributes` |  |  | Also takes these props |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler` | `-` | The native change event of the hidden input, with the rest of the input attributes (name, required, onBlur), so a form library's register() works. |
| `aria-label` | `string` | `-` | Label for a switch with no visible one. |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# TagInput

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/tagInput

> Collect a list of values as removable tags inside a single field.

`TagInput` holds an array rather than a string. Each entry renders as a [Tag](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tag)
that can be removed on its own, and typing a new one appends to the array.

TagInput:

```tsx
const [tags, setTags] = useState<string[]>(["React", "Next.js"]);

<TagInput
    id="interests"
    value={tags}
    onValueChange={setTags}
    placeholder="Add interest"
    suffix={<Kbd position="absolute" top="12" right="12">Enter</Kbd>}
/>
```

## Uncontrolled

Leave out `value` and the input keeps its own list, starting from `defaultValue`. `onValueChange` still receives every new array.

Uncontrolled:

```tsx
<TagInput
    id="topics"
    label="Topics"
    defaultValue={["Design", "Code"]}
/>
```

## Toolbar size

`size="xxs"` starts the field at 32px, the height of a `size="s"` Button. It grows as chips are added, like every size.

Toolbar size:

```tsx
const [tags, setTags] = useState<string[]>(["React", "Next.js"]);

<TagInput
    id="interests"
    placeholder="Add interest"
    size="xxs"
    value={tags}
    onValueChange={setTags}
/>
```

## Keyboard and screen readers

The tags are a list, each with a remove button named after its tag. Backspace in an empty field removes the last tag, and a polite live region says which; after a remove button is used, focus goes back to the field. `labels` translates the button names and the announcement.

Translated:

```tsx
<TagInput
    id="themen"
    label="Themen"
    defaultValue={["Design", "Code"]}
    labels={{
      remove: (tag) => `${tag} entfernen`,
      removed: (tag) => `${tag} entfernt`,
    }}
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string[]` |  | The tags, as an array of strings, controlled. Leave it out and the input keeps its own list. |
| `defaultValue` | `readonly string[]` |  | The starting tags when `value` is left out. |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string[]) => void` |  | Receives the whole new array, after an add or a remove. Was onChange in 2.x. |
| `labels` | `TagInputLabels` |  | The remove buttons' names and the removal announcement, to translate them. |
| `onChange` | `ChangeEventHandler` | `-` | The native change event of the text field, as on Input. |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

Everything on [Input](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/input) — `label`, `description`, `error`,
`size`, `prefix`, `suffix` — works here too.

---

# Textarea

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/textarea

> A multi-line text input component for collecting longer form text content.

The `Textarea` component provides a multi-line text input field for collecting longer form text content from users. It grows with its content by default; pass `lines` a number to fix it at that many rows instead.

Textarea:

```tsx
<Textarea
    id="basic-textarea"
    label="Comments"
    placeholder="Enter your comments here"
/>
```

## Description

Add a description to provide additional context or instructions for the textarea.

Description:

```tsx
<Textarea
    id="bio-textarea"
    label="Bio"
    placeholder="Tell us about yourself"
    description="Your bio will be displayed on your public profile"
    lines={5}
/>
```

## Error state

Display error messages by setting the `error` and `errorMessage` props.

Error state:

```tsx
<Textarea
    id="error-textarea"
    label="Description"
    placeholder="Enter a description"
    error={true}
    errorMessage="This field is required"
/>
```

## Resize

Control how the textarea can be resized using the `resize` prop. It applies only
to a fixed height — a textarea left on the default `lines="auto"` sizes itself,
so it has no resize handle to give you.

Resize:

```tsx
<Textarea
    id="resize-vertical"
    label="Vertical Resize"
    placeholder="This textarea can be resized vertically"
    lines={4}
    resize="vertical"
/>

<Textarea
    id="resize-none"
    label="No Resize"
    placeholder="This textarea cannot be resized"
    lines={4}
    resize="none"
/>
```

## Fixed height

A textarea resizes itself to fit its content. Pass `lines` a number to fix it at
that many rows instead, which is also what gives it a resize handle.

Fixed height:

```tsx
<Textarea
    id="fixed-height-textarea"
    label="Notes"
    placeholder="Enter your notes"
    lines={4}
/>
```

## Height

Use the `size` prop to set the height of the input.

Height:

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<string>("");

const handleChange = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => {
    setValue(e.target.value);
};

<Textarea
    id="height-textarea"
    placeholder="Height"
    value={value}
    onChange={handleChange}
    size="l"
/>
```

## Radius

You can use the `corners` prop to apply custom radius to sides or corners. It works well with the `Column` component's `-1` gap to create a seamless connection between textareas.

Styling:

```tsx
<Column gap="-1" fillWidth>
    <Textarea
      id="custom-top"
      label="Top Radius"
      placeholder="This textarea has top radius"
      corners="top"
    />
    <Textarea
      id="custom-bottom"
      label="Bottom Radius"
      placeholder="This textarea has bottom radius"
      corners="bottom"
    />
</Column>
```

## State

Manage the `Textarea` state with React's useState hook.

State:

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState('');

const handleChange = (e) => {
    setValue(e.target.value);
};

<Textarea
    id="state-textarea"
    label="Message"
    value={value}
    onChange={handleChange}
    placeholder="Type your message"
/>
```

## Sizes

The Textarea component supports the same six sizes as Input, from `xxs` (a 32px first line, for a one-line note in a toolbar) to `xl`. At `xxs` a `label` shows as the placeholder, as it does on Input.

Sizes:

```tsx
<Textarea id="size-xxs" placeholder="Extra Extra Small" size="xxs" />
<Textarea id="size-xs" placeholder="Extra Small" size="xs" />
<Textarea id="size-s" placeholder="Small" size="s" />
<Textarea id="size-m" placeholder="Medium" size="m" />
<Textarea id="size-l" placeholder="Large" size="l" />
<Textarea id="size-xl" placeholder="Extra Large" size="xl" />
```

Validation:

```tsx
const validateContent = (value) => {
    if (value && value.length < 20) {
        return "Please enter at least 20 characters";
    }
    return null;
};

<Textarea
    id="validation-textarea"
    label="Review"
    placeholder="Write your review"
    validate={validateContent}
/>
```

## Character count

Display a character counter with color-coded feedback based on remaining characters. The counter changes color when approaching the limit.

Character count:

```tsx
const [bio, setBio] = useState<string>("");

const handleChange = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLTextAreaElement>) => {
    setBio(e.target.value);
};

<Textarea
    id="bio-textarea"
    placeholder="Bio"
    value={bio}
    onChange={handleChange}
    maxLength={200}
    characterCount
    lines={4}
/>
```

## Focus ring

Like `Input`, a textarea draws no focus ring by default. Set `focusRing` to
outline the field on focus — see [Input](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/input#focus-ring) for
the whole story.

Focus ring:

```tsx
<Textarea id="about" label="About" focusRing />
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id (required)` | `string` |  |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `lines` | `number \| "auto"` | `auto` |  |
| `size` | `FieldSize` |  |  |
| `error` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `errorMessage` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `corners` | `"none" \| "top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" \| "top-left" \| "top-right" \| "bottom-right" \| "bottom-left"` |  | Round only some corners. Inside a [Form](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/form) with density="stacked" this is worked out for you. |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `suffix` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `variant` | `"default" \| "ghost"` | `default` | Ghost drops the border and background. |
| `focusRing` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `characterCount` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `resize` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical" \| "both" \| "none"` | `vertical` |  |
| `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the field's text after every change, after the native onChange. Controlled only when value is set. |
| `validate` | `(value: ReactNode) => ReactNode \| null` |  | Run on a debounce, controlled or not; return a message to show, or null to clear. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `span` | `number` |  | How many columns to occupy inside a [Form](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/form-controls/form) grid. Ignored outside one. |
| `fillWidth` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...TextareaHTMLAttributes` |  |  | Also takes these props |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Components overview

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/overview

> Every component in Once UI, grouped by what it is for.

Eighty components is a lot to scroll past alphabetically. This groups them by
the job they do, so you can find the one you need without knowing its name.

If you are new, start with [Structure](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/basics/structure) — layout is the part
everything else sits inside.

## Layout

The primitives, and the containers built from them.

- [Flex](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/flex) — the layout primitive; one axis, and every shared prop
- [Grid](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/grid) — two-dimensional layout with a responsive column count, or masonry columns for items of uneven height
- [SplitView](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/splitView) — two resizable panes, collapsing to tabs when narrow
- [Line](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/line) — a rule, horizontal or vertical
- [Mask](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/mask) — reveal content through a shape or cursor-following window

## Surfaces

Things that hold other things.

- [Card](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/card) — a surface that can be selected or clicked
- [Background](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/background) — gradients, dots, grids and lines behind a section
- [Fade](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/fade) — an edge that dissolves into the surface behind it
- [Banner](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/banner) — a full-width strip for an announcement
- [Book](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/book) — a 3D cover, for showing a publication

## Content

- [Heading](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/heading) — headings on the type scale
- [Text](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/text) — everything else on the type scale
- [BlockQuote](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/blockquote) — a pulled quote
- [InlineCode](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/inlineCode) — code inside a sentence
- [Kbd](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/kbd) — a key or shortcut
- [List](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/List) — ordered and unordered lists
- [Table](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/table) — sortable, selectable, paginated rows
- [Timeline](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/timeline) — events in order
- [Media](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/media) — images and video, with the framework's optimizer when there is one
- [MediaPlayers](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/mediaPlayers) — audio and video with real controls
- [CompareImage](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/compareImage) — two images under a draggable divider
- [Logo](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/logo) / [LogoCloud](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/logoCloud) — a mark, and a grid of them
- [OgCard](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/ogCard) — a link rendered as its own preview

## Navigation

- [SmartLink](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/smartLink) — the link, routed through the framework adapter
- [Button](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/button) / [IconButton](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/iconButton) / [ToggleButton](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/toggleButton)
- [SegmentedControl](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/segmentedControl) — one choice from a small set
- [Dropdown](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dropdown) / [Option](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/option) — a trigger and the menu it opens
- [Dropdown `openOn="contextmenu"`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dropdown#context-menu) — a menu on right-click
- [User `dropdown`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/user#menu) — the account menu
- [NavIcon](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/navIcon) — the hamburger, animated
- [ScrollToTop](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/scrollToTop) — the button that comes back on scroll

## Overlays

- [Dialog](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dialog) — a modal, stackable
- [Dialog `variant="sheet"`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dialog#sheet) — a full-height sheet with an optional backdrop
- [Tooltip](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tooltip) — a label on hover
- [HoverCard](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/hoverCard) — a preview on hover
- [Tooltip `content`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tooltip#info-icon) — an info icon that explains a field
- [Toast](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/toast) — transient confirmation
- [EmojiPicker](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/emojiPicker), inline or from a `trigger`

## Status and feedback

- [Spinner](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/spinner) — work in progress, duration unknown
- [Skeleton](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/skeleton) — the shape of content that has not arrived
- [ProgressBar](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/progressBar) — work in progress, duration known
- [StatusIndicator](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/statusIndicator) — a state dot, or a pulsing live indicator
- [Tag](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tag) — a label, an announcement or a toggle (Badge and Chip in 2.x)
- [Feedback](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/feedback) — an inline message with a severity

## Identity

- [Avatar](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/avatar) / [AvatarGroup](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/avatarGroup) — a person, and several
- [User](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/user) — avatar, name and detail as one unit
- [Icon](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/icon) — the icon set, typed by name

## Scrolling

- [Scroller](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/scroller) — a scrollable strip with arrow affordances
- [Scroller](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/scroller#track-mode) track mode — a run of tiles with drag, wrap-around and markers
- [Carousel](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/carousel) — one item at a time, cross-fading or snapping (`mode="snap"`)
- [Scroller `auto`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/scroller#auto) — a continuously moving strip
- [InfiniteScroll](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/infiniteScroll) — load more as it comes into view
- [ScrollLock](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/scrollLock) — freeze the page behind an overlay

## Motion

- [RevealFx](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/effects/revealFx) — enter on scroll
- [Animation](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/animation) — the primitive the rest are built on
- [HoverCard `placement="cover"`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/hoverCard#cover) — content over its trigger on hover
- [Scrubber](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/scrubber) — a playhead over time

See [Effects](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/effects/effect) for the ambient layers — blobs, matrix, weather,

- [ThemeSwitcher](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/themeSwitcher) — light, dark, system
