# Arrow

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/arrow

> An animated arrow that slides in while the element its trigger names is hovered.

A decorative arrow that animates in while a trigger element is hovered: the cue on a card or link that the whole surface goes somewhere. `Button` (`arrowIcon`) and `Tag` (`arrow`) draw the same arrow themselves; use `Arrow` on its own for anything else, such as a whole-card link or a hover card.

Arrow:

```tsx
<Row id="arrow-trigger-1" vertical="center" gap="8">
  Simple usage
  <Arrow trigger="#arrow-trigger-1" scale={1} />
</Row>
<Row id="arrow-trigger-2" vertical="center" gap="8" solid="brand-medium" onSolid="brand-strong">
  Customized usage
  <Arrow trigger="#arrow-trigger-2" color="onSolid" scale={1.2} />
</Row>
```

## On a card

Give the card an `id` and point `trigger` at it. The arrow takes Flex's layout props, so `position`, `top` and `right` pin it to a corner (a number is on the token scale, as the spacing step of the same name is).

Card:

```tsx
<Card id="case-study" href="/stories/case-study" position="relative" padding="24" radius="l" direction="column" gap="4">
  <Text textVariant="heading-strong-s">Read the case study</Text>
  <Text onBackground="neutral-weak">How a team of two shipped in a week.</Text>
  <Arrow trigger="#case-study" position="absolute" top="24" right="24" />
</Card>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger (required)` | `string` |  | CSS selector for the element whose hover draws the arrow. |
| `scale` | `number` | `0.8` | Arrow size, as a multiplier of its 16px box. |
| `color` | `"onBackground" \| "onSolid"` | `onBackground` | Whether it draws for a background or on a solid surface. |
| `as` | `"div" \| "span"` |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

## Usage notes

- `trigger` must be a valid CSS selector (`#element-id`, `[data-card="pro"]`), and the element must be on the page when the arrow mounts.
- The arrow is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; the trigger element carries the link or action.
- For a button or a tag, use `Button arrowIcon` or `Tag arrow`, which wire the hover for you.

# ArrowNavigation

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/arrowNavigation

> Internal since 3.0: use the useArrowNavigation hook for arrow-key movement.

`ArrowNavigation` is internal in Once UI 3.0. It is the arrow-key container `DropdownWrapper` and `DatePicker` use, and it is no longer exported from `@once-ui-system/core` (nor are `useArrowNavigationContext` and `withArrowNavigation`).

Use the [`useArrowNavigation`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/hooks/useArrowNavigation) hook on a container of your own: give it the container's ref and call its `handleKeyDown` from the container's `onKeyDown`. Wrap the container in [`FocusTrap`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/focusTrap) if focus should stay inside it.

useArrowNavigation:

```tsx
const listRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
const navigation = useArrowNavigation({ layout: "column", itemCount: 3, containerRef: listRef });

return (
  <Column ref={listRef} role="listbox" tabIndex={-1} onKeyDown={navigation.handleKeyDown}>
    <Option value="1" label="One" />
    <Option value="2" label="Two" />
    <Option value="3" label="Three" />
  </Column>
);
```

See [Migrating from 2.x](https://github.com/once-ui-system/core/blob/main/MIGRATING.md) for the full list of exports that became internal.

# AvatarGroup

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/avatarGroup

> The AvatarGroup component displays multiple avatars in a horizontal stack with customizable appearance and overflow handling.

A component for displaying multiple user avatars in a compact, horizontal stack. Commonly used in collaborative interfaces to show team members, participants, or contributors.

AvatarGroup:

```tsx
<AvatarGroup
    size="l"
    avatars={[
      { src: "/images/avatar.jpg" },
      { value: "B" },
      { value: "C" },
      { value: "D" },
      { value: "E" }
    ]}
/>
```

## Sizes

AvatarGroup supports the same T-shirt sizing model as Avatar.

Sizes:

```tsx
<AvatarGroup
    size="s"
    avatars={[
      { value: "A" },
      { value: "B" },
      { value: "C" },
      { value: "D" }
    ]}
/>
```

## Limit

Use the `limit` prop to control how many avatars are displayed. Any additional avatars will be represented by a count indicator.

Limit:

```tsx
<AvatarGroup
    size="m"
    limit={3}
    avatars={[
      { value: "A" },
      { value: "B" },
      { value: "C" },
      { value: "D" },
      { value: "E" },
      { value: "F" },
      { value: "G" }
    ]}
/>
```

## Reverse order

Use the `reverse` prop to change the stacking order of avatars.

Reverse:

```tsx
<AvatarGroup
    size="m"
    avatars={[
      { value: "A" },
      { value: "B" },
      { value: "C" },
    ]}
/>

<AvatarGroup
    size="m"
    reverse
    avatars={[
      { value: "A" },
      { value: "B" },
      { value: "C" },
    ]}
/>
```

## Mixed types

AvatarGroup supports all the same avatar types as the Avatar component.

Mixed:

```tsx
<AvatarGroup
    size="m"
    avatars={[
      { src: "/images/avatar.jpg" },
      { value: "B" },
      { empty: true },
      { value: "D", statusIndicator: { scheme: "green" } }
    ]}
/>
```

| `size` | `TShirtSizes` | `m` | Size of every avatar in the stack. |
| `reverse` | `boolean` | `false` | Stack from the other side. |
| `limit` | `number` |  | Show at most this many, then a +N. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

# Background

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/background

> The Background component provides customizable decorative backgrounds with gradients, dots, grids, lines, and masking effects.

A versatile component for creating decorative backgrounds with various visual effects. Commonly used to add visual interest to sections, cards, or containers while maintaining a clean and modern aesthetic.

Background:

```tsx
<Background
    fill
```

Add diagonal or straight lines to your backgrounds with customizable angle, thickness, and spacing.

Combine multiple background effects to create unique and visually interesting backgrounds.

Stacking:


Create a spotlight or reveal effect with the mask property.

Mask:


# Badge

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/badge

> Badge is Tag in Once UI 3.0: an announcement is <Tag variant="announce">.

`Badge` folded into [Tag](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tag) in Once UI 3.0 and is no longer exported. Its look is `<Tag variant="announce">`, with `href`, `arrow` and `effect` as before:

Badge → Tag:

```tsx
// 2.x
<Tag variant="announce" label="New release" prefixIcon="rocket" href="/changelog" />

// 3.0
<Tag variant="announce" label="New release" prefixIcon="rocket" href="/changelog" />
```

`title` is `label` and `icon` is `prefixIcon`. Each arrow now follows hover on its own tag, so the `id` 2.x needed on every badge of a page can go. The 3.0 codemod rewrites the element, its import and its props. See [Tag: Announcement](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tag#announcement).

# Banner

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/banner

> The Banner component displays important information in a highlighted horizontal bar across the interface.

A simple component for displaying important announcements, notifications, or status messages in a prominent horizontal bar. Commonly used to draw attention to critical information or updates.

Banner:

```tsx
<Banner>
    Free shipping on orders over $50
</Banner>
```

## Announcement

A launch strip: a soft mesh drawn from the theme's brand and accent scales, an inline link, and a dismiss button. With a `dismissKey` the dismissal is remembered in the browser and the banner stays hidden from the first paint on later visits (ThemeInit reads it). Use a new key for each announcement.

Announcement:

```tsx
<Banner
  variant="mesh"
  dismissKey="launch-3-0"
  link={{ label: "Try it out", href: "/changelog" }}
>
  Once UI 3.0 is here: our fastest, most agent-friendly release yet.
</Banner>
```

Pick the colour scales the mesh is drawn from with `meshColors`.

Mesh colours:

```tsx
<Banner variant="mesh" meshColors={["success", "info", "accent"]}>
  Your workspace is ready.
</Banner>
```

## With icons

Add icons to enhance visual communication.

Banner with icon:

```tsx
<Banner radius="s">
    <Icon name="check" size="s" />
    Claim your free credits.
</Banner>

<Row fillWidth padding="8">
    <Background height="64" fillWidth radius="m" border="neutral-alpha-medium" lines={{display: true, angle: -45, color: "neutral-alpha-weak", size: "8", thickness: 1}}/>
</Row>
```

## Custom styling

Customize the appearance of banners using Flex props.

Custom styled banners:

```tsx
<Banner solid="success-medium" onSolid="success-strong">
    <Icon name="check" size="s" />
    Operation completed successfully.
</Banner>

<Banner solid="warning-medium" onSolid="warning-strong">
    <Icon name="warning" size="s" />
    Please review your information before proceeding.
</Banner>

<Banner solid="danger-medium" onSolid="danger-strong">
    <Icon name="danger" size="s" />
    Critical error detected in the system.
</Banner>
```

## With actions

Add interactive elements to banners.

Banner with actions:

```tsx
<Banner horizontal="between">
    Accept our privacy policy to continue.
    <Row gap="8" data-theme="dark">
      <Button size="s">Decline</Button>
      <Button size="s" variant="secondary">Accept</Button>
    </Row>
</Banner>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"solid" \| "mesh"` | `solid` | solid is a flat brand strip; mesh is a soft blurred gradient wash from the theme's colour scales. |
| `meshColors` | `ColorScheme[]` |  | Up to three colour scales the mesh is drawn from. Default brand, accent, brand. |
| `link` | `{ label: ReactNode; href: string }` |  | An inline, underlined call to action after the message. |
| `dismissible` | `boolean` |  | Shows a dismiss button. Hides the banner until the next page load. |
| `dismissKey` | `string` |  | Remembers the dismissal in the browser under this key (implies dismissible). Use a new key per announcement. |
| `dismissLabel` | `string` |  | The dismiss button's accessible name. |
| `children` |  |  |  |
| `...flex` |  |  | Also takes these props |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# BlockQuote

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/blockquote

> The BlockQuote component displays a highlighted quotation with semantic <blockquote> markup.

Use `BlockQuote` to present quoted text with emphasis and proper semantics. It renders a semantic `<blockquote>` element and forwards all layout and style props from `Flex`.

BlockQuote:

```tsx
<BlockQuote
    author={{
      name: "Lorant",
      avatar: "/images/avatar.jpg",
    }}
    link={{
      href: "https://once-ui.com/blog/truth",
      label: "once-ui.com"
    }}
    subline="Building is lonely if you do it alone.">
    “If you’re going to take this path, find your people.”
</BlockQuote>
```

## Content

Use the `children` prop as the quote text and display an additional `preline` or `subline`.

Content:

```tsx
<BlockQuote
    preline="That’s when we realized the deeper problem."
    subline="Open your feed and you’ll see the same promises everywhere."
    author={{
      name: "Lorant",
      avatar: "/images/avatar.jpg",
    }}>
    “So much of the industry has shifted from solving real problems to selling shortcuts.”
</BlockQuote>
```

## Link

Attach a citation source using the `link` attribute. This is useful for accessibility and provenance.

Link:

```tsx
<BlockQuote
    author={{
      name: "Lorant",
    }}
    link={{
      href: "once-ui.com/truth",
      label: "once-ui.com"
    }}>
    “The first time a stranger pays for something you’ve built — something that came entirely from your mind — your worldview changes forever.”
</BlockQuote>
```

## Author

Include an author line below the quote.

Author:

```tsx
<BlockQuote
    author={{
      name: "Lorant",
      avatar: "/images/avatar.jpg",
    }}>
      “No single piece guarantees success, but together, they create inevitability. Over time, people start recognizing your name, your style, your values, and your products. That recognition compounds.”
</BlockQuote>
```

## Separators

Adjust the visibility of the separator lines by setting `top`, `bottom` or `none` to the `separator` prop.

Separator:

```tsx
<BlockQuote separator="top">
    “We weren’t interested in selling visions that fall apart the moment someone buys in. We wanted to build products that last.”
</BlockQuote>
```

## Alignment

Adjust the alignment of the quote text by setting `align` to `left`, `center` or `right`.

Alignment:

```tsx
<BlockQuote
    align="left"
    separator="none"
    author={{
      name: "Lorant",
    }}
    link={{
      href: "once-ui.com/truth",
      label: "once-ui.com"
    }}>
    “The first time a stranger pays for something you’ve built — something that came entirely from your mind — your worldview changes forever.”
</BlockQuote>
<BlockQuote
    align="right"
    separator="top"
    author={{
      name: "Lorant",
    }}
    link={{
      href: "once-ui.com/truth",
      label: "once-ui.com"
    }}>
    “The first time a stranger pays for something you’ve built — something that came entirely from your mind — your worldview changes forever.”
</BlockQuote>
```

## Styling

`BlockQuote` ships with a default look, but you can override appearance using any `Flex` styling props.

Styling:

```tsx
<BlockQuote 
    border="neutral-alpha-medium"
    background="surface"
    radius="xl"
    padding="l"
    align="left"
    separator="none"
    author={{
      name: "Lorant",
    }}
    link={{
      href: "once-ui.com/truth",
      label: "once-ui.com"
    }}>
    <Text textVariant="heading-default-l">“The first time a stranger pays for something you’ve built — something that came entirely from your mind — your worldview changes forever.”</Text>
</BlockQuote>
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children (required)` | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| `preline` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Content rendered above the quote, such as a label or eyebrow. |
| `subline` | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| `separator` | `"top" \| "bottom" \| "both" \| "none"` | `both` |  |
| `author` | `{ name?: React.ReactNode; avatar?: string; }` |  |  |
| `link` | `{ href: string; label: string }` |  |  |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `align` | `"center" \| "left" \| "right"` | `center` |  |
| `children` |  |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

## Accessibility Considerations

`BlockQuote` renders a semantic `<blockquote>` element to convey quoted content to assistive technologies. Provide a `link` URL when available to reference the source. Ensure sufficient color contrast if you override the default `background` or `onBackground` props.

# Book

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/book

> A cover with real depth: a spine, a page block and a tilt on hover.

`Book` renders artwork as a physical book rather than a flat image: a cover, a
blurred spine shadow, and a visible block of pages hinged on the cover's right
edge. On hover the whole object turns, and because the rotation is a real 3D
transform the page block turns with it instead of sliding behind it.

Use it wherever a cover is the subject — a library, a reading list, a chapter
index. For a plain image in a frame, use [`Media`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/media).

Book:

```tsx
<Row maxWidth="12rem">
  <Book src="/images/cover.jpg" alt="Once UI" />
</Row>
```

## Sizing

`Book` fills the box you give it and keeps its own cover proportions, so size it
from the outside — a `maxWidth` on the parent, or a grid cell. It takes every
`Flex` prop, so `aspectRatio`, `radius` and the spacing tokens work as usual.

## As a link

Pass `href` to make the whole book a link. It renders through
the same link element as [`Button`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/button), so internal routes get
client-side navigation and external ones get the right `rel`.

Linked book:

```tsx
<Book
  href="/library/once-ui"
  src="/images/cover.jpg"
  alt="Once UI"
/>
```

## Overlaying a title

`children` render above the artwork, inside a dark-themed column, so text sits
legibly on top of a cover. Leave `src` off entirely to get a blank cover you
compose yourself.

Overlay:

```tsx
<Book src="/images/cover.jpg" alt="Once UI">
  <Column fill vertical="end" padding="20" gap="4">
    <Text textVariant="heading-strong-m" onBackground="neutral-strong">Once UI</Text>
    <Text textVariant="label-default-s" onBackground="neutral-medium">A design system</Text>
  </Column>
</Book>
```

## Motion

The tilt is hover-gated and switched off under `prefers-reduced-motion`. On
touch devices the cover stays square-on: there is no hover to return from, and a
permanently rotated cover reads as a rendering fault rather than a style.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` |  | Cover artwork. Omit it for a blank cover you fill with children. |
| `alt` | `string` |  | Alternative text for the cover artwork. |
| `sizes` | `string \| number` |  | Responsive sizes hint passed to the underlying image. |
| `href` | `string` |  | Renders the whole book as a link. |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `-` | Overlaid on the cover, above the artwork. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Breadcrumbs

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/breadcrumbs

> Where the current page sits in the site: a navigation landmark with an ordered list of links.

`Breadcrumbs` renders the trail from the site's root to the current page as a `nav`
landmark named "Breadcrumb", holding an ordered list. The last item is the current
page and carries `aria-current="page"`. The separators are drawn but hidden from
screen readers, which announce the list and its length instead.

Breadcrumbs:

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs
  items={[
    { label: "Docs", href: "/", prefixIcon: "home" },
    { label: "Components", href: "/components/overview" },
    { label: "Breadcrumbs" },
  ]}
/>
```

Each crumb with an `href` is a [`SmartLink`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/smartLink), so an internal
path goes through the app's Link adapter: with `LayoutProvider` from
`@once-ui-system/core/next` it is a client-side navigation. A crumb without one is
plain text, for a section that has no page of its own. The current page links only
if you give it an `href`.

## Long trails

`maxItems` collapses a longer trail to the first crumb, a "more" button and the last
`maxItems - 1` crumbs. The button expands the whole trail in place and moves focus to
the first crumb it revealed. The minimum is 2: the root and the current page.

maxItems:

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs
  maxItems={3}
  items={[
    { label: "Home", href: "/" },
    { label: "Acme", href: "/acme" },
    { label: "Design", href: "/acme/design" },
    { label: "Website", href: "/acme/design/website" },
    { label: "Assets", href: "/acme/design/website/assets" },
    { label: "Hero.png" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Separator

The default separator is a small chevron. Pass any node as `separator`; it is hidden
from screen readers wherever it is drawn.

Separator:

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs separator="/" items={items} />
```

The landmark is named "Breadcrumb". Pass `aria-label` only to translate it.
`Breadcrumbs` is a Row and takes every Flex prop, such as `marginBottom` or a
different `textVariant`.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items (required)` | `BreadcrumbItem[]` |  | The trail, from the root to the current page. |
| `separator` | `ReactNode = <Icon name="chevronRight" size="xs" />` |  | Drawn between crumbs, hidden from screen readers. |
| `maxItems` | `number` |  | Collapse a longer trail to the first crumb, a more button and the last maxItems - 1. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

### BreadcrumbItem

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `React.ReactNode` | `-` | The crumb's text. |
| `href` | `string` | `-` | Where the crumb links. Without it the crumb is plain text. |
| `prefixIcon` | `IconName` | `-` | A leading icon. |

# Carousel

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/carousel

> The Carousel component displays a collection of images with navigation controls and transition effects.

An interactive component for displaying a collection of images with smooth transitions and navigation controls. The Carousel supports both line and thumbnail indicators for navigation between images.

> **Two components scroll a row** Pick by the job. [Carousel](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/carousel) shows one image or slide at a time, with line or thumbnail indicators and autoplay, or as a touch-first track on native scroll snapping with `mode="snap"` (2.x Swiper). [Scroller](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/scroller) scrolls overflowing chips, tabs or cards behind arrow buttons and edge fades; in track mode it moves a run of tiles with drag, wrap-around, markers and proximity scaling (2.x ScrollContainer), and with `auto` it is a marquee that moves on its own (2.x AutoScroll).

Carousel:

```tsx
<Carousel
    items={[
      { slide: "/images/1.jpg", alt: "Image 1" },
      { slide: "/images/2.jpg", alt: "Image 2" },
    ]}
/>
```

## Indicator

The Carousel supports two types of indicators for navigation: line (default) and thumbnail.

Indicator:

```tsx
<Carousel
    indicator="line"
    items={[
      { slide: "/images/1.jpg", alt: "Image 1" },
      { slide: "/images/2.jpg", alt: "Image 2" },
    ]}
/>

<Carousel
    indicator="thumbnail"
    items={[
      { slide: "/images/1.jpg", alt: "Image 1" },
      { slide: "/images/2.jpg", alt: "Image 2" },
    ]}
/>
```

## Controls

You can hide the controls with the `controls` prop.

Controls:

```tsx
<Carousel
    controls={false}
    items={[
      { slide: "/images/1.jpg", alt: "Image 1" },
      { slide: "/images/2.jpg", alt: "Image 2" },
    ]}
/>
```

## Aspect ratio

You can customize the aspect ratio of the carousel to fit your design needs.

Aspect ratio:

```tsx
<Carousel
    aspectRatio="4 / 3"
    items={[
      { slide: "/images/1.jpg", alt: "Image 1" },
      { slide: "/images/2.jpg", alt: "Image 2" },
    ]}
/>
```

## Auto Play

You can enable auto play with the `play` prop. Each field has its own default: `play={{ auto: true }}` moves every 3000ms with a pause button. Autoplay holds while the pointer is over the carousel, stops when keyboard focus comes into it, and does not start for a visitor who asks for reduced motion; the button then offers Play. Name the button in another language with `pauseLabel` and `playLabel`, and the carousel itself with `aria-label`.

Auto Play:

```tsx
<Carousel
    controls={false}
    indicator={false}
    aria-label="Theme previews"
    play={{auto: true, interval: 5000, controls: true, progress: true}}
    items={[
      { slide: "/images/1.jpg", alt: "Image 1" },
      { slide: "/images/2.jpg", alt: "Image 2" },
    ]}
/>
```

## Custom content

You can place custom content inside the slides as `ReactNode`.

Custom content:

```tsx
<Carousel
    items={[
      { slide: <Row height="20rem" fill center radius="s" background="brand-strong"><Text>Slide 1</Text></Row> },
      { slide: <Row height="20rem" fill center radius="s" background="accent-strong"><Text>Slide 2</Text></Row> },
    ]}
/>
```

## Snap mode

`mode="snap"` swaps the cross-fade for a touch-first track the slides scroll along, with native snapping, drag, arrows and dots. Its `aspectRatio` defaults to `"16 / 9"`, `controls="contained"` draws the dots over the slides, and `translateY`, `defaultRevealed`, `thumbnail` and `play` do not apply. It was `Swiper` in 2.x.

Swiper:

```tsx
<Carousel mode="snap"
    items={[
      { slide: "/images/backgrounds/1.jpg", alt: "Image 1" },
      { slide: "/images/backgrounds/2.jpg", alt: "Image 2" },
    ]}
/>
```

### Interactions

Snap mode uses native CSS scroll-snap, providing smooth touch gestures on mobile, trackpad scrolling, and mouse drag-to-scroll on desktop. Simply click and drag to navigate between slides.

Interactions:

```tsx
<Carousel mode="snap"
    items={[
      { slide: "/images/backgrounds/1.jpg", alt: "Image 1" },
      { slide: "/images/backgrounds/2.jpg", alt: "Image 2" },
      { slide: "/images/backgrounds/3.jpg", alt: "Image 3" },
    ]}
/>
```

### Indicators

By default, snap mode displays dot indicators below the carousel. The active dot is highlighted and slightly scaled for better visibility.

Indicators:

```tsx
<Carousel mode="snap"
    items={[...]}
/>

<Carousel mode="snap"
    items={[...]} indicator={false}
/>
```

### Controls

The `controls` prop supports three options: `true` (appear on hover), `false` (hidden), or `"contained"` (always visible inside the carousel). Buttons are automatically hidden when at the first or last slide.

Controls:

```tsx
<Carousel mode="snap"
    controls={true} // Appear on hover
    items={[...]}
/>

<Carousel mode="snap"
    controls="contained" // Always visible
    items={[...]}
/>

<Carousel mode="snap"
    controls={false} // Hidden
    items={[...]}
/>
```

### Aspect ratio

Customize the aspect ratio of the carousel to fit your design needs. Supports standard aspect ratio values.

Aspect ratio:

```tsx
<Carousel mode="snap"
    aspectRatio="16 / 9"
    items={[...]}
/>

<Carousel mode="snap"
    aspectRatio="4 / 3"
    items={[...]}
/>

<Carousel mode="snap"
    aspectRatio="1 / 1"
    items={[...]}
/>
```

### Custom content

You can place custom content inside the slides as `ReactNode`, not just images.

Custom content:

```tsx
<Carousel mode="snap"
    items={[
      { slide: <Row fill center background="brand-strong"><Text>Slide 1</Text></Row> },
      { slide: <Row fill center background="accent-strong"><Text>Slide 2</Text></Row> },
      { slide: <Row fill center background="neutral-strong"><Text>Slide 3</Text></Row> },
    ]}
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items (required)` | `CarouselItem[]` |  |  |
| `mode` | `"fade" \| "snap"` | `fade` | "fade" (the default) cross-fades slides; "snap" is a touch-first snapping track (2.x Swiper). |
| `controls` | `boolean \| "contained"` |  |  |
| `priority` | `boolean` |  | Eager-load the first slide. Use it when the carousel is above the fold. |
| `stretch` | `boolean` |  | Drop the intrinsic aspect ratio and let slides fill their box. |
| `indicator` | `"line" \| "thumbnail" \| false` |  |  |
| `translateY` | `SpacingToken \| number \| CSSUnit` |  |  |
| `aspectRatio` | `string` |  |  |
| `sizes` | `string \| number` |  |  |
| `unoptimized` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `defaultRevealed` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `thumbnail` | `ThumbnailItem` |  | Sizing of the thumbnail strip when indicator is "thumbnail". |
| `play` | `{ auto?: boolean; interval?: number; controls?: boolean; progress?: boolean; pauseLabel?: string; playLabel?: string; }` |  | Autoplay: `auto`, `interval` (3000), `controls` (the pause button, on unless false), `progress`, and the button's `pauseLabel` and `playLabel`. |
| `auto` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# ConfirmButton

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/confirmButton

> A button for an action that is hard to take back: press it twice, or hold it, to confirm.

One press of a `ConfirmButton` never acts. In the default `"twice"` mode the
first press arms it: the label asks for a second press, the button turns
`armedTone` (danger by default) and a bar runs down the time left. A second
press within `timeout` runs `onConfirm`. Escape, moving focus away or the time
running out disarms it, and a double click's second press is ignored, so a
double click never confirms by accident.

Reach for it where a dialog would be too slow and one press too easy: a manual
trip, stopping a deploy, deleting a row in a dense table.

ConfirmButton:

```tsx
<ConfirmButton
  label="Manual trip"
  labels={{ confirm: "Press again to trip" }}
  onConfirm={trip}
/>
<ConfirmButton mode="hold" label="Hold to silence" onConfirm={silence} />
```

## Hold

`mode="hold"` fills the button while it is held, by pointer or by Space or
Enter, and acts when it is full (`holdDuration`, 1.5 s by default). Letting go
early cancels.

## Accessibility

Every change is in words: the label changes as the button arms or fills, and a
status line tells a screen reader how to confirm or cancel. The bar and the
colour only repeat what the label says.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onConfirm (required)` | `() => void` |  |  |
| `mode` | `"twice" \| "hold"` | `twice` |  |
| `labels` | `Partial<ConfirmButtonLabels>` |  |  |
| `timeout` | `number` | `4000` |  |
| `holdDuration` | `number` | `1500` |  |
| `armed` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `defaultArmed` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `onArmedChange` | `(armed: boolean) => void` |  |  |
| `armedTone` | `ButtonProps["tone"]` | `danger` |  |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Drawer

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/drawer

> A panel that slides in from any edge over the page: mobile navigation, filters, a detail view beside a list.

`Drawer` is a modal dialog that slides in from an edge of the viewport. It is built
on the same pieces as [`Dialog`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dialog): it renders into a portal on the
body, makes the rest of the page inert, locks page scroll, keeps Tab inside with
[`FocusTrap`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/focusTrap), and gives focus back to whatever opened it
when it closes. Escape, a click on the overlay and the close button all ask it to
close through `onClose`; the drawer never closes itself.

Drawer:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open drawer</Button>
<Drawer
  open={open}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
  title="Filters"
  description="Narrow the list of projects."
  footer={
    <>
      <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Apply</Button>
    </>
  }
>
  <Column gap="16" paddingTop="8">
    <Input id="owner" label="Owner" />
    <Input id="tag" label="Tag" />
  </Column>
</Drawer>
```

The title is the dialog's accessible name and the description its description.
Without a title, pass `aria-label` so a screen reader can announce what opened.
The content scrolls between the header and the footer.

## Side and size

`side` picks the edge: `left`, `right` (the default), `top` or `bottom`. `size` is
the drawer's extent from that edge: the width of a left or right drawer, and the
maximum height of a top or bottom one, which is otherwise as tall as its content.

| `size` | Extent |
| --- | --- |
| `s` | 20rem |
| `m` | 28rem (default) |
| `l` | 40rem |
| `full` | The whole viewport, less the inset |

The drawer floats a small step in from the edge, as `Dialog` does on small screens,
and never grows past the viewport.

Side:

```tsx
<Drawer open={open} onClose={close} side="bottom" size="s" title="From the bottom">
  …
</Drawer>
```

## Navigation

A mobile navigation is a `left` drawer. `flush` drops the header and the padding,
so a list reaches the edges, and floats the close button in the corner. The title
still names the dialog, for screen readers only. This replaces the hand-made
`Animation` and fixed-`Column` menus behind a `NavIcon`, which had no dialog role,
no focus trap and no Escape.

Navigation:

```tsx
<Drawer open={open} onClose={close} side="left" size="s" title="Navigation" flush>
  <Column padding="8" paddingTop="64" gap="2">
    <NavItem href="/projects" icon="folder" label="Projects" selected />
    <NavItem href="/inbox" icon="inbox" label="Inbox" badge={3} />
    <NavItem href="/settings" icon="settings" label="Settings" />
  </Column>
</Drawer>
```

Close it when the route changes, as the menus it replaces did:

Route change:

```tsx
const pathname = usePathname();
useEffect(() => setOpen(false), [pathname]);
```

## Focus

On open, focus moves to the first focusable element (the close button, unless
`showClose` is off), or to `initialFocusRef`. On close it returns to the element
that had it before, or to `returnFocusRef`, and it is returned even if the drawer
unmounts while open. While the drawer slides out it is inert itself, so a quick Tab
cannot land back inside it.

A dropdown or picker inside the drawer that handles Escape itself (and calls
`preventDefault`, as Once UI's do) closes on its own without closing the drawer.

Set `closeOnClickaway={false}` for a drawer that holds unsaved input, so a stray
click on the overlay does not throw it away.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `open (required)` | `boolean` |  | Whether the drawer is open. |
| `onClose (required)` | `() => void` |  | Called on Escape, an overlay click and the close button. |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right" \| "top" \| "bottom"` | `right` | The edge the drawer slides in from. |
| `size` | `"s" \| "m" \| "l" \| "full"` | `m` | The width of a left or right drawer; the maximum height of a top or bottom one. |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  | The heading and the dialog's accessible name. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | A line under the title, announced as the dialog's description. |
| `footer` | `ReactNode` |  | Actions pinned below the scrolling content. |
| `showClose` | `boolean` | `true` | Show the close button. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `Close` |  |
| `closeOnClickaway` | `boolean` | `true` | Close when the overlay is clicked. |
| `flush` | `boolean` | `false` | No header and no padding; the title is kept for screen readers. |
| `initialFocusRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | The element to focus on open, instead of the first focusable one. |
| `returnFocusRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | The element to focus on close, instead of the one that opened the drawer. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The drawer's content. It scrolls. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Dropdown

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dropdown

> A trigger and the floating panel it opens: menus of options, pickers and selectors, and right-click context menus.

Dropdown is a trigger and the panel it opens, with the positioning and state management of a dropdown menu. In 3.0 it took the API of 2.x `DropdownWrapper`: the content goes in `children` (2.x `dropdown`, still accepted for one minor), and the 2.x `Dropdown` panel is internal. It provides a flexible way to create custom dropdown interfaces with various trigger elements and dropdown contents. It supports keyboard navigation when used with `Option` components.

## Basic usage

A simple dropdown with a button trigger and custom content.

Dropdown:

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
const [selected, setSelected] = useState("");

const options = [
    { label: "Option 1", value: "option1" },
    { label: "Option 2", value: "option2" },
    { label: "Option 3", value: "option3" }
];

const handleSelect = (value: string) => {
    setSelected(value);
    setIsOpen(false);
};

return (
    <Dropdown
      open={isOpen}
      onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
      trigger={
        <Button 
          variant="secondary" 
          suffixIcon="chevronDown"
          onClick={() => setIsOpen(!isOpen)}
        >
          {selected ? options.find(opt => opt.value === selected)?.label : "Select an option"}
        </Button>
      }><Column minWidth="10rem" padding="4" gap="2">
          {options.map((option) => (
            <Option
              key={option.value}
              label={option.label}
              value={option.value}
              selected={option.value === selected}
              onClick={handleSelect}
            />
          ))}
        </Column></Dropdown>
);
```

## Placement

Control the placement of the dropdown relative to its trigger element.

Placement:

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);

return (
  <Row horizontal="center">
    <Dropdown
      open={isOpen}
      onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
      placement="top"
      trigger={
        <Button onClick={() => setIsOpen(!isOpen)}>
          Open Upward
        </Button>
      }><Column fillWidth padding="4" gap="2">
          <Option
            label="Top option"
            value="top"
            onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
          />
          <Option
            label="Middle option"
            value="middle"
            onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
          />
          <Option
            label="Bottom option"
            value="bottom"
            onClick={() => setIsOpen(false)}
          />
        </Column></Dropdown>
  </Row>
);
```

## Custom

Control the dimensions of the dropdown menu.

Custom:

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
const [selected, setSelected] = useState("");
const [searchQuery, setSearchQuery] = useState("");

const options = [
    { label: "Apple", value: "apple", description: "Fruit" },
    { label: "Banana", value: "banana", description: "Fruit" },
    { label: "Carrot", value: "carrot", description: "Vegetable" },
    { label: "Broccoli", value: "broccoli", description: "Vegetable" },
    { label: "Orange", value: "orange", description: "Fruit" }
];

const handleSelect = (value: string) => {
    setSelected(value);
    setIsOpen(false);
};

const filteredOptions = options.filter(option => 
    option.label.toLowerCase().includes(searchQuery.toLowerCase())
);

return (
    <Dropdown
      open={isOpen}
      onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
      minHeight="200px"
      trigger={
        <Button 
          variant="secondary" 
          suffixIcon="chevronDown"
          onClick={() => setIsOpen(!isOpen)}
        >
          {selected ? options.find(opt => opt.value === selected)?.label : "Search items"}
        </Button>
      }><Column fillWidth minWidth="12rem">
          <Column padding="4" fillWidth position="sticky" top="0" background="surface" zIndex={1}>
            <Input
              size="s"
              id="search-dropdown"
              placeholder="Search"
              prefix={<Icon name="search" size="xs" />}
              value={searchQuery}
              onChange={(e) => setSearchQuery(e.target.value)}
              onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
            />
          </Column>
          <Column fillWidth gap="2" padding="4">
            {filteredOptions.length > 0 ? (
              filteredOptions.map((option) => (
                <Option
                  key={option.value}
                  label={option.label}
                  value={option.value}
                  description={option.description}
                  selected={option.value === selected}
                  onClick={handleSelect}
                />
              ))
            ) : (
              <Flex fillWidth center paddingX="16" paddingY="32">
                <Text>No results found</Text>
              </Flex>
            )}
          </Column>
        </Column></Dropdown>
);
```

## Where it opens

A panel opens on the option marked `aria-selected="true"`, scrolled into view
inside the panel, the way a native select opens on the value it is already
showing. `Option` sets that attribute from its `selected` prop, so a list built
from `Option` needs nothing further. With no selection the panel opens on its
first enabled option; a selected option that is disabled is skipped.

A panel that leads with something other than its list — a searchable `Select`
and its query field — opens on that instead.

## Button triggers

A `Button` or `IconButton` passed as the `trigger` renders a real
`<button type="button">` with `aria-haspopup` and `aria-expanded`, so the
dropdown opens from the keyboard as well as the mouse. There is no need to add
`type="button"` or an empty `onClick` to make it one. A disabled trigger does not
open the dropdown.

## Nested menus

Put a `Submenu` among the Options to nest a menu: its children are the items of the next level, and a Submenu can hold another. A pick at any depth reaches the Dropdown's `onSelect` and closes the whole menu, as any pick does. Submenus work in a context menu (`openOn="contextmenu"`) the same way.

Submenu:

```tsx
<Dropdown openOn="hover" trigger={<Button variant="secondary" suffixIcon="chevronDown">File</Button>}><Column padding="4" gap="2" minWidth="12rem">
    <Option value="new" label="New file" prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="document" onBackground="neutral-weak" />} />
    <Submenu label="Share" prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="send" onBackground="neutral-weak" />}>
      <Option value="email" label="Email" />
      <Option value="link" label="Copy link" />
      <Submenu label="Export as">
        <Option value="pdf" label="PDF" />
        <Option value="png" label="PNG" />
        <Option value="svg" label="SVG" />
      </Submenu>
    </Submenu>
    <Option value="rename" label="Rename" prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="edit" onBackground="neutral-weak" />} />
    <Line marginY="2" />
    <Option value="delete" label="Delete" danger prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="delete" onBackground="danger-medium" />} />
  </Column></Dropdown>
```

A submenu opens when the pointer rests on its item for a moment (`openDelay`, 100 ms), on a click or tap, and with Right arrow, Enter or Space, which also move focus to its first item. Left arrow or Escape closes it and returns focus to its item; Escape on the first level then closes the menu. The pointer can cut diagonally from the item into the open submenu across the items below it without closing it, and the submenu opens on the other side, or shifts, near the edge of the screen. In right-to-left layouts the arrows swap.

With a Submenu inside, the Dropdown's panel is a `menu`, its Options are `menuitem`s and its trigger says `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Each Submenu's item carries `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and its panel is a `menu` named after it. In any menu or list, typing the first letters of an item moves to it.

## Open on hover

`openOn="hover"` also opens the panel when the pointer rests on the trigger (`openDelay`, 100 ms by default) and closes it once the pointer has been away from the trigger and every panel of the menu for `closeDelay` (300 ms), enough to cross the gap or overshoot an edge. A panel the pointer opened leaves focus on the page and does not lock scrolling. A click on the trigger pins it open, and from the keyboard (Enter, Space, or an arrow key while it is open) it behaves as a click-opened dropdown. Touch screens have no hover, so a tap opens it there. The example above opens on hover.

## Context menu

`openOn="contextmenu"` opens the Dropdown at the pointer on right-click (or the context menu key) over its `trigger`, as a `menu` of `menuitem`s that stays on screen. `contents` renders no box around the trigger. It was `ContextMenu` in 2.x, which took the region as children and the menu as `dropdown`.

ContextMenu:

```tsx
<Dropdown openOn="contextmenu" trigger={<Row fillWidth align="center" horizontal="center" padding="40" radius="l" background="surface" border="neutral-alpha-medium" textVariant="label-default-m">Right click me</Row>}
    placement="bottom-start"><Column gap="2" padding="4" minWidth="10rem">
        <Option
          prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="edit" onBackground="neutral-weak" />}
          label="Edit"
          value="edit"
        />
        <Option
          prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="document" onBackground="neutral-weak" />}
          label="Duplicate"
          value="duplicate"
        />
        <Option
          prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="copy" onBackground="neutral-weak" />}
          label="Copy"
          value="copy"
        />
        <Option
          prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="eyeOff" onBackground="neutral-weak" />}
          label="Hide"
          value="hide"
        />
        <Line marginY="2" />
        <Option
          prefix={<Icon size="xs" name="delete" onBackground="danger-medium" />}
          danger
          label="Delete"
          value="delete"
        />
      </Column></Dropdown>
```

### Keyboard and screen readers

The menu opens at the pointer, or at the element when it is opened from the keyboard (Shift+F10 or the Menu key). Near the right or bottom edge of the screen it opens to the left of or above the pointer, so it stays on screen. It is a `menu` and its Options are `menuitem`s: the arrow keys move between them, skipping disabled ones and wrapping at the ends, Home and End jump to the first and last, and Escape closes it and returns focus to where it was.

### Without a wrapper box

`Dropdown openOn="contextmenu"` wraps its children in a box. Set `contents` to render the wrapper with `display: contents` instead, so it adds nothing to the layout: an absolutely positioned child still positions against its own ancestors, and a grid or flex item stays one. A timeline clip or a table row can take a context menu this way without a hand-made one. With `contents` there is no box for `className`, `style` or the disabled dimming to style.

contents:

```tsx
<Grid columns="3" gap="8">
  {files.map((file) => (
    <Dropdown openOn="contextmenu" trigger={<FileTile file={file} />} key={file.id} contents><FileMenu file={file} /></Dropdown>
  ))}
</Grid>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fillWidth` | `boolean` |  | Match the trigger's width. |
| `minWidth` | `number \| CSSUnit` |  | Lower bound on the dropdown's width: a number is on the token scale (16 = 1rem), a string a CSS length ("12rem"). |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| CSSUnit` |  | Upper bound on the dropdown's width: a number is on the token scale (16 = 1rem), a string a CSS length ("12rem"). |
| `minHeight` | `number \| CSSUnit` |  | Lower bound on the dropdown's height: a number is on the token scale (16 = 1rem), a string a CSS length. |
| `placement` | `Placement` |  | Which side of the trigger it opens on, and how it aligns. |
| `trigger (required)` | `ReactNode` |  | The element that opens the dropdown. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | What opens. Usually a Column of Options. |
| `openOn` | `"click" \| "hover" \| "contextmenu"` | `click` | What opens it: a click on the trigger, the pointer resting on it ("hover", a click still works), or a right-click ("contextmenu") at the pointer. |
| `openDelay` | `number` |  | With openOn="hover": how long, in ms, the pointer rests on the trigger before it opens. |
| `closeDelay` | `number` |  | With openOn="hover": how long, in ms, the pointer may be away from the trigger and its panels before it closes. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | With openOn="contextmenu": the region does not open the menu, and is dimmed. |
| `contents` | `boolean` |  | With openOn="contextmenu": no box around the trigger (display: contents). |
| `selectedOption` | `string` |  | Value of the Option to mark as current. |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `onSelect` | `(value: string) => void` |  | Called with the value of the Option that was picked. |
| `closeAfterClick` | `boolean` |  | Close on selection. Turn it off for a multi-select. |
| `handleArrowNavigation` | `boolean` |  | Move through options with the arrow keys. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Controlled open state. Leave it out to let the component manage its own. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called whenever it opens or closes, controlled or not. |
| `nested` | `boolean` |  | Marks a dropdown opened from inside another one. |
| `navigationLayout` | `NavigationLayout` |  | Whether arrow keys walk a row, a column or a grid. |
| `columns` | `number \| string` |  | Grid width, for a grid navigation layout. |
| `optionsCount` | `number` |  | How many options there are, when the component cannot count them itself. |
| `dropdownId` | `string` |  | Id for the dropdown element, to reference from a label. |
| `disableTriggerClick` | `boolean` |  | Stop the trigger opening it, when something else does. |
| `alignSelected` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onFocusCapture` | `React.FocusEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  |
| `onBlurCapture` | `React.FocusEventHandler<HTMLDivElement>` |  |  |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
### Submenu

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label (required)` | `ReactNode` |  | The item's label in the menu around it. Also names the submenu. |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` |  | Before the label: an icon, an avatar. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | A second line under the label. |
| `suffix` | `ReactNode` |  | After the label. Defaults to a chevron pointing the way the submenu opens. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | The item cannot open its submenu, and is skipped by the arrow keys. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The submenu's items: Options, more Submenus, Lines between groups. |
| `minWidth` | `number \| CSSUnit` | `192` | Lower bound on the submenu's width: a number is on the token scale (16 = 1rem), a string a CSS length. |
| `maxWidth` | `number \| CSSUnit` |  | Upper bound on the submenu's width: a number is on the token scale (16 = 1rem), a string a CSS length. |
| `openDelay` | `number` |  | How long, in ms, the pointer rests on the item before the submenu opens. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |

# DropdownWrapper

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dropdownWrapper

> Merged into Dropdown in 3.0.

`DropdownWrapper` became [`Dropdown`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dropdown) in 3.0: the same props, with the content in `children` instead of `dropdown` (still accepted for one minor). The 2.x `Dropdown` panel is internal; its children go straight into `Dropdown`. The 3.0 codemod rewrites it (see the migration guide, "Components that merged").

---

# ElementType

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/elementType

> Internal since 3.0: the link-or-button element behind Button, IconButton and SmartLink.

`ElementType` is internal in Once UI 3.0. It is the element `Button`, `IconButton`, `ToggleButton` and `SmartLink` render as a link when they get an `href` and as a button otherwise, through the framework adapter, and it is no longer exported from `@once-ui-system/core`.

Use the component for the job instead:

- A link: [`SmartLink`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/smartLink), which routes internal links through your framework's link.
- An action: [`Button`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/button) or [`IconButton`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/iconButton), which become links when given an `href`.
- A bare clickable box: a plain `<a>` or `<button>` with a `Flex` inside it.

See [Migrating from 2.x](https://github.com/once-ui-system/core/blob/main/MIGRATING.md) for the full list of exports that became internal.

# EmojiPicker

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/emojiPicker

> The EmojiPicker component provides a way to select emojis from categories.

The `EmojiPicker` component allows you to select and insert emojis from categories.
It carries its emoji dataset, so it has its own entry point and stays out of the
root bundle: `import { EmojiPicker } from "@once-ui-system/core/emoji";`

EmojiPicker:

```tsx
<EmojiPicker onSelect={(emoji) => console.log(emoji)} />
```

## Columns

You can pass a `columns` prop to the component to override the default columns.

Columns:

```tsx
<EmojiPicker columns={10} onSelect={(emoji) => console.log(emoji)} />
```

## Custom style

You can pass a `style` prop to the component to override the default styles.

Custom style:

```tsx
<EmojiPicker
    background="surface"
    border="neutral-medium"
    padding="8"
    radius="l"
    height="24rem"
    onSelect={(emoji) => console.log(emoji)}
/>
```

## From a trigger

With `trigger`, the picker opens in a Dropdown from it and closes itself after a pick, controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange` or not at all. `placement` and `closeAfterClick` set where it opens and whether it closes; other Dropdown props go in `dropdownProps`. It was `EmojiPickerDropdown` in 2.x.

EmojiPickerDropdown:

```tsx
const [selectedEmoji, setSelectedEmoji] = useState("");

<Row gap="16" vertical="center">
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<Button label="Select Emoji" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
  />
  {selectedEmoji && (
    <Text textVariant="heading-default-xl">
      Selected: {selectedEmoji}
    </Text>
  )}
</Row>
```

### With IconButton trigger

You can use an `IconButton` as the trigger for a more compact UI.

With IconButton:

```tsx
const [selectedEmoji, setSelectedEmoji] = useState("");

<Row gap="16" vertical="center">
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<IconButton icon="smiley" variant="secondary" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
  />
  {selectedEmoji && (
    <Text textVariant="heading-default-xl">
      {selectedEmoji}
    </Text>
  )}
</Row>
```

### Columns

You can customize the number of columns in the emoji grid.

Custom columns:

```tsx
const [selectedEmoji, setSelectedEmoji] = useState("");

<Row gap="16" vertical="center">
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<Button label="Select Emoji (10 columns)" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
    columns="10"
  />
  {selectedEmoji && (
    <Text textVariant="heading-default-xl">
      {selectedEmoji}
    </Text>
  )}
</Row>
```

### Placement

Control where the dropdown appears relative to the trigger using the `placement` prop.

Placement:

```tsx
const [selectedEmoji, setSelectedEmoji] = useState("");

<Row gap="16" wrap vertical="center">
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<Button label="Top" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
    placement="top"
  />
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<Button label="Bottom" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
    placement="bottom"
  />
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<Button label="Left" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
    placement="left"
  />
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<Button label="Right" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
    placement="right"
  />
  {selectedEmoji && (
    <Text textVariant="heading-default-xl">
      {selectedEmoji}
    </Text>
  )}
</Row>
```

### Custom background

Customize the dropdown background color.

Custom background:

```tsx
const [selectedEmoji, setSelectedEmoji] = useState("");

<Row gap="16" vertical="center">
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<Button label="Custom Background" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
    background="neutral-weak"
  />
  {selectedEmoji && (
    <Text textVariant="heading-default-xl">
      {selectedEmoji}
    </Text>
  )}
</Row>
```

### Controlled state

Control the open/close state externally using `open` and `onOpenChange`.

Controlled state:

```tsx
const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useState(false);
const [selectedEmoji, setSelectedEmoji] = useState("");

<Row gap="16" vertical="center">
  <EmojiPicker
    trigger={<Button label="Controlled Dropdown" />}
    onSelect={(emoji) => setSelectedEmoji(emoji)}
    open={isOpen}
    onOpenChange={setIsOpen}
  />
  <Button 
    variant="secondary" 
    label={isOpen ? "Close" : "Open"} 
    onClick={() => setIsOpen(!isOpen)}
  />
  {selectedEmoji && (
    <Text textVariant="heading-default-xl">
      {selectedEmoji}
    </Text>
  )}
</Row>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onSelect (required)` | `(emoji: string) => void` |  | Called with the chosen emoji. |
| `trigger` | `React.ReactNode` |  | Open the picker from this element, in a Dropdown (2.x EmojiPickerDropdown). |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | With trigger: controlled open state. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | With trigger: open on first render. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | With trigger: called with the next open state. |
| `placement` | `Placement` |  | With trigger: where it opens. |
| `closeAfterClick` | `boolean` | `true` | With trigger: close after a pick. |
| `dropdownProps` | `Omit< DropdownProps, "trigger" \| "children" \| "dropdown" \| "open" \| "onOpenChange" >` |  | With trigger: further Dropdown props. |
| `onClose` | `() => void` |  | Called when the picker is dismissed. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `background` | `StyleProps["background"]` |  | Surface colour behind the grid. |
| `columns` | `GridSize` |  | Emoji per row. |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# EmptyState

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/emptyState

> What a page, panel or list shows before it has anything in it: a visual, a title, one line on what to do, and the action that does it.

An empty page is the first thing a new user sees, so it should say what belongs there and offer the one step that puts it there. EmptyState does that in one tag, at three sizes, with a Mascot, a Cube Emote or an icon above it.

Page:

```tsx
<EmptyState
  size="l"
  visual={<Mascot size="l" surface="flat" lookAt="pointer" effects={false} />}
  title="No clients yet"
  description="Invite a client by email. They fill in their company details once, and every contract reads them from there."
  action={<Button size="s" prefixIcon="plus" label="New client" />}
/>
```

## Sizes

`l` is for a whole page with nothing in it yet, `m` for a card or panel, and `s` for inside a table, list, select or chart. Table's own empty and no-results states use `s`.

Sizes:

```tsx
<EmptyState
  icon="inbox"
  title="No invoices"
  description="Invoices show up here once a contract is accepted."
  secondaryAction={<Button size="s" variant="secondary" label="Learn more" />}
/>

<EmptyState
  size="s"
  icon="search"
  titleAs="h3"
  title="No results"
  description="Try a different search or filter"
  action={<Button size="s" variant="secondary" label="Clear filters" />}
/>
```

## Writing it

- The title says what is missing, plainly: "No clients yet", not "Nothing to see here".
- The description is one sentence on what fills the space, or what happens next.
- One primary action. When the page header has the same button, hide it there while the page is empty, so the step shows once.
- A Mascot reads best with `surface="flat"`. A Cube Emote from once-ui.com/emotes goes in `visual` the same way.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `visual` | `ReactNode` |  | What sits above the title: a Mascot, a Cube Emote, an illustration. Wins over icon. |
| `icon` | `IconName` |  | A plain icon above the title, when there is no visual. |
| `title (required)` | `ReactNode` |  | What is empty, said plainly. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | One sentence on what fills it, or what to do next. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | The one next step, usually the page's primary button. |
| `secondaryAction` | `ReactNode` |  | A second, quieter step. |
| `size` | `EmptyStateSize` | `m` | s inside a table or list, m in a card, l for a whole page. |
| `titleAs` | `"h1" \| "h2" \| "h3" \| "h4" \| "h5" \| "h6"` | `h2` | The title's element. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Fade

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/fade

> A component that creates a gradient fade effect in a specified direction with optional pattern and blur.

The Fade component creates a gradient fade effect that transitions from a base color to transparent in a specified direction. It can be used to create visually appealing overlays, masks, or transitions between content areas.

Fade:

```tsx
<Flex border="brand-alpha-medium" fillWidth aspectRatio={4 / 3} radius="l" overflow="hidden">
    <Media src="/image.jpg" />
    <Fade
      fillWidth
      position="absolute"
      top="0"
      to="bottom"
      topRadius="l"
      height="12rem"
      pattern={{ display: true, size: "2" }}
    />
    <Fade
      fillWidth
      position="absolute"
      bottom="0"
      to="top"
      bottomRadius="l"
      height="12rem"
      pattern={{ display: true, size: "2" }}
    />
</Flex>
```

## Direction

Control the direction of the fade effect.

Direction:

```tsx
<>
    <Fade
      fill
      position="absolute"
      left="0"
      to="right"
      leftRadius="l"
    />
    Fade from left to right
</>
```

## Base color

Customize the base color of the fade effect.

Base color:

```tsx
<>
    <Fade
      fill
      position="absolute"
      base="brand-medium"
      top="0"
      to="bottom"
      topRadius="l"
    />
    Match base color with background
</>
```

## Pattern

Add a dot pattern to the fade effect.

Pattern:

```tsx
<>
    <Fade
      fill
      position="absolute"
      base="page"
      bottom="0"
      to="top"
      bottomRadius="l"
      pattern={{ display: true, size: "8" }}
    />
    Dot pattern
</>
```

## Blur

Add a blur effect to the fade.

Blur:

```tsx
<>
    <Fade
      fill
      position="absolute"
      base="page"
      bottom="0"
      to="top"
      blur="2rem"
      bottomRadius="l"
    />
    Blur size
</>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `to` | `"bottom" \| "top" \| "left" \| "right"` | `bottom` | Which way it fades out. |
| `base` | `BaseColor` | `page` | The colour it fades from. Match the surface behind it, or the fade shows as a band of the wrong colour. |
| `blur` | `number \| CSSUnit` |  | Backdrop blur behind the fade: a number on the token scale (8 = 0.5rem) or a CSS length. Default 0.5rem. |
| `pattern` | `{ display?: boolean; size?: SpacingToken; }` | `{ display: false, size: "4", }` | Overlay a dot pattern in the base colour, and at what spacing. |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | Content drawn above the fade. |
| `position` | `CSSProperties["position"]` | `relative` |  |
| `children` |  |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Family footer

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/familyFooter

> One footer for a family of products: the brand's own band and links, then the sibling products and a co-brand bar that look the same on every site.

When one company makes several products, each site's footer is where a
visitor learns the others exist. `FamilyFooter` gives every site the same four
bands in the same order:

1. **Brand band.** The product's logo, its one-line promise and the primary button, plus one extra of the brand's choosing: a big wordmark, the mascot, a newsletter field.
2. **Link columns.** Up to five, chosen per site.
3. **Family row.** "More from Dopler": one tile per live sibling, with its mark, name and a line of four to six words. The product the footer is on is left out.
4. **Co-brand bar.** "A product by Dopler" with the parent's mark, then the year and legal entity, the language switch, the theme switch, social links and "Built with Once UI".

The first two bands are the brand's: they take its colours from the theme and
can carry a `decoration` behind them (a glow, a drawing, a background effect).
The family row and the co-brand bar sit on neutral tokens and keep one layout,
so the products read as one family wherever a visitor meets them.

The three previews below are one made-up family, Halden & Co, styled as three of its products.

Footer:

```tsx
import { FamilyFooter } from "@once-ui-system/blocks";

<FamilyFooter
  current="chirio"
  brand={{
    name: "Chirio",
    logo: <Logo icon="/trademarks/chirio-icon.svg" text="Chirio" href="/" />,
    tagline: "Understand your users, agents do the chores.",
    action: { label: "Start free", href: "/signup" },
  }}
  decoration={<BrandGlow />}
  columns={[
    { title: "Product", links: [{ label: "Pricing", href: "/pricing" }] },
    { title: "Developers", links: [{ label: "Docs", href: "https://docs.chirio.dev" }] },
    { title: "Legal", links: [{ label: "Privacy", href: "/privacy" }] },
  ]}
  legal="Dopler Kft."
  languageSwitch={<LocaleSwitcher />}
  social={[{ icon: "github", label: "GitHub", href: "https://github.com/…" }]}
/>
```

With an extra:

```tsx
<FamilyFooter
  current="ember"
  brand={{
    name: "Ember",
    tagline: "Tables, takeaway and the week's specials, in one place.",
    action: { label: "Open your café", href: "/start" },
    extra: <NewsletterField />,
  }}
  decoration={<CounterDrawing />}
  columns={columns}
/>
```

Quiet:

```tsx
<FamilyFooter
  current="quill"
  brand={{
    name: "Quill",
    tagline: "Contracts in plain words, signed in minutes.",
    action: { label: "Start a contract", href: "/new" },
  }}
  columns={fiveColumns}
/>
```

## The family

`familyProducts` is the list the footer shows by default, and `familyParent`
(Dopler) the company named in the co-brand bar. A new product added to the
list reaches every app's footer on its next blocks bump. A product with
`live: false` stays out of the row until it is public.

The list carries no artwork. Without a `mark`, a tile draws the name's first
letter on the product's `color`, or on the strongest neutral. An app that has
the marks passes them in:

Marks:

```tsx
import { FamilyFooter, familyProducts } from "@once-ui-system/blocks";

const marks: Record<string, string> = {
  chirio: "/trademarks/chirio-icon.svg",
  tavilio: "/trademarks/tavilio-icon.svg",
};

<FamilyFooter
  current="aveiro"
  brand={brand}
  products={familyProducts.map((product) => ({ ...product, mark: marks[product.id] }))}
/>
```

## Company and legal pages

The company lives in one place: About, careers, press and the terms and
privacy that apply to every product sit on the parent's site, and each
product's Company column links there instead of keeping its own copy. The
co-brand bar links the parent's shared legal page (`parent.legalHref`,
`https://dopler.app/legal` for Dopler). A product's own pages (pricing,
docs, support, its product-specific terms) stay on its own site.

The footer sets no cookies and draws no cookie banner. Pair it with
cookieless analytics and the page needs none.

## Referrals

Each sibling link, the parent link and the Once UI credit carry
`ref=<current>-footer`, so each product's analytics shows which sibling sent
the visit. A link that already has a `ref` keeps it. `familyHref(href, from)`
is the same rule for links an app draws itself.

## Languages

`labels` changes every word the footer writes itself; `familyFooterLabelsHu`
is the Hungarian set. A `productBy` label that already names the parent ("A
Dopler terméke") is shown as it is.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `brand` | `{ name, logo?, href?, tagline?, action?, extra? }` | required |
| `current` | `string`: the product the footer is on | |
| `columns` | `{ title, links: { label, href, tag? }[] }[]`, up to five | `[]` |
| `products` | `FamilyProduct[]` | `familyProducts` |
| `parent` | `{ name, href, mark?, legalHref? }` | `familyParent` |
| `legal` | `string` | the parent's name |
| `year` | `number` | this year |
| `social` | `{ icon, label, href }[]` | `[]` |
| `languageSwitch` | `ReactNode` | |
| `themeSwitch` | `boolean` | `true` |
| `builtWith` | `boolean` | `true`, `false` on Once UI |
| `decoration` | `ReactNode` | |
| `width` | `"s"`, `"m"` or `"l"` | `"l"` |
| `labels` | `FamilyFooterLabels` | |

# FocusTrap

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/focusTrap

> Keeps Tab inside a region while it is open, and gives focus back when it closes.

`FocusTrap` cycles Tab and Shift+Tab within its subtree while `active`, and
returns focus to wherever it came from when deactivated. It is the piece that
makes a dialog keyboard-safe: without it Tab walks straight out of the panel
into the page behind, which for a screen-reader or keyboard user means the
dialog effectively is not modal.

[`Dropdown`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dropdown), [`Dialog`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dialog) and [`Drawer`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/drawer) use it. Reach for it directly when you are building an overlay of your
own.

FocusTrap:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<FocusTrap active={open} onEscape={() => setOpen(false)}>
  <Column background="surface" radius="l" padding="24" gap="16">
    <Heading textVariant="heading-strong-m">Rename project</Heading>
    <Input id="name" label="Name" />
    <Row gap="8" horizontal="end">
      <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Cancel</Button>
      <Button onClick={save}>Save</Button>
    </Row>
  </Column>
</FocusTrap>
```

## What it traps

Focusable elements are found with
`button, [href], input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])`, in
DOM order. Two consequences worth knowing:

- A region with **no** focusable elements focuses the container itself, so focus
  is still inside rather than left on the page behind.
- Arrow keys are deliberately **not** handled — they pass through, so
  [`useArrowNavigation`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/hooks/useArrowNavigation) can own them. The two
  compose: `FocusTrap` decides what Tab may reach, `useArrowNavigation`
  decides what the arrows move between.

## Controlling where focus lands

By default the trap focuses the first focusable element on activation and
restores the previously focused element on deactivation. Both ends can be
pointed somewhere specific.

Focus targets:

```tsx
const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
const trigger = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);

// Open on the field rather than the first button, and hand focus back to the
// trigger even if it was not what opened the panel.
<FocusTrap
  active={open}
  initialFocusRef={input}
  returnFocusRef={trigger}
  onEscape={close}
>
  {children}
</FocusTrap>
```

Set `autoFocus={false}` when the region should open without stealing focus —
an inline editor revealed under the cursor, say. Set `restoreFocus={false}`
when the element that opened the region is gone by the time it closes, and
returning focus to it would throw the user to the top of the document.

## Escape

`onEscape` fires on the Escape key and nothing else — the trap never closes
itself. Owning the open state in the caller is what lets a confirm step or an
unsaved-changes prompt sit in between.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children (required)` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `active (required)` | `boolean` |  | Whether the trap is on. Required. |
| `onEscape` | `() => void` |  | Called on the Escape key. The trap does not close itself. |
| `containerRef` | `RefObject<HTMLDivElement \| null>` |  | Supply the container ref when the caller also needs it. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `initialFocusRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | Element to focus on activation, instead of the first focusable one. |
| `returnFocusRef` | `RefObject<HTMLElement \| null>` |  | Element to focus on deactivation, instead of the previously focused one. |
| `restoreFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Return focus when it deactivates. |
| `autoFocus` | `boolean` | `true` | Move focus into the region when it activates. |

# HeaderMenu

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/headerMenu

> The phone menu of a landing page header: the hamburger turns into a cross in place and the menu opens under the header.

One pattern for every landing page on a phone. Put `HeaderMenu` where the menu button goes, usually at the right end of the header. The header never moves: the button's lines fold into a cross in the same spot, and the menu grows down out of the header as a panel that fills the rest of the screen, its rows arriving one after another. Closing folds it back up. `footer` pins the page's main call to action to the panel's foot.

Following a link, Escape, or the button again closes it, and so does a window wide enough for the header's own links (`below`, default `"m"`). The panel keeps the look of the StyleScope the header sits in.

Header.tsx:

```tsx
"use client";

import { Button, HeaderMenu, Logo, MegaMenu, Row } from "@once-ui-system/core";

export function Header() {
  return (
    <Row as="header" position="sticky" top="0" zIndex={9} fillWidth padding="12" gap="8" vertical="center" background="page">
      <HeaderMenu footer={<Button fillWidth label="Sign up" href="/signup" />}>
        <MegaMenu collapseBelow="always" menuGroups={menu} />
      </HeaderMenu>
      <Logo href="/" icon="/trademarks/icon.svg" />
      <Row fillWidth m={{ hide: true }} horizontal="center">
        <MegaMenu menuGroups={menu} />
      </Row>
      <Button size="s" label="Sign up" href="/signup" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

## Behaviour

- **In place:** the menu button is the cross. A second button in the corner, or a header redrawn inside a drawer, makes the close control jump; this does not.
- **Under the header:** the panel starts at the bottom of the nearest `header` element and covers the page below it, with page scroll locked.
- **Keyboard:** opening moves focus to the first link, Tab off either end returns to the button, Escape closes and returns focus.
- **Controlled or not:** `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange`.

For a dashboard on a phone, use `Sidebar`: below `mobileBelow` it becomes a left drawer on its own.
