# HoverCard

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/hoverCard

> HoverCard displays content in a portal positioned relative to a trigger element on hover, with customizable animations and placement.

The `HoverCard` component is a syntactic sugar for the `Animation` component with a handful of smart defaults to display additional information about an element when hovered or focused.

> **Tooltip or HoverCard** [Tooltip](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tooltip) is a short text explanation on hover or focus: of its children, or of an info icon when it has none (2.x InfoTip), and the bubble a component's `tooltip` prop shows. [HoverCard](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/hoverCard) opens a card of rich content, such as a profile or a link preview, next to its trigger, following the pointer (2.x CursorCard) or over the trigger (2.x Hover).

```tsx
<HoverCard
    placement="top"
    trigger={<Avatar size="l" src="/images/avatar.jpg" tabIndex={0} />}
>
  <Column padding="20" gap="20" radius="l" maxWidth="24rem" background="page" border="neutral-alpha-medium">
    <Row gap="20" fillWidth vertical="center">
      <Avatar size="3rem" src="/images/avatar.jpg" />
      <Column gap="4">
        <Text textVariant="heading-strong-m">Lorant One</Text>
        <Text textVariant="body-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">
          Design Engineer
        </Text>
      </Column>
    </Row>
    <Text textVariant="body-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">
      Published 100k+ lines of open-source code. Author of The Dopler Method, The Design Dividend, and Learn anything.
    </Text>
    <Row gap="8" wrap>
      <Tag>Design</Tag>
      <Tag>Frontend</Tag>
      <Tag>Writing</Tag>
    </Row>
  </Column>
</HoverCard>
```

## Keyboard

The card opens when its trigger takes keyboard focus (not the focus a click gives, since the pointer already opened it by hovering), and closes on Escape or when focus leaves both the trigger and the card. While it is open, Tab moves from the trigger into the card's links and buttons, and on past them to what follows the trigger; Escape from inside the card returns focus to the trigger. A card with something to act on marks its trigger `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; a card of text describes the trigger while open (`aria-describedby`), unless the trigger already has a description. The trigger itself must be focusable: a button, a link, or an element with `tabIndex={0}`.

Keyboard:

```tsx
<HoverCard trigger={<Button type="button" variant="secondary" size="s" label="Lorant" />}>
  <Column padding="16" gap="8" radius="l" background="page" border="neutral-alpha-medium">
    <Text textVariant="label-default-s">Design engineer</Text>
    <SmartLink href="/profile">Profile</SmartLink>
  </Column>
</HoverCard>
```

## Cover

`placement="cover"` draws the card over the trigger itself, filling its box, while the pointer or focus is on it: an overlay of actions on a media tile. `delay` and `hideDelay` are milliseconds, `interactive` lets the card take pointer events, `disabled` turns it off, and `touch` decides what touch devices get. It was `Hover` in 2.x, which took the card as `overlay`.

```tsx
<HoverCard placement="cover"
    tabIndex={-1}
    trigger={
      <Card maxWidth="24rem" padding="8" direction="column" radius="l-8" href="#">
        <Media
          fillWidth
          aspectRatio="16 / 9"
          radius="l"
          alt="Example"
          src="/images/docs/once-ui/vibe-coding-light.jpg"
          sizes="480px"
        />
        <Column fillWidth padding="20" gap="8">
          <Text textVariant="heading-strong-m">Hover over me</Text>
          <Text onBackground="neutral-weak" textVariant="body-default-s">
            Move your cursor over this card to see the overlay effect.
          </Text>
        </Column>
      </Card>
    }><Tag position="absolute" top="24" right="24">
        New!
      </Tag></HoverCard>
```

### Delay

Add a delay before the overlay appears or disappears with the `delay` and `hideDelay` props.

```tsx
<HoverCard placement="cover"
    tabIndex={-1}
    delay={500}
    hideDelay={1000}
    trigger={
      <Card maxWidth="24rem" padding="8" direction="column" radius="l-8" href="#">
        <Media
          fillWidth
          aspectRatio="16 / 9"
          radius="l"
          alt="Example"
          src="/images/docs/once-ui/vibe-coding-light.jpg"
          sizes="480px"
        />
        <Column fillWidth padding="20" gap="8">
          <Text textVariant="heading-strong-m">Hover over me</Text>
          <Text onBackground="neutral-weak" textVariant="body-default-s">
            Move your cursor over this card to see the overlay effect.
          </Text>
        </Column>
      </Card>
    }><Row fill horizontal="center" padding="32">
        <Background top="0" left="0" position="absolute" gradient={{display: true, colorStart: "page-background", y: 0, width: "300%", height: "50%"}} radius="l-8"/>
        <Row textVariant="heading-strong-m">Read article</Row>
      </Row></HoverCard>
```

### Accessibility

The component supports keyboard navigation. For non-focusable triggers, add `tabIndex={0}` to make the wrapper keyboard-accessible. If your trigger is already focusable (like a Card with `href`), use `tabIndex={-1}` to prevent duplicate focus stops.

```tsx
<HoverCard placement="cover"
    trigger={
      <Card padding="l" direction="column" gap="12" maxWidth="24rem" center align="center" radius="l" tabIndex={0}>
        <Text textVariant="heading-strong-m">Keyboard accessible</Text>
        <Text onBackground="neutral-weak" textVariant="body-default-s">
          Tab to this card to see the overlay
        </Text>
      </Card>
    }><Column fill padding="l" gap="12" background="surface" border="neutral-medium" center align="center" radius="l">
        <Text textVariant="heading-strong-l">
          Focused!
        </Text>
        <Text onBackground="neutral-weak" textVariant="body-default-s">
          Showing an overlay
        </Text>
      </Column></HoverCard>
```

By default, the hover effect is disabled on touch devices. You can set `touch="enable"` to allow hover interactions, or `touch="display"` to always show the overlay on touch devices.

### Interactive

By default, the overlay is not interactive and click events are passed through to the trigger. You can set `interactive` to make the overlay interactive.

## Cursor

`placement="cursor"` makes the card follow the pointer while it is over the trigger, in a portal; `cursorPlacement` puts it on a side of the pointer (`"bottom-left"` by default). It was `CursorCard` in 2.x, which took the card as `overlay` and its side as `placement`.

CursorCard:

```tsx
<HoverCard placement="cursor"
    cursorPlacement="bottom-right"
    maxWidth="24rem"
    trigger={
      <Button weight="default" variant="secondary">
        See details
      </Button>
    }><Card maxWidth="24rem" radius="l-4" direction="column" border="neutral-alpha-medium">
        {children}
      </Card></HoverCard>
```

### Placement

The cursor placement supports different placement options to control how the overlay content is positioned relative to the cursor.

Placement:

```tsx
<HoverCard placement="cursor"
    cursorPlacement="top-left"
    trigger={
      <Button variant="secondary">
        Top left
      </Button>
    }><Row>
        Top left
      </Row></HoverCard>

  <HoverCard placement="cursor"
    cursorPlacement="top"
    trigger={
      <Button variant="secondary">
        Top
      </Button>
    }><Row>
        Top
      </Row></HoverCard>

  <HoverCard placement="cursor"
    cursorPlacement="bottom-right"
    trigger={
      <Button variant="secondary">
        Bottom right
      </Button>
    }><Row>
        Bottom right
      </Row></HoverCard>
```

### Accessibility Considerations

The cursor placement is designed for desktop use and automatically disables its functionality on touch devices. For touch devices, consider providing alternative ways to access the same information, such as expandable sections or dialogs.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `placement` | `Placement \| "cursor" \| "cover"` | `top` | A side to float beside the trigger, "cursor" to follow the pointer (2.x CursorCard) or "cover" to draw over the trigger (2.x Hover). |
| `cursorPlacement` | `CursorFollowerProps["placement"]` |  | With placement="cursor": the side of the pointer the card sits on. |
| `hideDelay` | `number` |  | With placement="cover": milliseconds before it hides. |
| `interactive` | `boolean` |  | With placement="cover": the card takes pointer events. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | With placement="cover": never show the card. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# IconButton

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/iconButton

> A button component that displays an icon with various styles, sizes, and interactive states.

The IconButton component provides a compact, icon-based interactive element for user actions. It's ideal for toolbar actions, navigation controls, and other UI elements where space is limited.

IconButton:

```tsx
<IconButton icon="check" variant="primary" />
<IconButton icon="plus" variant="secondary" />
<IconButton icon="chevronDown" variant="tertiary" />
<IconButton icon="danger" tone="danger" />
<IconButton icon="info" variant="ghost" />
<IconButton icon="sparkle" variant="ghost" />
<IconButton icon="settings" variant="subtle" />
<IconButton icon="check" tone="success" />
<IconButton icon="warning" tone="warning" />
<IconButton icon="link" variant="link" />
```

## Sizes

IconButtons come in different sizes to accommodate various use cases.

Sizes:

```tsx
<IconButton icon="chevronDown" size="s" />
<IconButton icon="chevronDown" size="m" />
<IconButton icon="chevronDown" size="l" />
```

## Tooltip

Add tooltips to provide context for icon buttons.

Tooltip:

```tsx
<IconButton variant="secondary" icon="check" type="button" tooltip="Confirm" tooltipPosition="left" />
<IconButton variant="secondary" icon="danger" type="button" tooltip="Delete" tooltipPosition="top" />
<IconButton variant="secondary" icon="info" type="button" tooltip="Information" tooltipPosition="bottom" />
<IconButton variant="secondary" icon="warning" type="button" tooltip="Warning" tooltipPosition="right" />
```

## Accessible name

An icon button has no text, so it needs a name for screen readers. It takes `aria-label`, or else a `tooltip` that is plain text, so the tooltips above already name their buttons. It is never named after its icon key. Without any of them it warns in development.

Accessible name:

```tsx
<IconButton icon="close" aria-label="Close dialog" />
<IconButton icon="search" aria-label="Search" />
<IconButton icon="copy" tooltip="Copy link" />
```

## Radius

Customize the border radius of the `IconButton` for different design needs.

Radius:

```tsx
<IconButton icon="chevronLeft" corners="top-left" />
<IconButton icon="chevronDown" corners="none" />
<IconButton icon="chevronRight" corners="bottom-right" />
```

## As link

IconButtons can function as links when provided with an `href` property.

Links:

```tsx
<IconButton icon="arrowUpRight" href="#" variant="secondary" aria-label="Open link" />
<IconButton icon="chevronRight" href="#" variant="tertiary" aria-label="Next" />
```

## Custom content

Use the children prop to add custom content to the IconButton.

Custom content:

```tsx
<IconButton>
    <Text textVariant="body-strong-s">A</Text>
</IconButton>
<IconButton variant="secondary">
    <Text textVariant="body-strong-s">B</Text>
</IconButton>
<IconButton variant="tertiary">
    <Text textVariant="body-strong-s">C</Text>
</IconButton>
```

# InfiniteScroll

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/infiniteScroll

> The InfiniteScroll component progressively loads content as the visitor scrolls.

The `InfiniteScroll` component provides an infinite scrollable container that progressively loads content as the visitor scrolls.

InfiniteScroll:

```tsx
import { useState, useCallback } from "react";
import { InfiniteScroll, Flex } from "@once-ui-system/core";

function InfiniteScrollExample() {
    const [items, setItems] = useState(Array(5).fill(null).map((_, i) => i));
    const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false);
    
    const loadMore = useCallback(async () => {
      setLoading(true);
      
      // Simulate API call
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1500));
      
      const lastItem = items[items.length - 1] || 0;
      const newItems = Array(5).fill(null).map((_, i) => lastItem + i + 1);
      
      setItems(prev => [...prev, ...newItems]);
      setLoading(false);
      
      // Return true if there are more items to load
      return items.length < 50;
    }, [items]);
    
    return (
      <InfiniteScroll
        items={items}
        loadMore={loadMore}
        loading={loading}
        threshold={200}
        renderItem={(item) => (
          <Flex key={item}/>
        )}
      />
    );
}
```

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items (required)` | `T[]` |  | What has been loaded so far. |
| `renderItem (required)` | `(item: T, index: number) => ReactNode` |  | How to render one. |
| `loadMore (required)` | `() => Promise<boolean>` |  | Fetch the next page. Resolve false when there is nothing left. |
| `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether a fetch is in flight. |
| `threshold` | `number` | `200` | How many pixels from the bottom to start loading. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Kbd

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/kbd

> A component for displaying keyboard keys and shortcuts with consistent styling.

The Kbd component is used to display keyboard keys and shortcuts with consistent styling. It's useful for showing keyboard interactions in documentation, tutorials, or application interfaces.

Kbd:

```tsx
<Kbd>Tab</Kbd>
<Kbd>Enter</Kbd>
<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>
<Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
```

## Shortcuts

Use multiple Kbd components together to display keyboard shortcuts.

Shortcuts:

```tsx
<Flex gap="8" vertical="center">
    <Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
    <Text>+</Text>
    <Kbd>C</Kbd>
    <Text>to copy</Text>
</Flex>
```

## Label

You can use either the `children` prop or the `label` prop to set the content of the Kbd component.

Label:

```tsx
<Kbd label="Space"/>
<Kbd>Enter</Kbd>
```

## Customization

Kbd keeps its keycap look and takes the leaf props: margins, `flex`,
`fillWidth`, `position` and the offsets. For a one-off colour or size, set
`style` (or `className`), which wins over the keycap's own classes.

Custom styling:

```tsx
<Kbd
  style={{
    background: "var(--brand-background-medium)",
    borderColor: "var(--brand-border-medium)",
    color: "var(--brand-on-background-weak)",
  }}
>
  Cmd
</Kbd>
<Kbd style={{ padding: "var(--static-space-4) var(--static-space-8)" }}>Space</Kbd>
```

## Shortcuts with keys

With `keys`, Kbd draws a whole shortcut as keycaps for the reader's platform, after the action `label` names (2.x's `KeyTip`). It takes the same string [`useHotkeys`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/hooks/useHotkeys) registers, so one constant drives both and the hint cannot drift from the binding. `mod` shows as ⌘ on macOS and iOS and as Ctrl everywhere else.

Shortcut:

```tsx
const SEARCH = "mod+k";

useHotkeys(SEARCH, () => setOpen(true));

<Kbd label="Search" keys={SEARCH} />
<Kbd label="Redo" keys="mod+shift+z" />
<Kbd label="Go to inbox" keys="g i" />
<Kbd label="Next" keys={["j", "down"]} />
```

A space separates the steps of a sequence, drawn with "then"; an array lists
alternatives, drawn with "or". The full syntax is on the
[`useHotkeys`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/hooks/useHotkeys) page.

### In a tooltip

A hover that names the action and its keys teaches the shortcut. Pass a Kbd with `keys` as a
tooltip's label:

Tooltip:

```tsx
<IconButton
  icon="arrowLeft"
  tooltip={<Kbd label="Undo" keys="mod+z" />}
  aria-label="Undo"
/>
```

### In a sentence

Kbd is inline, so it sits in a line of text.

Inline:

```tsx
<Text>
  Press <Kbd keys="shift+?" /> to see every shortcut.
</Text>
```

### Screen readers

Symbols such as ⌘ and ⇧ are read inconsistently, or not at all. The keycaps are
hidden from assistive technology, and a screen reader hears the combination spelled
out instead: "Undo, Command+Z" on a Mac, "Undo, Control+Z" elsewhere.

The page renders Ctrl on the server, where the platform is unknown, and switches to
⌘ right after it hydrates on Apple platforms, without a hydration warning.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `string \| readonly string[]` |  | A shortcut in useHotkeys syntax, drawn as caps; an array lists alternatives. |
| `label` | `string \| ReactNode` |  | The key as a string or, with keys, the action shown before them. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  | The key, when it needs markup. |
| `children` |  |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

---

# List

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/List

> Create an ordered or unordered list of items.

A component for creating an ordered or unordered list of items. The `List` component can be used to create nested lists and supports `Flex` props. The `ListItem` component can be used to create list items and supports `Text` props.

List:

```tsx
<List as="ol" textVariant="body-default-m" gap="4">
  <ListItem>
    Item 1
    <List as="ul" gap="4" paddingLeft="24" marginTop="4">
      <ListItem>Subitem 1</ListItem>
    </List>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>
    Item 2
    <List as="ul" gap="4" paddingLeft="24" marginTop="4">
      <ListItem>Subitem 1</ListItem>
      <ListItem>
        Subitem 2
        <List as="ul" gap="4" paddingLeft="24" marginTop="4">
          <ListItem textVariant="body-default-s">Subsubitem 1</ListItem>
          <ListItem textVariant="body-default-s">Subsubitem 2</ListItem>
          <ListItem textVariant="body-default-s">Subsubitem 3</ListItem>
        </List>
      </ListItem>
      <ListItem>Subitem 3</ListItem>
    </List>
  </ListItem>
  <ListItem>Item 3</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Item 4</ListItem>
</List>
```

## Starting number

A numbered list counts from 1. Pass `start` to count from another number, for example to continue a list that a paragraph interrupted. It applies to `as="ol"` only.

List:

```tsx
<List as="ol" start={4} gap="4">
  <ListItem>Item 4</ListItem>
  <ListItem>Item 5</ListItem>
</List>
```

# Logo

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/logo

> A component for displaying brand logos with consistent styling and sizing options.

The Logo component is used to display brand logos with consistent styling and sizing. It supports displaying both an icon and a wordmark, either separately or together.

Logo:

```tsx
<Logo
    icon={{ light: "/trademarks/icon-light.svg", dark: "/trademarks/icon-dark.svg" }}
    wordmark={{ light: "/trademarks/type-light.svg", dark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg" }}
    size="s"
    href="https://once-ui.com"
/>
```

## Sizes

The Logo component comes in different sizes to accommodate various use cases.

Sizes:

```tsx
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" size="xs" />
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" size="s" />
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" size="m" />
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" size="l" />
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" size="xl" />
```

## Icon

Display only the icon part of the logo.

Icon:

```tsx
<Logo icon="/trademarks/icon-dark.svg" size="s" />
<Logo icon="/trademarks/icon-dark.svg" size="l" />
```

## Wordmark

Display only the wordmark part of the logo.

Wordmark:

```tsx
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" size="s" />
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" size="l" />
```

## Text wordmark

For a brand with no wordmark file, `text` sets the name in the heading font at the logo's size,
after the icon if there is one. A link is then named by the text.

Text wordmark:

```tsx
<Logo icon="/trademarks/icon-dark.svg" text="Acme" size="s" />
<Logo text="Acme" size="l" />
```

## Monogram

For a brand with no designed icon yet, `monogram` draws a favicon-style mark at the icon's height:
a bare solid shape with no tile behind it, in the strongest text colour, so it is black in light mode
and white in dark mode. `monogram` picks one of a few geometric shapes from the name, so a product
always gets the same mark. A string draws those characters instead, as a heavy glyph. Beside `text`
the mark is decorative. When the real mark exists, pass it as `icon`: an icon always replaces the
monogram.

Monogram:

```tsx
<Logo text="Acme" monogram size="s" />
<Logo text="Holo Zone" monogram size="l" />
<Logo text="Acme" monogram="Ac" size="l" />
```

## As link

The Logo component can function as a link when provided with an `href` property.

Links:

```tsx
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" href="https://once-ui.com" />
<Logo wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg" href="https://once-ui.com" size="l" />
```

## Brand

The `brand` prop provides a `copy` option for allowing the icon and wordmark to be separately copied as an svg to the clipboard on right click through a context menu. The `url` option displays a link to your brand page when provided.

Brand:

```tsx
<Logo
    wordmark="/trademarks/type-dark.svg"
    brand={{
      copy: true,
      url: "https://once-ui.com/brand"
    }}
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `TShirtSizes` | `m` | Scale of whichever parts are shown. |
| `icon` | `LogoSource` |  | The mark. Takes one source, or { light, dark } for a per-theme pair. |
| `wordmark` | `LogoSource` |  | The wordmark. Same shape as icon. |
| `text` | `string` |  | A text wordmark, set in the heading font at the logo's size. |
| `monogram` | `boolean \| string` |  |  |
| `symbol` | `IconName` |  |  |
| `tone` | `Tone` |  |  |
| `href` | `string` |  | Makes it a link, usually home. |
| `showIn` | `"dark" \| "light"` |  | Render only in the dark or the light theme (2.x's dark and light). |
| `brand` | `{ copy?: boolean; url?: string }` |  | Turns the logo into a brand menu: copy the assets as SVG, and link to a brand page. |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...AnchorHTMLAttributes` |  |  | Also takes these props |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

```tsx
      { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "m" }
    ]}
    columns="2"
    gap="16"
    limit={4}
/>
```

## Rotation

When you have more logos than the limit allows, the LogoCloud will automatically rotate through them. If the limit equals the number of logos, rotation will be disabled.

Rotation:

```tsx
<LogoCloud 
    logos={[
      { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "m" },
      { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "m" },
      { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "m" },
      { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "m" },
      { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "m" },
      { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "m" }
    ]}
    limit={6}
    rotationInterval={3000}
    columns="3"
    gap="16"
/>
```

## Grid layout

The LogoCloud component extends the Grid component, so you can use all Grid props to customize the layout.

Grid layout:

```tsx
<LogoCloud 
    logos={[
        { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "s" },
        { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "s" },
        { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "s" },
        { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "s" },
        { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "s" },
        { wordmark: "/trademarks/type-dark.svg", size: "s" }
    ]}
    columns="4"
    s={{columns: 2}}
    gap="24"
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `logos (required)` | `LogoProps[]` |  | The marks to show. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `limit` | `number` | `6` | How many are visible at once. The rest rotate through. |
| `rotationInterval` | `number` | `ANIMATION_DURATION` | Milliseconds each set stays before the next rotates in. |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...GridProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# LogoLoader

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/logoLoader

> A page or app splash drawn from your own logo: each shape is traced, then the logo fills in and holds.

`LogoLoader` takes your product's wordmark or symbol as an SVG and plays it as a loading state: each letter and shape is traced in turn, then the logo fills in and stays. Use it for the splash while a page or app boots. `LogoSpinner` is the looping Once UI mark, and `Spinner` stays the neutral loader for buttons and fields.

From a file:

```tsx
<LogoLoader src="/trademarks/wordmark.svg" height={64} />
```

## Your logo

Pass the SVG as a URL (`src`, fetched on the client) or as markup (`svg`), for example a file a server component read, so the loader can draw on the first paint. The logo is drawn in one color, so one file covers both themes; `tone` picks it.

Every path, circle, rect, ellipse, polygon and line is drawn. A compound path splits into its parts, so each letter, and each counter inside one, gets its own stroke. Strokes draw left to right by default. With `order="document"` they keep the file's order instead, so a logo can list its symbol last to have it land after the letters. Groups' transforms, masks and gradients are not read: export the logo with flat, outlined paths.

Inline markup:

```tsx
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { LogoLoader } from "@once-ui-system/core";

// A server component reads the file once and hands the markup down.
export default async function Splash() {
  const wordmark = await readFile("public/trademarks/wordmark.svg", "utf8");
  return <LogoLoader svg={wordmark} height={120} tone="brand" />;
}
```

## Holding the splash

The intro plays once, and the filled logo holds for as long as the loader is on the page. `onComplete` fires when the intro has played; keep the splash up until both that and your data are ready, and pass `settled` so a remount never replays the strokes.

Splash:

```tsx
const [introDone, setIntroDone] = useState(false);
const showSplash = loading || !introDone;

{showSplash && (
  <Column fill center position="fixed" style={{ inset: 0, zIndex: 50 }}>
    <LogoLoader
      src="/trademarks/wordmark.svg"
      height={120}
      settled={introDone}
      onComplete={() => setIntroDone(true)}
    />
  </Column>
)}
```

## Accessibility

The loader is one `status` region named "Loading" unless you pass `aria-label`. With reduced motion the strokes are skipped and the logo fades in on the same schedule, so `onComplete` still fires.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `svg` | `string` |  | The logo as SVG markup. Wins over src. |
| `src` | `string` |  | URL of the logo's SVG file, fetched on the client. |
| `height` | `number \| string` | `120` | Height in px or any CSS length; the width follows the viewBox. |
| `tone` | `LogoLoaderTone` | `neutral` | brand, accent, neutral, or inherit for the text color. |
| `settled` | `boolean` | `false` | Show the filled logo without the intro. |
| `order` | `"reading" \| "document"` | `reading` | reading (left to right) or document (the file's order). |
| `onComplete` | `() => void` |  | Fires once the intro has played. |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |

# MascotPanel

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/mascotPanel

> MascotPanel is a character designer for the Mascot: body, eyes, face, accessories, how it works and how it moves, with a live preview and free exports.

`MascotPanel` lets people design their own [Mascot](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/modules/ai#mascot). It edits a `MascotDesign`, a plain JSON value your app stores (a database column, a URL, local storage) and spreads back onto `<Mascot />` with `mascotDesignProps`. It comes from `@once-ui-system/blocks`, next to StylePanel, and works the same way.

MascotPanel:

```tsx
import { MascotPanel } from "@once-ui-system/blocks";

const [design, setDesign] = useState<MascotDesign>({ v: 1 });

<MascotPanel value={design} onValueChange={(next) => setDesign(next)} />
```

## Storing a design

`MascotDesign` holds no React nodes or functions, so it fits a jsonb column as it is. Read every stored or AI-written design through `parseMascotDesign`: it never throws, drops what it does not know, clamps numbers to their range and only keeps colors and paths that look like colors and paths.

```tsx
import { Mascot, mascotDesignProps, parseMascotDesign } from "@once-ui-system/core";

const design = parseMascotDesign(agent.look);

<Mascot {...mascotDesignProps(design)} state="thinking" size="m" />
```

Without `value` the panel keeps its own state from `defaultValue`, and with `storageKey` it remembers it in the browser.

## What it edits

- **Body:** color (brand, accent, neutral or your own), roundness, width and surface.
- **Eyes:** shape, size, spacing, height and an optional color.
- **Face:** mouth, brows and cheeks.
- **Accessories:** the nine built-ins as tiles, several at once, and one optional color.
- **Working:** what it turns into while it thinks: nothing, the `cube` or the `d20`, with its sides and face.
- **Motion:** its personality.

The pickers for surface, eye shape, mouth, accessories, state and mood are one scrolling row of tiles, each showing your mascot with that option on, so people see what they pick. Arrow keys move between the tiles.

The preview tries every state and mood, kawaii ones included. That part is never saved.

`size="s"` makes it denser: tighter rows and groups, smaller tiles and a smaller preview, as on [StylePanel](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/stylePanel#size).

Size s:

```tsx
<MascotPanel size="s" />
```

## Exports

The preview's "more" menu, in its top right corner, holds Randomize, Reset and the free exports: Copy JSON, Copy JSX, and the flat mascot as an SVG or PNG file, drawn in the browser. Pass `exports` to add your own menu items after them; they read the design with `useMascotPanel()`.

```tsx
function GifItem() {
  const { value } = useMascotPanel();
  return <Option value="gif" label="Download GIF" onClick={() => makeGif(value)} />;
}

<MascotPanel exports={<GifItem />} />
```

## Compose your own

Like StylePanel, the panel is a plain composition of its parts. Use `MascotPanelRoot` with only the sections you need, and hide single rows with `rows`:

```tsx
<MascotPanelRoot value={design} onValueChange={setDesign} stacked>
  <MascotPanelPreview rows={{ mood: false }} />
  <MascotPanelBody rows={{ aspect: false }} />
  <MascotPanelAccessories />
</MascotPanelRoot>
```

`visibility` does the same on the whole panel, `preview` moves the preview (`side`, `top` or `none`), and `labels` translates every string it shows or announces.

# Mask

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/mask

> The Mask component provides a customizable radial mask effect.

The Mask component provides a customizable radial mask effect.

Mask:

```tsx
<Mask
    fill
    height="24rem"
    x="50%"
    y={0}
    radius="33vh">
    <Media fill src="/image.jpg" />
</Mask>
```

## Coordinates

Use the `x` and `y` props to position the mask. The coordinates are relative to the parent element.

Coordinates:

```tsx
<Mask
    fill
    height="24rem"
    x="50%"
    y={0}
    radius="33vh">
    <Media fill src="/image.jpg" />
</Mask>
```

## Radius

Use the `radius` prop to set the radius of the mask (defined in `vh` - viewport height).

Radius:

```tsx
<Mask
    fill
    height="24rem"
    x="35%"
    y="40%"
    radius="10vh">
    <Media fill src="/image.jpg" />
</Mask>
```

## Feather

Use the `feather` prop to set how much of the radius the edge fades over, from `0` (a sharp circle) to `100` (a soft fade from the centre, the default).

Feather:

```tsx
<Mask
    fill
    height={384}
    x="35%"
    y="40%"
    radius="16svh"
    feather={0}>
    <Media fill src="/image.jpg" />
</Mask>
```

## Cursor

Use the `cursor` prop to enable cursor tracking reveal.

Cursor:

```tsx
<Mask
    fill
    height="24rem"
    cursor>
    <Media fill src="/image.jpg" />
</Mask>
```

## Flex

The `Mask` component extends the `Flex` component, so you can use all the props of `Flex`.

Flex:

```tsx
<Mask
    fillWidth
    x="50%"
    y="50%"
    radius="20vh"
    borderBottom="neutral-medium"
/>
<Text onBackground="neutral-weak" textVariant="label-default-s" align="center">
    Fading lines
</Text>
<Mask
    fillWidth
    x="50%"
    y="50%"
    radius="20vh"
    borderBottom="neutral-medium"
/>
```

## Performance

When `cursor` is enabled, Mask automatically detects low-end devices and the `prefers-reduced-motion` system setting. When either is detected, cursor tracking is disabled and the mask remains at its initial position. The cursor effect also pauses when the element is outside the viewport. You can override this with the `reducedMotion` prop.

See [useReducedMotion](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/hooks/useReducedMotion) for details.

| `y` | `number \| CSSUnit` |  |  |
| `radius` | `number \| CSSUnit` | `50svh` |  |
| `feather` | `number` | `100` | How much of the radius the edge fades over, from 0 (a sharp circle) to 100 (soft from the centre). |
| `reducedMotion` | `boolean \| "auto"` | `auto` | Controls motion reduction for cursor tracking. Auto detects device capability and prefers-reduced-motion. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `style` | `React.CSSProperties` |  |  |
| `children` | `React.ReactNode` |  |  |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `children` |  |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Media players

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/mediaPlayers

> MediaAudioPlayer and MediaVideoPlayer — the two players behind Media, usable on their own.

[`Media`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/media) decides what to render by looking at the
file extension, and hands video off to a player. `MediaVideoPlayer` and
`MediaAudioPlayer` are those players, and you can reach for either directly.

You need them directly in two situations: when the source has **no usable
extension** — a `blob:` URL from `MediaRecorder`, a signed URL with the type in
a query string — so `Media` cannot sniff it; and when the media **is** the
component, as in an audio player that has no visual counterpart at all.

## Importing

Both live on the `@once-ui-system/core/media` subpath rather than the root
barrel, so they are not pulled into every bundle that imports something from
Once UI. They need no optional peer (only `MediaUpload` there uses `compressorjs`).

Import:

```tsx
import { MediaAudioPlayer, MediaVideoPlayer } from "@once-ui-system/core/media";
```

## MediaVideoPlayer

A video surface with play/pause, a scrubbable progress bar and elapsed time.
It is the right component for an extension-less source:

Recorder output:

```tsx
const [url, setUrl] = useState<string>();

// MediaRecorder output has no extension, so Media cannot sniff it.
recorder.ondataavailable = (event) => {
  setUrl(URL.createObjectURL(event.data));
};

{url && <MediaVideoPlayer src={url} objectFit="contain" />}
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src (required)` | `string` |  | Video source. Required. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `false` | Start playing as soon as the video can play. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Restart when playback reaches the end. |
| `muted` | `boolean` | `true` | Start muted. Autoplay is blocked with sound in most browsers. |
| `objectFit` | `CSSProperties["objectFit"]` | `cover` | How the frame fits its box. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## MediaAudioPlayer

Play/pause, a scrubbable progress bar and elapsed/total time, laid out as a
row rather than a surface. It takes every `Column` prop, so it sits in a layout
like any other block.

Audio player:

```tsx
<MediaAudioPlayer
  src="/audio/chapter-one.mp3"
  label="Chapter one"
  border
  radius="m"
  padding="12"
/>
```

### Synchronising with playback

`onTimeUpdate` fires on every `timeupdate` with the position in seconds. The
player owns playback; the caller owns what that position means — highlighting
the paragraph being narrated, advancing a transcript, moving a chapter marker.

Narration sync:

```tsx
const [time, setTime] = useState(0);
const current = chapters.findLast((chapter) => chapter.start <= time);

<MediaAudioPlayer src={audio} onTimeUpdate={setTime} />
<Text onBackground={current ? "neutral-strong" : "neutral-weak"}>
  {current?.title ?? "Not started"}
</Text>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src (required)` | `string` |  | Audio source. Required. |
| `autoplay` | `boolean` | `false` | Start playing as soon as the audio can play. |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | Restart when playback reaches the end. |
| `label` | `string` | `Audio player` | Accessible name for the player group. |
| `onTimeUpdate` | `(currentTime: number) => void` |  | Fires on every timeupdate with the position in seconds. |
| `onPlayingChange` | `(playing: boolean) => void` |  | Fires when playback starts or stops. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

# Nav, NavItem and NavGroup

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/nav

> The rows a product sidebar is made of, one setting for their look, and the route matcher that decides which one is current.

Every product built on Once UI grew its own sidebar, and they all converged on
the same two rows: a link that knows whether it is the current page, and a
collapsible group of those links indented behind a rail. These are those two.

They are rows, not a sidebar. Headers, footers, org switchers and storage meters
differ per product and stay yours to compose.

## A row

NavItem:

```tsx
<NavItem href="/projects" icon="home" label="Projects" selected />
<NavItem href="/presets" icon="sparkle" label="Presets" />
<NavItem href="/inbox" icon="inbox" label="Inbox" badge={42} />
<NavItem href="/activity" icon="bell" label="Activity" indicator />
<NavItem href="/reports" icon="barChart" label="Reports" badge="New" />
```

`badge` prints a count and caps it at `9+`; text such as `"New"` prints as given.
`indicator` is the dot for unread with no number worth showing.

## With an avatar

A link to a person, a team or a workspace can lead with its avatar. Pass it, or
any other node, as `prefix`: it sits where the icon would, and stays out of the
row's accessible name so the link reads as the label alone.

NavItem:

```tsx
<NavItem
  href="/people/ada"
  label="Ada Lovelace"
  prefix={<Avatar size="xs" src="/avatars/ada.png" />}
  badge={3}
  selected
/>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label (required)` | `ReactNode` |  | The text. |
| `icon` | `IconName` |  | Leading icon. Leave it off inside a NavGroup, where the rail carries the hierarchy instead. |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` |  | Any node before the label, such as an Avatar. Decorative: hidden from assistive tech, so the row is named by its label. |
| `badge` | `number \| ReactNode` |  | A pill at the end of the row. A number is a count: above 9 it prints 9+, with the real number on the label for assistive tech. Text such as "New" prints as given. |
| `indicator` | `boolean` |  | A dot at the end of the row, when there is no number worth showing. |
| `truncate` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

## A group

NavGroup:

```tsx
<NavGroup label="Settings" icon="settings" defaultOpen>
    <NavItem href="/settings/profile" label="Profile" selected />
    <NavItem href="/settings/billing" label="Billing" badge={2} />
    <NavItem href="/settings/members" label="Members" />
</NavGroup>
```

The rail is a vertical `Line`, not padding — indentation alone stops reading as
hierarchy the moment a label wraps. A group manages its own open state unless
you pass `open` and `onOpenChange`, which is what you do to open the group holding
the current route.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label (required)` | `ReactNode` |  | The group's own text. |
| `icon` | `IconName` |  | Leading icon, matching the NavItems beside it. |
| `children (required)` | `ReactNode` |  | The rows inside. |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Open state, when the host owns it — to keep one group open at a time, say. |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` | Starting state when the group manages its own. |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  | Called with the state the group moves to: true when it opens. |
| `selected` | `boolean` | `false` | Mark the header itself as current, for a group that is also a link. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

## One look for the whole sidebar

Wrap the rows in `Nav` and set the look once. Three props cover the sidebars
Once UI apps actually ship: how tight the rows are, how the current page stands
out, and whether groups draw their rail. Every row inside follows, and `NavSection`
gives each block its heading.

Dashboard:

```tsx
<Nav density="compact">
    <NavSection label="Home">
        <NavItem href="/" icon="home" label="Dashboard" selected />
        <NavItem href="/analytics" icon="analytics" label="Analytics" />
    </NavSection>
    <Line marginY="8" />
    <NavSection label="Projects" action={<IconButton icon="plus" size="s" variant="ghost" tooltip="Create" />}>
        <NavItem href="/projects" label="Overview" />
    </NavSection>
</Nav>
```

Docs:

```tsx
<Nav variant="subtle">
    <NavItem href="/start" icon="rocket" label="Get started" />
    <NavGroup label="Components" icon="grid" defaultOpen>
        <NavItem href="/button" label="Button" selected />
        <NavItem href="/input" label="Input" />
    </NavGroup>
</Nav>
```

Chat:

```tsx
<Nav density="compact" variant="minimal" rail={false}>
    <NavSection label="Pinned">
        <NavItem href="/c/1" icon="sparkle" label="Launch plan" selected />
    </NavSection>
    <NavSection label="Projects">
        <NavGroup label="Website" icon="project" defaultOpen>
            <NavItem href="/c/2" label="Hero copy" />
        </NavGroup>
    </NavSection>
</Nav>
```

- **`density`**: `compact` rows are 32px with the small label, the size for
  dashboards. `normal` is 40px, `spacious` 48px. Left out, a `Nav` takes the
  theme's `density` (`style.density` in your config), so a compact app gets a
  compact sidebar; set it to give one sidebar its own.
- **`variant`**: `solid` fills the current row. `subtle` fills it and dims the
  others, the docs look. `minimal` drops fills and marks the current row by
  weight and contrast; hover still tints.
- **`rail`**: the line down an open group. Off, the children keep the indent,
  so nothing shifts.

The rows work without a `Nav` too, at `normal`, `solid`, with the rail. An
explicit `size` on a NavItem still beats the nav's density. A line between
sections is just a `Line`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `density` | `NavDensity` |  | Row height and text size: compact (32px, small label), normal (40px) or spacious (48px). Defaults to the theme's density. |
| `variant` | `NavVariant` | `solid` | How the current page stands out: solid fills it, subtle fills it and dims the rest, minimal uses weight and contrast only. |
| `tone` | `Tone` | `neutral` |  |
| `rail` | `boolean` | `true` | The vertical line down an open NavGroup. Off, the indent stays. |
| `collapsed` | `boolean` | `false` | Icons only. Labels, badges and headings fade out but stay the rows' accessible names; a group opens its rows in a menu beside its icon. Inside a Sidebar it follows the Sidebar. |
| `expandOnHover` | `boolean` | `false` | With collapsed, open over the page on a resting mouse or keyboard focus, without moving the layout. |
| `expandedWidth` | `number \| SpacingToken` | `256` | How wide expandOnHover opens: rem, or a spacing token. 16 by default. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  | The heading over the rows. Leave it off for an untitled block. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | A control at the end of the heading, such as an add button. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

## An icon rail

An editor or a dense app often keeps only the icons. Set `collapsed` and the
`Nav` narrows to one icon column: labels, badges and section headings fade out,
groups close, and every row still answers to its label for a screen reader.

Add `expandOnHover` and the rail opens over the page, labels and all, while a
mouse rests on it or the keyboard is in it, instead of a tooltip per icon. It
keeps its collapsed width in the layout, so the panel beside it never moves.
Touch never opens it, Escape closes it, and reduced motion drops the animation.

Icon rail:

```tsx
<Row fill>
    <Nav aria-label="Editor" collapsed expandOnHover expandedWidth={12} padding="8" borderRight>
        <NavItem icon="pages" label="Pages" />
        <NavItem icon="grid" label="Layouts" selected />
        <NavItem icon="sparkle" label="Components" />
        <NavItem icon="settings" label="Settings" />
    </Nav>
    <Column fill>{panel}</Column>
</Row>
```

- The rail lifts above what follows it, so keep it out of an ancestor that
  clips overflow: a sidebar `Column` with `overflowY="auto"` cuts the open rail
  off at its edge.
- Give every row an `icon`. A collapsed row is its icon; one without shows as
  an empty pill.
- Without `expandOnHover`, `collapsed` is a static icon rail, for a host that
  toggles it from a button of its own.

## Which row is current

This is the part worth taking from here rather than writing again.

`pathname === href` misses a nested route: on `/settings/billing/invoices/42`
nothing is highlighted. `pathname.startsWith(href)` overshoots the other way:
`/settings` is a prefix of every child, so the parent lights up alongside them.
The answer is the **longest** href that matches.

selectNavHref:

```tsx
import { selectNavHref } from "@once-ui-system/core";

const items = [
    { href: "/settings", label: "General" },
    { href: "/settings/billing", label: "Billing" },
];

const current = selectNavHref(pathname, items.map((i) => i.href));

{items.map((item) => (
    <NavItem key={item.href} {...item} selected={item.href === current} />
))}
```

It returns `null` when nothing matches, and will not match a sibling that merely
shares a prefix — `/settings-v2` is not inside `/settings`.

## Related

- [ToggleButton](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/toggleButton) — what a NavItem is underneath
- [Accordion](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/accordion) — what a NavGroup is underneath
- [SplitView](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/splitView) — the other half of an app shell

# NavIcon

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/navIcon

> The menu button: the built-in menu icon, whose lines fold into a cross in place while its menu is open.

A simple yet effective component for creating hamburger menu icons that can toggle between active and inactive states. NavIcon is commonly used in responsive navigation interfaces to indicate the presence of a menu.

NavIcon:

```tsx
"use client";

import { NavIcon, Flex, Text, Row } from "@once-ui-system/core";
import { useState } from "react";

function NavIconToggle() {
    const [isActive, setIsActive] = useState(false);
    
    const handleClick = () => {
      setIsActive(!isActive);
    };

    return (
      <Column fillWidth>
        <Flex 
          paddingX="20" 
          paddingY="8" 
          background="surface"
          border="surface"
          radius="l" 
          horizontal="between" 
          vertical="center"
          fillWidth
        >
          <Logo icon="/trademarks/icon-dark.svg" />
          <NavIcon 
            active={isActive} 
            onClick={handleClick} 
            aria-label="Toggle navigation menu"
            aria-expanded={isActive}
            aria-controls="demo-nav"
          />
        </Flex>
        
        {isActive && (
          <Column 
            id="demo-nav"
            padding="16" 
            background="surface" 
            border="surface"
            radius="l" 
            marginTop="8"
            fillWidth
            gap="8"
          >
            <ToggleButton fillWidth horizontal="start" size="l">
              Home
            </ToggleButton>
            <ToggleButton fillWidth horizontal="start" size="l">
              Products
            </ToggleButton>
            <ToggleButton fillWidth horizontal="start" size="l">
              About
            </ToggleButton>
            <ToggleButton fillWidth horizontal="start" size="l">
              Contact
            </ToggleButton>
          </Column>
        )}
      </Column>
    );
}
```

## States

NavIcon has two states: `active` and `inactive`, controlled by the `active` prop.

States:

```tsx
<NavIcon active={false} />
<NavIcon active={true} />
```

## Customization

NavIcon keeps its 40px button look and takes the leaf props: margins, `flex`, `position` and the offsets. For another size or fill, set `style` (or `className`), which wins over its own classes.

Customization:

```tsx
<NavIcon
    active={isActive}
    onClick={handleClick}
    style={{
        width: 48,
        height: 48,
        padding: "var(--static-space-8)",
        borderRadius: "var(--radius-full)",
        background: "var(--neutral-background-strong)",
        border: "1px solid var(--neutral-alpha-medium)",
    }}
/>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `onClick` | `() => void` |  | Called on press. |
| `active` | `boolean` |  | Whether the menu is open. Drives which way the bars animate. |
| `className` |  |  |  |
| `style` |  |  |  |
| `...LeafProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

## Accessibility

The NavIcon component includes a `tabIndex={0}` by default, making it keyboard accessible. When implementing NavIcon in your application, consider the following accessibility best practices:

- Add an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` attribute to describe the purpose of the button
- Use `aria-expanded` to indicate the current state of the menu it controls
- Ensure the menu that is toggled by the NavIcon is properly accessible

Accessibility:

```tsx
<NavIcon 
    active={isMenuOpen} 
    onClick={toggleMenu}
    aria-label="Toggle navigation menu"
    aria-expanded={isMenuOpen}
    aria-controls="mobile-nav"
/>
```

# OgCard

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/ogCard

> A component that displays rich link previews with Open Graph metadata for URLs.

The `OgCard` component displays rich link previews for URLs by fetching and rendering Open Graph metadata. It's perfect for showcasing external links with preview images, titles, and descriptions.

```tsx
<OgCard 
    url="https://once-ui.com"
/>
```

## Mock data

Instead of fetching Open Graph data from a URL, you can directly provide the data to display.

Mock data:

```tsx
<OgCard 
    title="Design Engineers Club"
    description="The Design Engineers Club is a community of vibe coders."
    image="/images/docs/once-ui/vibe-coding-dark.jpg"
    favicon="/images/avatar.jpg"
    url="https://designengineers.club"
/>
```

## Direction

The OgCard component supports different layout directions.

Direction:

```tsx
<OgCard 
    url="https://once-ui.com/about"
    direction="row"
/>

<OgCard 
    url="https://once-ui.com/products"
    direction="row-reverse"
/>
```

## Size

The OgCard component supports different sizes.

Size:

```tsx
<OgCard 
    size="s"
    url="https://once-ui.com/about"
/>
<OgCard 
    size="m"
    url="https://once-ui.com/products"
/>
<OgCard 
    size="l"
    url="https://once-ui.com/customize"
/>
```

## Conditional rendering

You can hide each element of the `OgCard` component by setting its prop value to `false`.

```tsx
<OgCard 
    description={false}
    url="https://once-ui.com/about"
/>
```

## Custom style

The `OgCard` extends the `Card` component, so you can use all `Card` props to customize its appearance.

Custom style:

```tsx
<OgCard 
    url="https://once-ui.com/customize"
    direction="column"
    background="brand-alpha-weak"
    border="brand-alpha-medium"
    shadow="l"
/>
```

## Required API routes

To use `OgCard` with automatic Open Graph fetching, your application must expose two routes: one that fetches a page's metadata, and one that serves its image from your origin. In a Next.js app, both are ready-made in `@once-ui-system/core/next`, with SSRF protection built in:

app/api/og/fetch/route.ts:

```tsx
import { createOgFetchRoute } from "@once-ui-system/core/next";

export const { GET } = createOgFetchRoute();
```

app/api/og/proxy/route.ts:

```tsx
import { createOgProxyRoute } from "@once-ui-system/core/next";

export const { GET } = createOgProxyRoute();
```

See [OG route handlers](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/utils/ogRoutes) for their options. Outside Next.js, build the routes on [`handleOGFetch`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/utils/handleOGFetch) and [`handleOGProxy`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/utils/handleOGProxy).

`OgCard` calls `/api/og/fetch` and `/api/og/proxy` by default. If your routes live elsewhere, wrap the app in `OgRoutesProvider`:

Custom routes:

```tsx
<OgRoutesProvider routes={{ fetch: "/og/fetch", proxy: "/og/proxy" }}>
  {children}
</OgRoutesProvider>
```

The optional `/api/og/generate` route renders social images for `Meta.generate`; it is not needed by `OgCard`.

## Service configuration

Use `serviceConfig` to point a single `OgCard` at custom API routes (it takes precedence over `OgRoutesProvider`) or to transform proxied image and favicon URLs. Pass pre-fetched data with `ogData` to skip the fetch entirely.

Service configuration:

```tsx
<OgCard
  url="https://example.com"
  serviceConfig={{
    fetchOgUrl: '/api/og/fetch',
    proxyOgUrl: '/api/og/proxy',
    proxyImageUrl: (url) => `/api/og/proxy?url=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`,
    proxyFaviconUrl: (url) => `/api/og/proxy?url=${encodeURIComponent(url)}`,
  }}
/>

<OgCard
  ogData={{
    url: 'https://example.com',
    title: 'Example',
    description: 'Pre-fetched metadata',
    image: 'https://example.com/og.png',
    faviconUrl: 'https://example.com/favicon.ico',
  }}
/>
```

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` |  | The page to preview. Its Open Graph data is fetched and rendered. |
| `sizes` | `string \| number` | `320px` | The sizes attribute for the preview image. |
| `unoptimized` | `boolean` | `false` | Skip the framework image optimizer. |
| `size` | `CondensedTShirtSizes` | `m` | Card scale. |
| `ogData` | `Partial<OgData> \| null` |  | Supply the data yourself instead of fetching it. |
| `direction` | `"column" \| "row" \| "column-reverse" \| "row-reverse"` | `column` | Image above the text, or beside it. |
| `serviceConfig` | `OgServiceConfig` | `{}` | Where to fetch the Open Graph data from. |
| `title` | `string \| false` |  | Override the fetched title, or false to hide it. |
| `description` | `string \| false` |  | Override the fetched description, or false to hide it. |
| `favicon` | `string \| false` |  | Override the fetched favicon, or false to hide it. |
| `image` | `string \| false` |  | Override the fetched image, or false to hide it. |
| `cardUrl` | `string \| false` |  | Override the displayed link text, or false to hide it. |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

### OgServiceConfig

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fetchOgUrl` | `string` | `OgRoutesProvider's fetch, or '/api/og/fetch'` | Endpoint for fetching OG metadata. |
| `proxyOgUrl` | `string` | `OgRoutesProvider's proxy, or '/api/og/proxy'` | Endpoint for proxying external assets. |
| `proxyImageUrl` | `(url: string) => string` | `-` | Transform OG image URLs before rendering. |
| `proxyFaviconUrl` | `(url: string) => string` | `-` | Transform favicon URLs before rendering. |

## Notes

- The component automatically fetches favicons for the domain
- Images are proxied through an API endpoint to avoid CORS issues
- You can overwrite the default props by providing static values
- You can set any value to `false` to disable it

# Pagination

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/pagination

> Page through a long list: previous and next, the pages around the current one, and an ellipsis for the rest.

`Pagination` draws the controls for a list split into pages: previous and next
buttons, the first and last pages, the pages around the current one, and an
ellipsis for each run left out. It is a `nav` landmark named "Pagination" holding a
list of buttons, and the current page carries `aria-current="page"`.

Pagination:

```tsx
<Pagination total={12} defaultPage={5} />
```

Pass the number of pages as `total`, or the number of items as `count` with
`perPage`, and Pagination works the page count out. An empty list is page 1 of 1.

## Long ranges

The control keeps the same number of items wherever the current page is, so it does
not change width as the reader pages through. `boundaries` sets how many pages are
always drawn at each end, and `siblings` how many on each side of the current page.
Both default to 1. An ellipsis never stands for a single page: that page is drawn
instead.

Long ranges:

```tsx
<Pagination total={40} defaultPage={20} siblings={2} />
<Pagination total={40} defaultPage={20} boundaries={2} siblings={0} />
```

## First and last

`showFirstLast` adds buttons that jump to either end, for very long ranges where the
boundary pages are not enough.

First and last:

```tsx
<Pagination total={120} defaultPage={60} showFirstLast size="s" />
```

## Controlled, with a page size

Pass `page` and `onPageChange` when the host owns the page, as it does when the page
comes from the URL or a server request. `perPageOptions` adds a page-size select in
front of the pages; pair `perPage` with `onPerPageChange` to own that too. When the
size changes, the page moves so the first item on screen stays on screen, and
`onPageChange` reports the move.

Controlled:

```tsx
const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
const [perPage, setPerPage] = useState(20);

<Pagination
  page={page}
  onPageChange={setPage}
  count={248}
  perPage={perPage}
  perPageOptions={[10, 20, 50]}
  onPerPageChange={setPerPage}
  size="s"
/>
```

## Accessibility

- The landmark is named "Pagination". Give each one its own `aria-label` when a page
  has more than one, and to translate it. `labels` translates the arrow buttons and
  the per-page label.
- Every control is a real button, reached with Tab. When an arrow reaches the first
  or last page and disables itself, focus moves to the current page instead of
  dropping to the document.
- `disabled` turns every control off, such as while the next page loads.
- `Table` draws its page buttons with Pagination when it is `paginated`.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` | `number` |  | The current page, from 1, when the host owns it. Pair with onPageChange. |
| `defaultPage` | `number` | `1` | The page shown first when Pagination owns the state. |
| `onPageChange` | `(page: number) => void` |  | Called with the new page; not for the page already shown. |
| `total` | `number` |  | How many pages there are. |
| `count` | `number` |  | How many items there are. With perPage, gives the page count. |
| `perPage` | `number` |  | Items per page, when the host owns it. |
| `defaultPerPage` | `number` | `10` | Items per page when Pagination owns it. |
| `perPageOptions` | `number[]` |  | Page sizes to offer in a select. Without it there is no select. |
| `onPerPageChange` | `(perPage: number) => void` |  | Called with the new page size. |
| `siblings` | `number` | `1` | Pages drawn on each side of the current page. |
| `boundaries` | `number` | `1` | Pages always drawn at each end. |
| `showFirstLast` | `boolean` | `false` | Add first-page and last-page buttons. |
| `size` | `TShirtSizes` | `m` | The buttons' size. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disable every control. |
| `labels` | `Partial<PaginationLabels>` |  | The arrow buttons' names and the per-page label, to translate them. |
| `aria-label` | `string` |  |  |
| `...CommonProps, ...DisplayProps, ...FlexProps, ...SizeProps, ...SpacingProps, ...StyleProps` |  |  | Also takes these props |

### PaginationLabels

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `previous` | `string` | `"Previous page"` | The previous-page button's name. |
| `next` | `string` | `"Next page"` | The next-page button's name. |
| `first` | `string` | `"First page"` | The first-page button's name. |
| `last` | `string` | `"Last page"` | The last-page button's name. |
| `perPage` | `string` | `"Per page"` | The per-page select's label. |

# PeerCursor

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/peerCursor

> Collaborators' pointers for multiplayer views: an arrow in each person's colour with their name, gliding between the positions your realtime layer sends.

PeerCursor draws what other people are pointing at: an arrow in their colour, a label with their name, and, if they type one, a short message. It has no backend. Feed `PeerCursors` the positions from whatever carries them (Supabase Realtime, Liveblocks, a WebSocket) and send your own with `usePeerPointer`.

Positions from the network arrive 20 to 30 times a second. Each cursor glides to the latest one by writing `transform` every frame, without a React render, so a full room costs nothing between updates. Under reduced motion they jump.

Live:

```tsx
const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
const { peers, move } = usePresence("doc-42"); // your realtime layer

// Send your pointer, throttled to 25 a second; null when it leaves.
usePeerPointer(ref, move);

<Column ref={ref} fillWidth height={320} style={{ position: "relative" }}>
  {/* the shared surface */}
  <PeerCursors peers={peers} />
</Column>
```

## Positions

`PeerCursors` fills its positioned parent and reads `x` and `y` as a fraction of it by default (`units="fraction"`), so people on screens of different widths point at the same spot of a fluid layout. Use `units="px"` for a fixed-size surface. `usePeerPointer` reports in the same units.

On a canvas that pans and zooms, there are two ways:

- Put `PeerCursors` inside the world layer, with `units="px"` in world coordinates and `scale={1 / zoom}` so the cursors keep their size. Panning moves them with the layer for free.
- Put it in a screen overlay and pass `project` (world to screen), with `unproject` (screen to world) on `usePeerPointer`.

World layer:

```tsx
<div style={{ transform: `translate(${pan.x}px, ${pan.y}px) scale(${zoom})` }}>
  {/* items */}
  <PeerCursors units="px" scale={1 / zoom} peers={peers} />
</div>
```

## Colour, label and message

Each person keeps the same hue on every screen: left out, `scheme` comes from `peerColor(id)`, a hash of the id over the palette. Light hues take dark text.

- `message`: a live line of text in a bubble under the pointer (cursor chat).
- `avatar`: a small picture before the name.
- `idle`: set it when someone has not moved for a while; the label folds away and only the arrow stays.

Looks:

```tsx
<PeerCursor id="mira" name="Mira Holt" x={40} y={30} />
<PeerCursor id="teo" name="Teo Varga" x={240} y={24} scheme="cyan" message="This heading could be bigger" />
<PeerCursor id="ines" name="Ines Ferro" x={480} y={40} scheme="violet" idle />
```

## Accessibility

Cursors are decorative and hidden from screen readers. Say who is here in a way that reads, such as an `AvatarGroup` of the people in the room.

## API

### PeerCursors

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `peers` | `PeerCursorData[]` | | Everyone else's pointer: `{ id, name, x, y, scheme?, message?, avatar?, idle? }`. |
| `units` | `"fraction" \| "px"` | `"fraction"` | What `x` and `y` mean. |
| `project` | `(x, y) => { x, y }` | | Maps a position to px in the layer, after `units`. |
| `scale` | `number` | | Cursor scale about the tip; also `--peer-cursor-scale`. |
| `smooth` | `boolean` | `true` | Glide between positions. |

### PeerCursor

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | | The label. |
| `x`, `y` | `number` | | Px from the top left of the positioned parent. |
| `id` | `string` | | Picks the default colour. |
| `scheme` | `Schemes` | `peerColor(id)` | The hue. |
| `message` | `string` | | A bubble under the pointer. |
| `avatar` | `string` | | A picture before the name. |
| `idle` | `boolean` | `false` | Folds the label away. |
| `smooth` | `boolean` | `true` | Glide between positions. |

### usePeerPointer(ref, onMove, options)

Calls `onMove({ x, y })` as the pointer moves over `ref`'s element, at most once per `interval` ms (default 40) with the last move always sent, and `onMove(null)` when it leaves. Options: `interval`, `units`, `unproject`, `disabled`. Touch is left out.

# PhotoViewer

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/photoViewer

> A full-screen viewer for a set of photos: swipe between them, pinch to zoom, and close back into the tile it opened from.

`PhotoViewer` shows a set of photos full screen, the way a phone's photo app does. A photo
grows out of the tile it opened from and shrinks back into it on close. Swipe or use the
arrows to move between photos, with a little resistance at either end; swipe down to close;
pinch, double-tap or double-click to zoom and drag to pan. Escape closes it and focus goes
back to the tile. Under reduced motion every animation becomes a short fade.

It is a modal dialog on the same overlay core as [`Dialog`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dialog) and
[`Drawer`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/drawer): the page behind it is inert and does not scroll, and Tab
stays inside. Render it while it is open and unmount it in `onClose`. For a single image,
`Media enlarge` is still the lighter choice; `Media` never loads the viewer.

Gallery:

```tsx
const [open, setOpen] = useState<number | null>(null);
const gridRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);

<Grid ref={gridRef} columns={3} gap="8">
  {photos.map((photo, index) => (
    <Media
      key={photo.src}
      src={photo.src}
      alt={photo.alt}
      aspectRatio="1 / 1"
      role="button"
      tabIndex={0}
      aria-label={`View ${photo.alt}`}
      data-photo-index={index}
      onClick={() => setOpen(index)}
    />
  ))}
</Grid>
{open !== null && (
  <PhotoViewer
    items={photos}
    defaultIndex={open}
    getOrigin={(i) => gridRef.current?.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`[data-photo-index="${i}"]`) ?? null}
    onClose={() => setOpen(null)}
  />
)}
```

## Items

Each item is `{ src, alt }`, plus an optional `title` shown above the counter and a
`caption` shown after it ("3 / 12 · 2024"). Give `width` and `height` when you know them, so
the photo opens at its real proportions; without them the viewer measures each photo as it
loads. Images render through the Image adapter, like `Media`, so a Next.js app gets
`next/image` and `unoptimized` skips it.

## Which photo

`index`, `defaultIndex` and `onIndexChange` follow the usual pattern: leave `index` out and
the viewer keeps its own, starting at `defaultIndex`, or control it to keep your page in step
(scrolling the grid along, for example).

## Deep links

Pass `deepLink="photo"` to keep the open photo in the URL (`?photo=<file name>`), so a photo
can be shared, and so Back closes the viewer. To open on a shared photo when the page loads,
read the URL with `photoViewerIndexFromUrl`:

Deep link:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  const index = photoViewerIndexFromUrl(photos, "photo");
  if (index >= 0) setOpen(index);
}, []);

{open !== null && (
  <PhotoViewer items={photos} defaultIndex={open} deepLink="photo" onClose={() => setOpen(null)} />
)}
```

Without `deepLink` the viewer leaves the URL and history alone.

## Closing

`getOrigin(index)` returns the element a photo opens from and closes into, usually its tile.
Focus goes back to it on close. If the tile has scrolled off screen, the viewer fades out where
it is; set `scrollToOrigin` to scroll the page to the tile instead, which suits a gallery page.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items (required)` | `PhotoViewerItem[]` |  | The photos, in order: { src, alt, title?, caption?, width?, height? }. |
| `index` | `number` |  | The photo on screen, controlled. |
| `defaultIndex` | `number` | `0` | The first photo of an uncontrolled viewer. |
| `onIndexChange` | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called with the photo the viewer moves to. |
| `onClose (required)` | `(index: number) => void` |  | Called with the photo it closed on, once the closing animation has finished. Unmount the viewer here. |
| `getOrigin` | `(index: number) => HTMLElement \| null` |  | The element photo `index` opens from and closes into. Focus returns to it. |
| `scrollToOrigin` | `boolean` | `false` | On close, scroll the page so the tile is in view instead of fading out. |
| `deepLink` | `string` |  | Keep the open photo in this search parameter; Back closes the viewer. |
| `unoptimized` | `boolean` |  | Skip the framework's image optimization. |
| `labels` | `PhotoViewerLabels` |  | The viewer's own words (dialog, close, previous, next, counter, error, retry), for a translated interface. |

# ProgressBar

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/progressBar

> The ProgressBar component shows the progress of an action or task with an animation as it progresses.

A component for showing the progress of an action or task with an animation as it progresses.

ProgressBar:

```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<number>(0);
  
useEffect(() => {
    let currentValue = 0;
    const interval = setInterval(() => {
      currentValue += 1;
      setValue(currentValue);
      
      if (currentValue >= 100) {
        clearInterval(interval);
      }
    }, 50);
    
    return () => clearInterval(interval);
}, []);
  
return (
    <ProgressBar value={value} />
);
```

# Schematic

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/schematic

> A process schematic from data: vessels, pumps, valves, exchangers and the lines that show what flows where.

`Schematic` draws parts and the lines between them from two lists, so a plant,
a network or a pipeline is data, not a drawing. Dashes run along a line in the
direction of its `flow` as dots in the brand colour, at its speed, with an arrow that shows the direction
even when motion is reduced. A pump turns while it runs.

Parts are outlined in the neutral scale and only take a tone when something is
wrong. A part's state reads without colour: `warning` has a dashed outline,
`alarm` a heavy one, `off` is dashed and struck through, and each writes its
state under the part. Parts fill with the page colour; on a panel, set
`--schematic-background` on an ancestor to the panel's colour, such as
`var(--surface-background)`. A screen reader hears every part with its reading and state, and
then the flows.

Schematic:

```tsx
<Schematic
  aria-label="Primary loop"
  nodes={[
    { id: "core", kind: "vessel", x: 80, y: 130, label: "Reactor", value: "312 °C" },
    { id: "pump", kind: "pump", x: 280, y: 180, label: "Pump B", running: false, state: "alarm" },
    // …
  ]}
  links={[
    { from: "core", to: "sg", via: [[80, 40], [280, 40]], flow: 1.2, label: "Hot leg" },
    // …
  ]}
  onNodeSelect={setSelected}
  selected={selected}
/>
```

## Parts

`vessel`, `tank`, `pump`, `valve`, `exchanger`, `turbine`, `sensor` (an
instrument bubble with its `tag`) and `box`. Positions are in the drawing's own
units; the `viewBox` is fitted to the parts unless you give one.

## Selecting

With `onNodeSelect`, every part is a button (Enter or Space presses it), and
`selected` draws a ring round one.

## Phones

Below `minWidth` (560 px by default) the drawing scrolls sideways instead of
shrinking its text out of reach.

## API reference

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `nodes (required)` | `readonly SchematicNode[]` | `[]` |  |
| `links` | `readonly SchematicLink[]` | `[]` |  |
| `viewBox` | `[number, number, number, number]` |  |  |
| `selected` | `string` |  |  |
| `onNodeSelect` | `(id: string) => void` |  |  |
| `minWidth` | `number` | `560` |  |
| `aria-label (required)` | `string` |  |  |
| `labels` | `Partial<SchematicLabels>` |  |  |
