# Text (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/text

> Body text for React Native screens, set from the same typography and colour tokens as the web.

`Text` renders a React Native `Text` with a Once UI type style and colour. Set the style with one `textVariant`, such as `"body-default-m"`; `family` and `weight` swap its family and weight. Without any of them it is `body-default-m` in `neutral-strong`. See the [web Text page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/text) for the full set of variants.

## Variants

A variant is `family-weight-size`. The families are `body`, `heading`, `display`, `label` and `code`.

Variants.tsx:

```tsx
import { Column, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Variants() {
  return (
    <Column gap="8">
      <Text textVariant="display-strong-s">Display</Text>
      <Text textVariant="heading-strong-m">Heading</Text>
      <Text textVariant="body-default-m">Body text</Text>
      <Text textVariant="label-default-s">Label</Text>
      <Text textVariant="code-default-s">npm install</Text>
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Parts.tsx:

```tsx
import { Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Parts() {
  return (
    <Text textVariant="body-default-s" family="label" weight="strong">
      Strong small label
    </Text>
  );
}
```

Colors.tsx:

```tsx
import { Column, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Colors() {
  return (
    <Column gap="8">
      <Text onBackground="neutral-weak">Secondary text</Text>
      <Text onBackground="brand-medium">Brand text</Text>
      <Column padding="12" background="brand-strong" radius="m">
        <Text onSolid="brand-strong">Text on a solid surface</Text>
      </Column>
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Caption.tsx:

```tsx
import { Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Caption() {
  return (
    <>
      <Text align="center" marginBottom="8">
        Centered
      </Text>
      <Text truncate>A long product name that does not fit on one line of a phone screen</Text>
      <Text numberOfLines={2}>A description that may run to two lines, then stops.</Text>
    </>
  );
}
```

# Heading (React Native)

> A title for React Native screens and sections, announced to screen readers as a header.

`Heading` is [Text](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/text) set to `heading-strong-l`, with `accessibilityRole="header"` so screen readers announce it as a header and let people jump between headings.       <Heading textVariant="heading-default-s">Small, default weight</Heading>
```tsx
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Section.tsx:

```tsx
import { Column, Heading, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Section() {
```

# Icon (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/icon

> Once UI's built-in icons drawn with react-native-svg, plus IconProvider for adding icons of your own by name.

`Icon` draws one icon by name. The native package ships the same icon data as the web package and draws it with `react-native-svg`, so the names match and no icon font or extra icon library is needed. `react-native-svg` 15 is a peer dependency, and Expo includes it. See the [web Icon page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/icon).

## Sizes and colours

`size` takes `xs` to `xl`: 16, 20, 24, 32 or 40 points. `m` is the default. The colour is `neutral-strong` unless you set `onBackground` or `onSolid`.

Icons.tsx:

```tsx
import { Icon, Row } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Icons() {
  return (
    <Row gap="16" vertical="center">
      <Icon name="heart" size="xs" />
      <Icon name="heart" size="m" onBackground="danger-medium" />
      <Icon name="heart" size="xl" onBackground="brand-strong" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Status.tsx:

```tsx
import { Icon, Row, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Status() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8" vertical="center">
      <Icon name="check" size="s" onBackground="success-medium" decorative={false} aria-label="Paid" />
      <Text>Invoice 1042</Text>
    </Row>
  );
}
```

App.tsx:

```tsx
import Ionicons from "@expo/vector-icons/Ionicons";
import { Button, Column, Icon, IconProvider } from "@once-ui-system/native";

declare module "@once-ui-system/native" {
  interface IconLibraryOverrides {
    rocket: true;
  }
}

const icons = {
  rocket: ({ size, color }: { size: number; color: string }) => (
    <Ionicons name="rocket-outline" size={size} color={color} />
  ),
};

export default function App() {
  return (
    <IconProvider icons={icons}>
      <Column gap="12">
        <Icon name="rocket" />
        <Button prefixIcon="rocket" label="Launch" onPress={() => {}} />
      </Column>
    </IconProvider>
  );
}
```

# Media (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/media

> An image in a clipped box at a set aspect ratio, with a skeleton until it loads.

`Media` shows an image from a URL in a box with rounded corners and a set aspect ratio. A skeleton fills the box until the image loads. It extends Flex props, so radius, border, margin and sizes work as on any `Flex`. See the [web Media page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/media) for the web version.

Media:

```tsx
import { Media } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Cover() {
  return (
    <Media
      src="https://example.com/cover.jpg"
      alt="A cup of coffee on a wooden table"
      aspectRatio="16 / 9"
      radius="l"
      border="neutral-alpha-weak"
    />
  );
}
```

Loading and caption:

```tsx
import { Column, Media } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Gallery({ src }: { src?: string }) {
  return (
    <Column gap="16">
      <Media src={src ?? ""} loading={!src} aspectRatio="1" radius="m" />
      <Media
        src="https://example.com/shop.jpg"
        alt="The shop front"
        aspectRatio="4 / 3"
        radius="m"
        caption="Our shop on Main Street"
      />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Pressable:

```tsx
import { Media } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Thumbnail({ onOpen }: { onOpen: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Media
      src="https://example.com/photo.jpg"
      alt="Open the photo"
      aspectRatio="1"
      radius="m"
      maxWidth="8rem"
      onPress={onOpen}
    />
  );
}
```

Stretch:

```tsx
import { Column, Media } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Banner() {
  return (
    <Column height="12rem" fillWidth radius="l" overflow="hidden">
      <Media src="https://example.com/banner.jpg" alt="" stretch objectFit="cover" />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

# Dialog (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/dialog

> A modal task shown as a bottom sheet, with a title, description and footer, for React Native.

`Dialog` takes the same main props as on the web (`open`, `onClose`, `title`, `description`, `footer`) and opens as a bottom sheet, the shape phones use for a modal task. It slides up from the bottom edge, shows a grabber, and scrolls its content when it is taller than the screen allows. See the [web Dialog](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dialog) for the same component in the browser.

## Basic usage

The dialog is always controlled: keep `open` in state and close it in `onClose`. The close button, the Android back button and a tap on the backdrop all call `onClose`.

ShareSheet.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button, Dialog, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function ShareSheet() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button label="Share" onPress={() => setOpen(true)} />
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        title="Share list"
        description="People you invite can edit this list."
      >
        <Text>Invite someone by email.</Text>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

DeleteSheet.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button, Dialog, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function DeleteSheet() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button label="Delete" tone="danger" onPress={() => setOpen(true)} />
      <Dialog
        open={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        title="Delete list?"
        footer={
          <>
            <Button label="Cancel" variant="secondary" onPress={() => setOpen(false)} />
            <Button label="Delete" tone="danger" onPress={() => setOpen(false)} />
          </>
        }
      >
        <Text>This removes the list for everyone.</Text>
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

SortSheet.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button, Dialog, Option } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function SortSheet() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button label="Sort" variant="tertiary" onPress={() => setOpen(true)} />
      <Dialog open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Sort by" flush closeOnClickaway={false}>
        <Option value="newest" label="Newest first" onPress={() => setOpen(false)} />
        <Option value="oldest" label="Oldest first" onPress={() => setOpen(false)} />
      </Dialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

# IconButton (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/iconButton

> A square React Native button that holds one icon, with the same variants and sizes as Button.

`IconButton` is a square `Pressable` that shows one icon. It takes the same `variant` values as [Button](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/button) and handles taps with `onPress`. See the [web IconButton page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/iconButton) for more on when to use it.

## Accessible name

An icon alone tells a screen reader nothing, so give every `IconButton` an `aria-label`. Without one, and without children, it logs a warning.

Toolbar.tsx:

```tsx
import { IconButton, Row } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Toolbar() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8">
      <IconButton icon="search" variant="secondary" aria-label="Search" onPress={() => {}} />
      <IconButton icon="settings" variant="tertiary" aria-label="Settings" onPress={() => {}} />
      <IconButton icon="trash" tone="danger" aria-label="Delete" onPress={() => {}} />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Sizes.tsx:

```tsx
import { IconButton, Row } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8" vertical="center">
      <IconButton size="s" icon="plus" aria-label="Add" onPress={() => {}} />
      <IconButton size="m" icon="plus" aria-label="Add" onPress={() => {}} />
      <IconButton size="l" icon="plus" rounded aria-label="Add" onPress={() => {}} />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Custom.tsx:

```tsx
import { Icon, IconButton, Row, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Custom() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8">
      <IconButton variant="ghost" aria-label="Like" onPress={() => {}}>
        <Icon name="heart" onBackground="danger-medium" />
      </IconButton>
      <IconButton variant="secondary" aria-label="Three items" onPress={() => {}}>
        <Text textVariant="label-strong-s">3</Text>
      </IconButton>
    </Row>
  );
}
```

# ToggleButton (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/toggleButton

> A quiet React Native button that stays highlighted while it is selected, for filters, toolbars and segmented choices.

`ToggleButton` is a quiet `Pressable` with a label and optional icons. While `selected` is true it keeps a highlighted background. It does not hold its own state: keep `selected` in your component and flip it in `onPress`. See the [web ToggleButton page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/toggleButton) for more examples.

## Selected state

Filters.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Row, ToggleButton } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Filters() {
  const [filter, setFilter] = useState("all");
  return (
    <Row gap="4">
      <ToggleButton label="All" selected={filter === "all"} onPress={() => setFilter("all")} />
      <ToggleButton
        label="Unread"
        selected={filter === "unread"}
        onPress={() => setFilter("unread")}
      />
      <ToggleButton
        label="Starred"
        prefixIcon="star"
        selected={filter === "starred"}
        onPress={() => setFilter("starred")}
      />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Variants.tsx:

```tsx
import { Row, ToggleButton } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Variants() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8">
      <ToggleButton variant="ghost" label="Ghost" selected onPress={() => {}} />
      <ToggleButton variant="outline" label="Outline" onPress={() => {}} />
      <ToggleButton variant="subtle" label="Subtle" selected onPress={() => {}} />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Menu.tsx:

```tsx
import { Column, ToggleButton } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Menu() {
  return (
    <Column gap="4" fillWidth>
      <ToggleButton size="l" rounded label="Rounded" onPress={() => {}} />
      <ToggleButton
        size="l"
        fillWidth
        horizontal="between"
        label="Notifications"
        suffixIcon="chevronRight"
        onPress={() => {}}
      />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

# Line (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/line

> A 1 point divider for React Native layouts, horizontal or vertical.

`Line` draws a 1 point divider in `neutral-alpha-medium`. It is horizontal and fills its parent's width by default. See the [web Line page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/line).

## Horizontal

Section.tsx:

```tsx
import { Column, Line, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Section() {
  return (
    <Column gap="12" fillWidth>
      <Text>Account</Text>
      <Line />
      <Text>Notifications</Text>
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Stats.tsx:

```tsx
import { Line, Row, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Stats() {
  return (
    <Row gap="16" height="40" vertical="center">
      <Text>7 stamps</Text>
      <Line vert />
      <Text>2 rewards</Text>
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Divider.tsx:

```tsx
import { Column, Line, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Divider() {
  return (
    <Column fillWidth>
      <Text>Above</Text>
      <Line background="brand-alpha-strong" style={{ marginVertical: 16 }} />
      <Text>Below</Text>
    </Column>
  );
}
```

# Avatar (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/avatar

> A circular profile picture, or initials when there is no image.

`Avatar` shows a person's picture in a circle. Without `src`, it shows the initials from `value` on a neutral background. Screen readers read it as one image, labelled by `value`. See the [web Avatar page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/avatar) for the web version.

Avatar:

```tsx
import { Avatar, Row } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function People() {
  return (
    <Row gap="12" vertical="center">
      <Avatar src="https://example.com/ada.jpg" value="Ada" />
      <Avatar value="LT" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Sizes:

```tsx
import { Avatar, Row } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Row gap="12" vertical="center">
      <Avatar size="xs" value="XS" />
      <Avatar size="s" value="S" />
      <Avatar size="m" value="M" />
      <Avatar size="l" value="L" />
      <Avatar size={4} value="4" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Status and loading:

```tsx
import { Avatar, Row } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Presence() {
  return (
    <Row gap="12" vertical="center">
      <Avatar size="l" value="AB" statusIndicator={{ scheme: "green" }} />
      <Avatar size="l" value="CD" statusIndicator={{ scheme: "gray" }} />
      <Avatar size="l" loading />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Rings:

```tsx
import { Avatar, Row } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Rings() {
  return (
    <Row gap="12" vertical="center">
      <Avatar size="l" value="AB" ring />
      <Avatar size="l" value="CD" ring="success" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

# AvatarGroup (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/avatarGroup

> A row of overlapping avatars, with the rest collapsed into a count.

`AvatarGroup` lays out a list of [avatars](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/avatar) in a row, each one overlapping the one before it by the `8` spacing step. Each entry in `avatars` takes the same props as `Avatar`. It extends Flex props, so spacing and alignment work as on any `Flex`. See the [web AvatarGroup page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/avatarGroup) for the web version.

AvatarGroup:

```tsx
import { AvatarGroup } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Team() {
  return (
    <AvatarGroup
      avatars={[
        { src: "https://example.com/ada.jpg", value: "Ada" },
        { value: "BK" },
        { value: "CM" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

Sizes:

```tsx
import { AvatarGroup, Column } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const avatars = [{ value: "AB" }, { value: "CD" }, { value: "EF" }];

export function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Column gap="16">
      <AvatarGroup size="s" avatars={avatars} />
      <AvatarGroup size="m" avatars={avatars} />
      <AvatarGroup size="l" avatars={avatars} />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Limit and reverse:

```tsx
import { AvatarGroup } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const avatars = [
  { value: "AB" },
  { value: "CD" },
  { value: "EF" },
  { value: "GH" },
  { value: "IJ" },
];

export function Attendees() {
  return <AvatarGroup avatars={avatars} limit={3} reverse />;
}
```

# Badge (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/badge

> Badge is Tag in Once UI 3.0, on React Native as on the web: an announcement is <Tag variant="announce">.

`Badge` folded into [Tag](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/tag) in Once UI 3.0, as it did on the [web](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/badge), and `@once-ui-system/native` no longer exports it. Its look is `<Tag variant="announce">`, with `arrow` and `href` as before; `title` is `label` and `icon` is `prefixIcon`.

Announcement.tsx:

```tsx
import { Tag } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Announcement() {
  return <Tag variant="announce" label="New release" prefixIcon="rocket" arrow onPress={() => {}} />;
}
```

---

# Tag (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/tag

> A small label on a weak tint of its color scheme.

`Tag` is a static label for a status, a category or a piece of metadata. It stays on one line. For something that announces or links, use `variant="announce"`; with `selected`, `onPress` or `onRemove` it is a toggle (2.x Chip). See the [web Tag page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tag) for the web version.

Tag:

```tsx
import { Tag } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Status() {
  return <Tag label="In stock" tone="success" />;
}
```

Schemes and sizes:

```tsx
import { Row, Tag } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Labels() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8" wrap vertical="center">
      <Tag size="s" label="Draft" />
      <Tag size="m" label="Brand" tone="brand" />
      <Tag size="l" label="Overdue" tone="danger" />
      <Tag label="Pending" tone="warning" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Icons:

```tsx
import { Row, Tag } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Meta() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8">
      <Tag label="Today" prefixIcon="calendar" tone="info" />
      <Tag label="Favourite" suffixIcon="star" tone="brand" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

# Feedback (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/feedback

> An inline alert with a title and description, tinted by its variant.

`Feedback` shows a message inside the layout: an error under a form, a warning above a list, a note after a save. It fills the width and takes the color of its `tone`. Screen readers announce it as an alert when it appears. See the [web Feedback page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/feedback) for the web version.

Feedback:

```tsx
import { Feedback } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Saved() {
  return (
    <Feedback
      tone="success"
      title="Card saved"
      description="Your stamps are synced to this device."
    />
  );
}
```

Icon:

```tsx
import { Feedback, Icon } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Offline() {
  return (
    <Feedback
      tone="warning"
      icon={<Icon name="warning" onBackground="warning-medium" />}
      title="You are offline"
      description="Changes will sync when you reconnect."
    />
  );
}
```

Close button:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Feedback } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Notice() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(true);
  if (!open) return null;
  return (
    <Feedback
      tone="info"
      title="New rewards"
      description="Every tenth coffee is now free."
      showCloseButton
      onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
    />
  );
}
```

Custom content:

```tsx
import { Button, Feedback } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function PaymentFailed({ onRetry }: { onRetry: () => void }) {
  return (
    <Feedback tone="danger" title="Payment failed" description="Your card was declined.">
      <Button variant="secondary" size="s" label="Try again" onPress={onRetry} />
    </Feedback>
  );
}
```

# List (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/List

> A bulleted or numbered list of ListItem rows.

`List` is a column of `ListItem` rows with a bullet before each one, or a number when `as="ol"`. React Native has no list markers, so `List` counts its items and `ListItem` draws the marker itself, right-aligned in the same `20` step indent the web uses. See the [web List page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/List) for the web version.

List:

```tsx
import { List, ListItem } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Perks() {
  return (
    <List gap="4">
      <ListItem>A free coffee every ten stamps</ListItem>
      <ListItem>Early access to new blends</ListItem>
      <ListItem>A birthday treat</ListItem>
    </List>
  );
}
```

Numbered list:

```tsx
import { List, ListItem } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Steps() {
  return (
    <List as="ol" start={3} gap="4">
      <ListItem>Scan the code at the till</ListItem>
      <ListItem>Collect your stamp</ListItem>
      <ListItem>Show the card for your free coffee</ListItem>
    </List>
  );
}
```

Rich items:

```tsx
import { List, ListItem, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Menu() {
  return (
    <List gap="8">
      <ListItem textVariant="body-default-s" onBackground="neutral-weak">
        <Text textVariant="body-strong-s">Espresso.</Text> A short, strong shot.
      </ListItem>
      <ListItem>
        <Text>Milk drinks</Text>
        <List>
          <ListItem>Flat white</ListItem>
          <ListItem>Cappuccino</ListItem>
        </List>
      </ListItem>
    </List>
  );
}
```

# Skeleton (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/skeleton

> A pulsing placeholder that holds the space of content while it loads.

`Skeleton` is a grey shape that pulses while content loads. It comes as a line, a circle or a block. The pulse holds still when the device's reduce motion setting is on. Screen readers read it as "Loading". See the [web Skeleton page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/skeleton) for the web version.

Skeleton:

```tsx
import { Column, Row, Skeleton } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function ProfileLoading() {
  return (
    <Row gap="12" vertical="center">
      <Skeleton shape="circle" size="l" />
      <Column flex={1} gap="8">
        <Skeleton shape="line" size="m" width="60%" />
        <Skeleton shape="line" size="s" />
      </Column>
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Shape and size:

```tsx
import { Column, Skeleton } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Shapes() {
  return (
    <Column gap="12">
      <Skeleton shape="line" size="xs" />
      <Skeleton shape="line" size="xl" width={192} />
      <Skeleton shape="circle" size="m" />
      <Skeleton shape="block" height={128} fillWidth />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Delay:

```tsx
import { Column, Skeleton } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Staggered() {
  return (
    <Column gap="8">
      <Skeleton shape="line" delay={0} />
      <Skeleton shape="line" delay={150} />
      <Skeleton shape="line" delay={300} />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

# Spinner (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/spinner

> A loading indicator drawn by the platform's own activity indicator.

`Spinner` shows that something is loading when you cannot show its shape. For content with a known layout, a [Skeleton](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/skeleton) usually reads better. See the [web Spinner page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/spinner) for the web version.

Spinner:

```tsx
import { Row, Spinner, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Syncing() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8" vertical="center">
      <Spinner size="s" />
      <Text onBackground="neutral-weak">Syncing your card</Text>
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Sizes:

```tsx
import { Row, Spinner } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Row gap="16" vertical="center">
      <Spinner size="xs" />
      <Spinner size="s" />
      <Spinner size="m" />
      <Spinner size="l" />
      <Spinner size="xl" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Color and label:

```tsx
import { Spinner, useTheme } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Uploading() {
  const theme = useTheme();
  return <Spinner color={theme.color("brand-solid-strong")} aria-label="Uploading photo" />;
}
```

# StatusIndicator (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/statusIndicator

> A small colored dot that shows a status.

`StatusIndicator` is a round dot in the 700 step of a color scheme, such as `green` for online or `red` for an error. It extends Flex props, so margin and positioning work as on any `Flex`. See the [web StatusIndicator page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/statusIndicator) for the web version.

StatusIndicator:

```tsx
import { Row, StatusIndicator, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Online() {
  return (
    <Row gap="8" vertical="center">
      <StatusIndicator scheme="green" aria-label="Online" />
      <Text>Online</Text>
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Sizes:

```tsx
import { Row, StatusIndicator } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Sizes() {
  return (
    <Row gap="12" vertical="center">
      <StatusIndicator size="s" scheme="blue" />
      <StatusIndicator size="m" scheme="blue" />
      <StatusIndicator size="l" scheme="blue" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Colors:

```tsx
import { Row, StatusIndicator } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Colors() {
  return (
    <Row gap="12" vertical="center">
      <StatusIndicator scheme="green" />
      <StatusIndicator scheme="yellow" />
      <StatusIndicator scheme="red" />
      <StatusIndicator scheme="violet" />
      <StatusIndicator scheme="gray" />
    </Row>
  );
}
```

# ProgressBar (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/progressBar

> A rounded track that fills to a value, with the value as a label.

`ProgressBar` shows how far along something is. The bar fills to `value` between `min` and `max`, and animates over one second when the value changes. Screen readers read it as a progress bar with its value. See the [web ProgressBar page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/progressBar) for the web version.

ProgressBar:

```tsx
import { ProgressBar } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Upload() {
  return <ProgressBar value={64} />;
}
```

Label:

```tsx
import { Column, ProgressBar } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Labels() {
  return (
    <Column gap="24">
      <ProgressBar value={30} labelPosition="top" />
      <ProgressBar value={50} labelPosition="right" />
      <ProgressBar value={70} showLabel={false} />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Range and color:

```tsx
import { Column, ProgressBar, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Stamps({ stamps }: { stamps: number }) {
  return (
    <Column gap="8">
      <Text textVariant="label-default-s">{stamps} of 10 stamps</Text>
      <ProgressBar value={stamps} max={10} showLabel={false} barBackground="success-medium" />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

# Tabs (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/tabs

> A list of tabs and the panel each one shows, horizontal or vertical, for React Native.

`Tabs` holds one `TabList` of `Tab`s and a `TabPanel` for each tab, matched by `value`. Each `Tab` is a [ToggleButton](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/toggleButton) with the tab role, so it takes every ToggleButton prop. The first enabled tab is selected unless you pick one. See the [web Tabs](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/tabs) for the same component in the browser.

## Uncontrolled

Pass `defaultValue` to choose the first tab, or leave it out to start on the first enabled one.

OrderTabs.tsx:

```tsx
import { Tab, TabList, TabPanel, Tabs, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function OrderTabs() {
  return (
    <Tabs defaultValue="active">
      <TabList aria-label="Orders">
        <Tab value="active" label="Active" />
        <Tab value="past" label="Past" />
        <Tab value="drafts" label="Drafts" disabled />
      </TabList>
      <TabPanel value="active">
        <Text>Two orders on the way.</Text>
      </TabPanel>
      <TabPanel value="past">
        <Text>Nothing here yet.</Text>
      </TabPanel>
      <TabPanel value="drafts">
        <Text>No drafts.</Text>
      </TabPanel>
    </Tabs>
  );
}
```

ProfileTabs.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Tab, TabList, TabPanel, Tabs, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function ProfileTabs() {

      <TabPanel value="posts">
        <Text>Your posts</Text>
      </TabPanel>
      <TabPanel value="likes">
        <Text>Posts you liked</Text>

}
```

# Accordion (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/accordion

> A header that shows and hides the content under it, with a short animation, for React Native.

`Accordion` is a header that opens and closes the content under it. The content's height eases open and the icon turns. Closed content stays mounted, so it keeps its state. See the [web Accordion](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/accordion) for the same component in the browser.

## Uncontrolled

The accordion keeps its own state. `defaultOpen` (or `open` without a handler) sets the first state.

Faq.tsx:

```tsx
import { Accordion, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Faq() {
  return (
    <Accordion title="How do refunds work?" defaultOpen>
      <Text onBackground="neutral-weak">Refunds reach your card within five working days.</Text>
    </Accordion>
  );
}
```

Details.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Accordion, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Details() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <Accordion title="Order details" open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} size="l">
      <Text>Two items, shipped to Berlin.</Text>
    </Accordion>
  );
}
```

Help.tsx:

```tsx
import { useRef } from "react";
import { Accordion, type AccordionHandle, Button, Column, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Help() {
  const accordion = useRef<AccordionHandle>(null);
  return (
    <Column gap="12">
      <Button label="Show help" variant="secondary" onPress={() => accordion.current?.open()} />
      <Accordion ref={accordion} title="Help">
        <Text>Tap a card to see its details.</Text>
      </Accordion>
    </Column>
  );
}
```

# Toast (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/toast

> Short messages that stack at the bottom of the screen and hide themselves, for React Native.

A toast is a short message on a surface card that hides itself after six seconds. Wrap the app in `ToastProvider`, then call `addToast({ tone, message })` from `useToast` anywhere under it, as on the web. See the [web Toast](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/toast) for the same component in the browser.

## Setup

Put `ToastProvider` inside `ThemeProvider`, around the rest of the app. It draws the toasts above everything in it, stacked at the bottom of the screen with the newest last.

App.tsx:

```tsx
import { Column, Text, ThemeProvider, ToastProvider } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <ThemeProvider>
      <ToastProvider>
        <Column fill background="page" padding="20">
          <Text>Your app</Text>
        </Column>
      </ToastProvider>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

SaveButton.tsx:

```tsx
import { Button, useToast } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function SaveButton() {
  const { addToast } = useToast();
  return (
    <Button
      label="Save"
      onPress={() => addToast({ tone: "success", message: "Changes saved" })}
    />
  );
}
```

ArchiveButton.tsx:

```tsx
import { Button, useToast } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function ArchiveButton() {
  const { addToast } = useToast();
  return (
    <Button
      label="Archive"
      variant="secondary"
      onPress={() =>
        addToast({
          tone: "info",
          message: "Conversation archived",
          action: <Button size="s" variant="tertiary" label="Undo" onPress={() => {}} />,
          duration: 10000,
        })
      }
    />
  );
}
```

OfflineNotice.tsx:

```tsx
import { Toast } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function OfflineNotice() {
  return (
    <Toast tone="warning" duration={Infinity} showIcon>
      You are offline. Changes will sync later.
    </Toast>
  );
}
```

# SegmentedControl (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/segmentedControl

> A row of buttons where one is selected, for React Native.

`SegmentedControl` picks one value out of a few, shown as a row of buttons in a frame. Each button takes a `label` and optional icons. It fills the width by default. See the [web SegmentedControl](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/segmentedControl) for the same component in the browser.

## Uncontrolled

Without `value`, the control keeps its own state. It starts on `defaultValue`, or on the first button. `onValueChange` is required.

```tsx
        { value: "grid", label: "Grid" },
        { value: "map", label: "Map", disabled: true },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

Period.tsx:

```tsx
      />

    </>
  );
}
```


# Option (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/option

> One row of a list to pick from, used by Select and in your own menus, for React Native.

`Option` is one row of a list to pick from, at least 44pt tall. [Select](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/form-controls/select) draws its options with it, and you can use it in your own menus, such as a list in a [Dialog](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/dialog). A selected option is highlighted and shows a check. See the [web Option](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/option) for the same component in the browser.

## Basic usage

`onPress` is called with the option's `value`. `label` falls back to the `value`.

SizeList.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Column, Option } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function SizeList() {

    <Column gap="4">
      <Option value="s" label="Small" selected={size === "s"} onPress={setSize} />
      <Option value="m" label="Medium" selected={size === "m"} onPress={setSize} />
      <Option value="l" label="Large" selected={size === "l"} onPress={setSize} />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

PlanList.tsx:

```tsx
import { Column, Icon, Option, Tag } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function PlanList() {

        label="Pro"
        description="Unlimited projects"

        suffix={<Tag label="Popular" />}
        onPress={() => {}}
      />
      <Option value="free" label="Free" description="Three projects" onPress={() => {}} />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

ItemMenu.tsx:

```tsx

    </Column>
  );
}
```

# DropdownWrapper (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/dropdownWrapper

> A trigger that opens a menu anchored under it, flipping above when there is no room, for React Native.

`DropdownWrapper` opens a menu next to its trigger. It measures the trigger on screen and draws the menu in a transparent modal over everything else, under the trigger by default. If there is no room below, the menu opens above. Pressing outside the menu or the back button closes it. The menu is a `Dropdown`, the bordered surface, and its items are usually [Option](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/option)s. See the [web DropdownWrapper page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/dropdownWrapper) for the web version.

## Basic usage

Pass the trigger and the menu's content. The wrapper keeps its own open state. Pressing an `Option` calls `onSelect` with its value and closes the menu.

FileActions.tsx:

```tsx
import { Button, DropdownWrapper, Option } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function FileActions({ onAction }: { onAction: (action: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <DropdownWrapper
      trigger={<Button variant="secondary" label="Actions" suffixIcon="chevronDown" />}
      onSelect={onAction}
      dropdown={
        <>
          <Option value="rename" label="Rename" />
          <Option value="duplicate" label="Duplicate" />
          <Option value="delete" label="Delete" danger />
        </>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

SortMenu.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button, DropdownWrapper, Option } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const options = [
  { value: "name", label: "Name" },
  { value: "date", label: "Date modified" },
  { value: "size", label: "Size" },
];

export function SortMenu() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [sort, setSort] = useState("name");
  return (
    <DropdownWrapper
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={setOpen}
      selectedOption={sort}
      onSelect={setSort}
      trigger={
        <Button
          variant="secondary"
          suffixIcon="chevronDown"
          label={options.find((o) => o.value === sort)?.label}
        />
      }
      dropdown={options.map((o) => (
        <Option key={o.value} value={o.value} label={o.label} />
      ))}
    />
  );
}
```

FilterMenu.tsx:

```tsx
import { Button, DropdownWrapper, Option } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function FilterMenu({ onToggle }: { onToggle: (value: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <DropdownWrapper
      placement="bottom-end"
      minWidth="14rem"
      closeAfterClick={false}
      onSelect={onToggle}
      trigger={<Button variant="tertiary" label="Filter" prefixIcon="filter" />}
      dropdown={
        <>
          <Option value="unread" label="Unread" />
          <Option value="starred" label="Starred" />
        </>
      }
    />
  );
}
```

# ContextMenu (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/contextMenu

> A menu that opens where the user long-presses, the phone's right-click, for React Native.

`ContextMenu` opens a menu when the user long-presses its children. The menu opens at the press point, with its top-left corner under the finger by default. Near an edge of the screen it opens on the other side of the point. It uses the same menu as [DropdownWrapper](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/dropdownWrapper): pressing outside it or the back button closes it. See the [web ContextMenu page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/contextMenu) for the web version.

## Basic usage

Wrap the element and pass the menu's content, usually [Option](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/option)s. Pressing an option calls `onSelect` with its value and closes the menu.

FileRow.tsx:

```tsx
import { Card, ContextMenu, Option, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function FileRow({ onAction }: { onAction: (action: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <ContextMenu
      onSelect={onAction}
      dropdown={
        <>
          <Option value="share" label="Share" />
          <Option value="rename" label="Rename" />
          <Option value="delete" label="Delete" danger />
        </>
      }
    >
      <Card padding="16" radius="l">
        <Text>Invoice-0042.pdf</Text>
      </Card>
    </ContextMenu>
  );
}
```

OpenButton.tsx:

```tsx
import { Button, ContextMenu, Option } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function OpenButton({ onOpen }: { onOpen: () => void }) {
  return (
    <ContextMenu
      placement="top-start"
      dropdown={
        <>
          <Option value="new-tab" label="Open in new tab" />
          <Option value="copy" label="Copy link" />
        </>
      }
    >
      <Button label="Open" onPress={onOpen} />
    </ContextMenu>
  );
}
```

Message.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { ContextMenu, Option, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Message({ locked }: { locked: boolean }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <ContextMenu
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={setOpen}
      disabled={locked}
      dropdown={<Option value="reply" label="Reply" />}
    >
      <Text>See you at 6.</Text>
    </ContextMenu>
  );
}
```

# CodeBlock (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/codeBlock

> Code snippets with tabs, a copy button, line numbers and syntax colours, for React Native.

`CodeBlock` shows one or more snippets of code in a surface with a header. Pass them in `codes`, each with `code`, `language` and `label`. With several snippets the header becomes a row of tabs. The code is set in the code font and scrolls sideways instead of wrapping. A small built-in tokenizer colours keywords, strings, comments and numbers for `js`, `jsx`, `ts`, `tsx`, `css`, `bash` and `json`, with the same `--code-*` colours as the web. Other languages show as plain text. See the [web CodeBlock page](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/modules/codeBlock) for the web version.

CodeBlock:

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Install() {
  return (
    <CodeBlock
      codes={[{ code: "pnpm add @once-ui-system/native", language: "bash", label: "Terminal" }]}
    />
  );
}
```

Tabs:

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const codes = [
  { code: "export const size = 16;", language: "ts", label: "size.ts" },
  { code: ".title { font-size: 16px; }", language: "css", label: "title.css" },
  { code: '{ "size": 16 }', language: "json", label: "size.json" },
];

export function Snippets() {
  return <CodeBlock codes={codes} onInstanceChange={(index) => console.log(index)} />;
}
```

onCopy:

```tsx
import * as Clipboard from "expo-clipboard";
import { CodeBlock } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Copyable() {
  return (
    <CodeBlock
      onCopy={(code) => Clipboard.setStringAsync(code)}
      codes={[{ code: "npx expo start", language: "bash", label: "Start" }]}
    />
  );
}
```

Line numbers:

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const code = ["function greet(name: string) {", "  return 'Hi ' + name;", "}"].join("\n");

export function Numbered() {
  return (
    <CodeBlock
      lineNumbers
      codes={[{ code, language: "ts", label: "greet.ts", startLineNumber: 12, highlight: "13" }]}
    />
  );
}
```

Preview:

```tsx
import { Button, CodeBlock } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Example({ code }: { code: string }) {
  return (
    <CodeBlock
      reloadButton
      isCollapsible
      maxLines={4}
      preview={<Button label="Order" />}
      codes={[{ code, language: "tsx", label: "Order.tsx" }]}
    />
  );
}
```

Diff:

```tsx
import { CodeBlock } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const diff = ["@@ -1 +1 @@", "-let total = 0;", "+const total = 0;"].join("\n");

export function Change() {
  return <CodeBlock lineNumbers codes={[{ code: diff, language: ["diff", "ts"], label: "total.ts" }]} />;
}
```

# Grid (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/grid

> Children in equal columns that reflow per breakpoint or by a minimum column width, for React Native.

`Grid` lays its children out in `columns` equal columns, `gap` apart in both directions. Like [Flex](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/flex) it takes spacing, size and surface props and the `xl` to `xs` breakpoint objects, so the column count can change with the screen width. See the [web Grid](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/grid) for the browser version.

## Columns and gap

Each child sits in a cell `1 / columns` of the width. Cells in a row are as tall as the tallest one; give a child `flex={1}` to fill its cell's height.

Menu.tsx:

```tsx
import { Card, Grid, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Menu() {
  return (
    <Grid columns={2} gap="12" padding="16">
      {["Espresso", "Flat white", "Cortado", "Mocha"].map((drink) => (
        <Card key={drink} padding="16" flex={1}>
          <Text textVariant="label-default-m">{drink}</Text>
        </Card>
      ))}
    </Grid>
  );
}
```

Gallery.tsx:

```tsx
import { Grid, Media } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Gallery({ photos }: { photos: string[] }) {
  return (
    <Grid columns={4} gap="8" s={{ columns: 2 }} xs={{ columns: 1 }}>
      {photos.map((src) => (
        <Media key={src} src={src} aspectRatio="1 / 1" radius="l" />
      ))}
    </Grid>
  );
}
```

AutoFit:

```tsx
import { Grid, Tag } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Origins() {
  return (
    <Grid minColumnWidth="8rem" gap="8" xs={{ columns: 2 }}>
      <Tag label="Ethiopia" />
      <Tag label="Colombia" />
      <Tag label="Kenya" />
      <Tag label="Brazil" />
    </Grid>
  );
}
```

# InfoTip (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/infoTip

> An info icon that shows a sentence of context when it is pressed, for React Native.

`InfoTip` is the "what is this?" icon. A tap opens a short explanation beside the icon, kept on screen, and a tap anywhere closes it. It lets a setting explain itself without spending a line on a description. Screen readers hear the explanation as the icon's hint. See the [web InfoTip](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/infoTip) for the browser version.

## Basic usage

Put it beside the text it explains. `size` matches the icon to that text.

Setting.tsx:

```tsx
import { InfoTip, Row, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function RoundUp() {
  return (
    <Row gap="4" vertical="center">
      <Text textVariant="label-default-m">Round up for charity</Text>
      <InfoTip size="s">We round your total to the next euro and donate the difference.</InfoTip>
    </Row>
  );
}
```

Translated:

```tsx
import { InfoTip } from "@once-ui-system/native";
```

# Breadcrumbs (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/breadcrumbs

> A trail of links to where the current screen sits, collapsible when long, for React Native.

`Breadcrumbs` shows where the current screen sits, as a trail from the root. The last item is the current screen, drawn stronger and not pressable. A long trail wraps onto more lines, or collapses with `maxItems`. See the [web Breadcrumbs](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/breadcrumbs) for the browser version.

## Basic usage

There is no URL routing on a phone, so `onNavigate` gets a crumb's `href` and hands it to your router. A crumb can also have its own `onPress`.

Trail.tsx:

```tsx
import { Breadcrumbs } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Trail({ navigate }: { navigate: (href: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <Breadcrumbs
      onNavigate={navigate}
      items={[
        { label: "Home", href: "/", prefixIcon: "home" },
        { label: "Beans", href: "/beans" },
        { label: "Ethiopia Guji" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

Collapsed:

```tsx
import { Breadcrumbs } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Deep({ navigate }: { navigate: (href: string) => void }) {
  return (
    <Breadcrumbs
      maxItems={3}
      onNavigate={navigate}
      items={[
        { label: "Home", href: "/" },
        { label: "Shop", href: "/shop" },
        { label: "Coffee", href: "/shop/coffee" },
        { label: "Beans", href: "/shop/coffee/beans" },
        { label: "Ethiopia" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

# Pagination (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/pagination

> Page through a long list with previous and next, page numbers and an optional page size, for React Native.

`Pagination` pages through a long list: previous and next buttons, the first and last pages, the pages around the current one, and an ellipsis for the rest. The number of buttons stays the same wherever you are, so the row keeps its width. Pass `total` pages, or `count` items and `perPage`. See the [web Pagination](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/pagination) for the browser version.

## Basic usage

Without `page`, Pagination keeps its own state, starting at `defaultPage`.

Orders.tsx:

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Orders({ onPage }: { onPage: (page: number) => void }) {
  return <Pagination total={12} onPageChange={onPage} />;
}
```

Products.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Pagination } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Products({ count }: { count: number }) {
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1);
  const [perPage, setPerPage] = useState(10);
  return (
    <Pagination
      count={count}
      page={page}
      onPageChange={setPage}
      perPage={perPage}
      onPerPageChange={setPerPage}
      perPageOptions={[10, 25, 50]}
      size="s"
      siblings={0}
    />
  );
}
```

# Timeline (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/timeline

> Steps joined by a line, each with a dot coloured by its state, for React Native.

`Timeline` shows a sequence of steps, such as an order's progress. Each step has a dot coloured by its `state`, a label, a description and any children. `marker` draws inside the dot, such as a step number. Screen readers hear a list, with the `active` step selected.

```tsx
        { label: "Ready for pickup", marker: "3" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

Layouts:

```tsx
import { Timeline } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const steps = [
  { label: "Cart", state: "success" as const },

  { label: "Done" },
];

export function Layouts() {

      <Timeline alignment="right" items={steps} />

  );
```

# Scroller (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/scroller

> A scrolling row or column with Flex layout, pull to refresh and safe-area padding, for React Native.

`Scroller` is a `ScrollView` that takes the [Flex](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/flex) props. Layout props such as `gap`, `padding`, `vertical` and `safeArea` lay out the content, while size props such as `flex`, `height` and margins size the scroller itself. It scrolls sideways by default, as the [web Scroller](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/scroller) does. Use `direction="column"` for a screen.

Row:

```tsx
import { Card, Scroller, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Venues({ names }: { names: string[] }) {
  return (
    <Scroller gap="12" paddingX="16">
      {names.map((name) => (
        <Card key={name} padding="16" width={160}>
          <Text>{name}</Text>
        </Card>
      ))}
    </Scroller>
  );
}
```

Screen:

```tsx
import { Scroller, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Bookings({ reload }: { reload: () => Promise<void> }) {
  return (
    <Scroller
      direction="column"
      flex={1}
      gap="16"
      padding="16"
      safeArea={["bottom"]}
      onRefresh={reload}
    >
      <Text>Tonight</Text>
    </Scroller>
  );
}
```

# Drawer (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/drawer

> A panel that slides in from one edge of the screen, for a menu, filters or details, for React Native.

`Drawer` takes the same props as on the web (`open`, `onClose`, `side`, `size`, `title`, `description`, `footer`, `showClose`, `closeOnClickaway`, `flush`). It slides in from one edge and floats a step in from it, clear of the notch and the home indicator. Use it for an app's menu, a set of filters or a record's details; for a short task, a [`Dialog`](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/dialog) bottom sheet fits better. See the [web Drawer](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/drawer) for the same component in the browser.

## Basic usage

The drawer is always controlled: keep `open` in state and close it in `onClose`. The close button, the Android back button and a tap on the backdrop all call `onClose`.

Filters.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Button, Drawer, Switch } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Filters() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <Button label="Filters" prefixIcon="filter" variant="secondary" onPress={() => setOpen(true)} />
      <Drawer
        open={open}
        onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
        title="Filters"
        description="Show only what you need today."
        footer={<Button label="Apply" onPress={() => setOpen(false)} />}
      >
        <Switch label="Only open tables" defaultChecked />
      </Drawer>
    </>
  );
}
```

Menu.tsx:

```tsx
<Drawer open={open} onClose={close} side="left" size="s" title="Morning Coffee">
  <Nav density="compact">
    <NavItem icon="home" label="Today" selected />
    <NavItem icon="calendar" label="Bookings" />
  </Nav>
</Drawer>
```

# Nav (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/nav

> An app's navigation: a bottom tab bar, or a list of rows in a drawer or sidebar, for React Native.

`Nav`, `NavItem`, `NavSection` and `NavGroup` take the same props as on the web. As a column (the default) they are a list of rows, for a drawer or a tablet sidebar. As a row (`direction="row"`) they are the phone's bottom tab bar: the items share the width, each an icon over its label, with a line along the top and the home indicator's inset below. See the [web Nav](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/nav) for the same components in the browser.

## Bottom tab bar

Put the bar last in the screen's column, under a view with `flex={1}`. The current tab is `selected` and drawn in the brand colour. A number `badge` is a count on the icon (0 hides it, above 9 prints 9+); `indicator` is a dot.

Tabs.tsx:

```tsx
import { useState } from "react";
import { Column, Nav, NavItem, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const TABS = [
  { icon: "home", label: "Today" },
  { icon: "calendar", label: "Bookings" },
  { icon: "person", label: "Account" },
] as const;

export function Tabs() {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState(0);
  return (
    <Column flex={1} background="page">
      <Column flex={1} padding="16">
        <Text>{TABS[tab].label}</Text>
      </Column>
      <Nav direction="row">
        {TABS.map((t, i) => (
          <NavItem
            key={t.label}
            icon={t.icon}
            label={t.label}
            badge={t.label === "Bookings" ? 3 : undefined}
            selected={tab === i}
            onPress={() => setTab(i)}
          />
        ))}
      </Nav>
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Menu.tsx:

```tsx
import { Nav, NavGroup, NavItem, NavSection } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Menu() {
  return (
    <Nav density="compact" variant="subtle">
      <NavSection label="Venue">
        <NavItem icon="home" label="Today" selected />
        <NavItem icon="calendar" label="Bookings" badge={3} />
        <NavItem icon="inbox" label="Messages" indicator />
      </NavSection>
      <NavGroup icon="settings" label="Venue settings" defaultOpen>
        <NavItem label="Opening hours" />
        <NavItem label="Tables" />
      </NavGroup>
    </Nav>
  );
}
```

# Table (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/table

> Rows of data with search, sort, row taps, row actions and pages, for React Native.

`Table` takes the same props as on the web: `data` (headers and rows), `searchable`, sortable columns, `onRowClick`, row `actions`, `striped`, `compact`, `loading`, `emptyState` and `paginated`. On a phone, drop the columns that matter least with a header's `hide`, as on the web. See the [web Table](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/components/table) for the same component in the browser.

## Basic usage

Cells are text or any element. Numbers in text sort as numbers, so `"12"` comes after `"9"`.

Guests.tsx:

```tsx
import { Table, Tag } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Guests() {
  return (
    <Table
      searchable
      searchPlaceholder="Search guests"
      paginated
      defaultPageSize={5}
      actions={[{ icon: "moreHorizontal", label: "More", onClick: (row) => open(row) }]}
      data={{
        headers: [
          { content: "Guest", key: "name", sortable: true },
          { content: "Visits", key: "visits", sortable: true, width: "96px", align: "right" },
          { content: "Last visit", key: "last", hide: { s: true } },
          { content: "Tier", key: "tier", width: "88px" },
        ],
        rows: [
          ["Anna Kovács", "12", "Oct 18", <Tag size="s" tone="warning" label="Gold" />],
          ["Bence Szabó", "4", "Oct 20", <Tag size="s" label="Silver" />],
        ],
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

# Mascot (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/mascot

> An animated companion for an assistant that idles, listens, thinks, speaks and sleeps, with a mood on top.

`Mascot` is one soft, single-color shape with eyes. By default its eyes are the tiles of the Once UI mark, and they turn like the logo loader while it thinks. It takes the same props as the [web Mascot](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/modules/ai#mascot), and a `seed` gives the same character on the phone as in the browser.

Mascot:

```tsx
import { Column, Mascot, Text } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Empty() {
  return (
    <Column center gap="12" padding="32">
      <Mascot size="xl" mood="happy" />
      <Text onBackground="neutral-weak">Ask me anything about your orders.</Text>
    </Column>
  );
}
```

States:

```tsx
import { Mascot, type MascotState } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Assistant({ status }: { status: MascotState }) {
  return <Mascot size="l" state={status} mood={status === "idle" ? "happy" : "neutral"} />;
}
```

Level:

```tsx
import { Mascot } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Reply({ level }: { level: number }) {
  return <Mascot state="speaking" mouth="smile" level={level} />;
}
```

Make it yours:

```tsx
import { Mascot, mascotLook } from "@once-ui-system/native";
import { Circle } from "react-native-svg";

export function Characters({ userId }: { userId: string }) {
  const look = mascotLook(userId);
  return (
    <>
      <Mascot seed={userId} size="m" />
      <Mascot {...look} eyes="round" size="m" />
      <Mascot
        color="#b87333"
        surface="glass"
        eyes="pill"
        mouth="smile"
        cheeks
        accessory={<Circle cx={100} cy={18} r={10} fill="#ffd166" />}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Cube:

```tsx
import { Mascot } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Thinking({ busy }: { busy: boolean }) {
  return <Mascot working="cube" state={busy ? "thinking" : "idle"} sides="tints" size="xl" />;
}
```

# Reactions (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/reactions

> Animated reactions for posts, comments and chat: each reaction has its own gesture, a pick bursts and rolls the count, and an app can bring its own images.

`Reactions` is the row under a post, a comment or a message: a chip per reaction in use with how many people left it, and an add button that opens every option above it. Pressing a chip adds the viewer's reaction or takes it back. Each reaction moves in its own way (a heart beats, a thumbs-up nods, a laugh shakes, fire flickers), and a pick sends a few copies flying out of the chip. It takes the same props as the [web Reactions](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/modules/social), so the two apps can share their reaction code.

Reactions:

```tsx
import { Reactions, type ReactionOption } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const options: ReactionOption[] = [
  { value: "❤️", label: "Love" },
  { value: "👍", label: "Like" },
  { value: "😂", label: "Haha" },
  { value: "😮", label: "Wow" },
  { value: "😢", label: "Sad" },
];

export function PostReactions({ post }: { post: Post }) {
  return (
    <Reactions
      options={options}
      counts={post.reactionCounts}
      value={post.myReaction}
      onValueChange={(value, { option, selected }) => react(post.id, option.value, selected)}
    />
  );
}
```

Reaction:

```tsx
<Row gap="16">
  <Reaction value="❤️" size="xl" trigger="loop" />
  <Reaction value="🔥" size="xl" trigger="loop" />
  <Reaction value="party" label="Party" src="https://example.com/party.webp" size="xl" />
</Row>
```

# Markdown (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/components/markdown

> Render Markdown, such as a post body or release notes, with Once UI components in React Native.

`Markdown` takes a Markdown string and draws it with the same components core's [MDX components](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/modules/mdx) use on the web. Headings, body text, links, inline code, `CodeBlock`, quotes, `List`, `Table`, `Media` and `Line` all look the same as on your site. Use it for content you store as Markdown, such as posts, comments, release notes or help articles.

## Basic usage

Pass the source as the child. The parser runs on the device and has no dependencies.

PostBody.tsx:

```tsx
import { Markdown } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function PostBody({ body }: { body: string }) {
  return <Markdown>{body}</Markdown>;
}
```

Article.tsx:

```tsx
import { Markdown } from "@once-ui-system/native";
import { router } from "expo-router";
import { Linking } from "react-native";

export function Article({ body }: { body: string }) {
  return (
    <Markdown
      onLinkPress={(href) =>
        href.startsWith("/") ? router.push(href) : Linking.openURL(href)
      }
    >
      {body}
    </Markdown>
  );
}
```

# BarChart (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/data/barChart

> A bar chart for comparing values across categories, with a tap-to-show tooltip, for React Native.

`BarChart` draws a bar for each series in each row of `data`, grouped by the row's x value. It sits on a bordered card with an optional title and description, a legend and axis labels, and draws with react-native-svg. It takes the same `data` and `series` as the [web BarChart](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/data/barChart). Tap a row to see its values.

BarChart:

```tsx
import { BarChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const data = [
  { month: "Jan", coffee: 120, tea: 80 },
  { month: "Feb", coffee: 150, tea: 60 },
  { month: "Mar", coffee: 90, tea: 110 },
];

export function Sales() {
  return (
    <BarChart
      title="Cups sold"
      description="First quarter"
      data={data}
      series={[
        { key: "coffee", color: "orange" },
        { key: "tea", color: "emerald" },
      ]}
    />
  );
}
```

Labels:

```tsx
import { BarChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Visits() {
  return (
    <BarChart
      data={[
        { day: "mon", label: "Monday", visits: 32 },
        { day: "tue", label: "Tuesday", visits: 41 },
        { day: "wed", label: "Wednesday", visits: 28 },
      ]}
      series={{ key: "visits" }}
    />
  );
}
```

Bar width:

```tsx
import { BarChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Compact({ data }: { data: { month: string; orders: number }[] }) {
  return <BarChart data={data} series={{ key: "orders" }} barWidth="s" variant="flat" />;
}
```

Axis and legend:

```tsx
import { BarChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Minimal({ data }: { data: { month: string; orders: number }[] }) {
  return (
    <BarChart
      data={data}
      series={{ key: "orders" }}
      axis="x"
      grid="none"
      legend={{ position: "bottom-center" }}
    />
  );
}
```

Hover:

```tsx
import { BarChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Highlight({ data }: { data: { month: string; orders: number }[] }) {
  return <BarChart data={data} series={{ key: "orders" }} hover />;
}
```

States:

```tsx
import { BarChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Orders({ data, loading, failed }: { data: { month: string; orders: number }[]; loading: boolean; failed: boolean }) {
  return (
    <BarChart
      title="Orders"
      data={data}
      series={{ key: "orders" }}
      loading={loading}
      error={failed}
      emptyState="No orders yet"
      errorState="Could not load orders"
    />
  );
}
```

---

# LineChart (React Native)

Source: https://next.docs.once-ui.com/native/data/lineChart

> A line chart for showing trends over time, with a filled area and a tap-to-show tooltip, for React Native.

`LineChart` draws a line for each series across the rows of `data`, with the area under it filled. It sits on a bordered card with an optional title and description, a legend and axis labels, and draws with react-native-svg. It takes the same `data` and `series` as the [web LineChart](https://next.docs.once-ui.com/data/lineChart). Tap a row to see its values.

LineChart:

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

const data = [
  { date: "2026-01-01", visits: 320, orders: 120 },
  { date: "2026-02-01", visits: 410, orders: 150 },
  { date: "2026-03-01", visits: 380, orders: 140 },
  { date: "2026-04-01", visits: 520, orders: 190 },
];

export function Traffic() {
  return (
    <LineChart
      title="Traffic"
      description="Visits and orders per month"
      data={data}
      series={[
        { key: "visits", color: "blue" },
        { key: "orders", color: "aqua" },
      ]}
      date={{ format: "MMM" }}
    />
  );
}
```

Curve:

```tsx
import { Column, LineChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Curves({ data }: { data: { day: string; sales: number }[] }) {
  return (
    <Column gap="16">
      <LineChart data={data} series={{ key: "sales" }} curve="monotone" />
      <LineChart data={data} series={{ key: "sales" }} curve="stepAfter" />
    </Column>
  );
}
```

Outline:

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Outline({ data }: { data: { day: string; sales: number }[] }) {
  return <LineChart data={data} series={{ key: "sales" }} variant="outline" grid="y" />;
}
```

Dates:

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function FirstQuarter({ data }: { data: { date: string; visits: number }[] }) {
  return (
    <LineChart
      data={data}
      series={{ key: "visits" }}
      date={{ start: new Date(2026, 0, 1), end: new Date(2026, 2, 31), format: "MMM d" }}
    />
  );
}
```

Numeric x:

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Temperature() {
  return (
    <LineChart
      data={[
        { hour: 6, temp: 12 },
        { hour: 9, temp: 16 },
        { hour: 15, temp: 22 },
        { hour: 21, temp: 17 },
      ]}
      series={{ key: "temp", color: "orange" }}
      xAxisType="number"
      xDomain={[0, 24]}
    />
  );
}
```

Empty:

```tsx
import { LineChart } from "@once-ui-system/native";

export function Empty() {
  return <LineChart title="Visits" data={[]} series={{ key: "visits" }} emptyState="No visits yet" />;
}
```
